FPCGExConnectorConstraint.name: Connector Constraints
FPCGExConnectorConstraint.purpose: Attachment is exact: two connector frames mate and the child lands in precisely one place. Connector constraints are what make that interesting, taking the one placement and turning it into a set of candidates, then shaping, offsetting and thinning that set. Where a module ends up is whatever survives. This page holds what every constraint shares; each of the sixteen has its own.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint.situation: Reading how the constraint list runs, before reading what any one constraint does.

mechanism.text: Constraints run in list order, so the list reads as a pipeline top to bottom. Each one plays a role: a generator turns the placements it is handed into several, a modifier changes each of them in place, and a filter throws some away. Order is the whole of it, because a modifier above a generator changes the one placement the variants are then made from, and the same modifier below it changes every variant instead.

bEnabled.semantics: A disabled constraint is skipped without disturbing the order of the rest, which makes it the way to bisect a pipeline that is producing the wrong spread.

hints.text: Two roles beyond the three sit outside the generate, modify, discard reading. A Preset expands another asset contents inline before the pipeline runs, and a Branch forks the variant pool on a condition and rejoins it. Both are about composing pipelines rather than about placement.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_AngularRange.name: Connector : Angular Range
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_AngularRange.purpose: Rotates the child around a frame axis in evenly-spaced steps across an angular range. It is the plainest generator and the one most spreads start from: a fan of placements that all share an origin and differ only in how far round they sit.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_AngularRange.situation: Several placements around one socket, all at the same distance.

mechanism.text: The range is a centre and a half-width, so a half-width of 180 is a full circle and anything less is an arc centred where you put it. Steps are spaced evenly across whatever that range came to, and the rotation happens in place: nothing moves away from the frame origin, so this fans orientations rather than positions.

RotationAxis.tooltip: Axis around which to rotate variants, in frame-local space

CenterAngleDegrees.tooltip: Center of the angular range in degrees

HalfWidthDegrees.tooltip: Half-width of the angular range in degrees (total sweep = 2 * HalfWidth). 180 = full circle.
HalfWidthDegrees.semantics: Half-width rather than total sweep, so the arc spans twice this. 180 closes the circle, and values above it overlap the sweep back onto itself.

Steps.tooltip: Number of evenly-spaced rotation steps within the range. <= 0 inherits the parent connector's Spawn Capacity.

bRandomOffset.tooltip: Jitter each step within its cell (centered, so the sweep stays balanced)
bRandomOffset.semantics: Jitter is per cell and centred, so the sweep stays balanced and the steps stay in order. It breaks the mechanical evenness without letting two variants swap places.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ArcRepeat.name: Connector : Arc Repeat
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ArcRepeat.purpose: Places evenly-spaced variants along an arc at a radius, each rotated to follow the curve. The difference from Angular Range is that these move: they sit out on the arc rather than turning on the spot.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ArcRepeat.situation: Pieces laid around a circle, facing the way the circle runs: a colonnade, a ring of buildings.

mechanism.text: The same centre and half-width define the arc, and the radius decides how far out it sits in the frame right and up plane. Each variant is both positioned along the arc and turned to follow it, so a piece keeps the same relationship to the curve wherever on it it lands.

CenterAngleDegrees.tooltip: Center of the angular range in degrees

HalfWidthDegrees.tooltip: Half-width of the angular range in degrees (total sweep = 2 * HalfWidth). 180 = full circle.

Radius.tooltip: Radius of the arc, in the frame's right/up plane
Radius.semantics: Measured in the frame plane and multiplied by the frame scale, so scaling the working frame resizes the whole ring without touching this. A radius of 0 collapses the arc to the origin and leaves only the rotations, which is Angular Range the long way round.

Steps.tooltip: Number of evenly-spaced positions along the arc. <= 0 inherits the parent connector's Spawn Capacity.

bRandomOffset.tooltip: Jitter each step within its cell (centered, so the arc stays balanced)

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ArcSurface.name: Connector : Arc Surface
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ArcSurface.purpose: Slides the attachment point to a random spot in an arc-shaped area of the frame plane. The two radii and the angular range make it four shapes in one: a disk, a ring, a sector, or a band along part of a circle.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ArcSurface.situation: Scatter that should respect a round boundary rather than a rectangular one.

mechanism.text: The angular range cuts the sector and the two radii cut the band, and the point lands anywhere in what is left. An inner radius of 0 includes the centre and gives a disk or a pie slice; raising it hollows the middle out into a ring or a band.

CenterAngleDegrees.tooltip: Center of the angular range in degrees

HalfWidthDegrees.tooltip: Half-width of the angular range in degrees (total sweep = 2 * HalfWidth). 180 = full circle.

InnerRadius.tooltip: Inner radius of the arc area (0 = includes center)
InnerRadius.semantics: The difference between a disk and a ring, and it is what keeps scatter off the socket itself. Setting it equal to the outer radius reduces the area to a line on the circle, which places pieces at a fixed distance and a random angle.

OuterRadius.tooltip: Outer radius of the arc area

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Branch.name: Connector : Branch
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Branch.purpose: Forks the variant pool on a condition, runs a separate sub-pipeline over each side, and rejoins them. It is the constraint for a spread whose halves should be treated differently rather than uniformly.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Branch.situation: One socket where some candidates need one treatment and the rest need another.

mechanism.text: The condition partitions the variants, each side is handed to its own preset asset, and what both produce comes back into one pool. Either side may be left empty, which makes the branch a filter that only shapes the half that matched.

Condition.tooltip: Condition filter: evaluated on each variant to partition the pool

OnPass.tooltip: Sub-pipeline for variants that PASS the condition
OnPass.semantics: Both sides take a preset rather than an inline list, so a branch is composed from pipelines authored elsewhere. Leaving one empty passes that half through untouched instead of dropping it.

OnFail.tooltip: Sub-pipeline for variants that FAIL the condition

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ConicRange.name: Connector : Conic Range
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ConicRange.purpose: Spreads variants over a cone surface rather than around a circle. Where Angular Range rotates in the plane, this tilts away from the frame forward axis and spins around it, so the spread is genuinely three-dimensional.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ConicRange.situation: A spray rather than a fan: branches leaving a trunk, spokes off a hub in three dimensions.

mechanism.text: Two angles set the cone and one sets how many places sit on its rim. The aperture is a half-angle from the frame forward, so 0 is no spread at all and 90 opens the cone flat into the perpendicular plane. Variants sit at evenly-spaced azimuths around that rim.

ApertureAngleDegrees.tooltip: Half-angle of the cone aperture in degrees (0 = no spread, 90 = perpendicular plane)
ApertureAngleDegrees.semantics: At 90 the cone is a flat plane and this behaves much like Angular Range about the forward axis. The useful range is well below that, where the spread still reads as leaving the parent.

TiltAngleDegrees.tooltip: Tilt the whole cone axis away from the frame forward, around the frame's Right axis
TiltAngleDegrees.semantics: Tilts the whole cone axis rather than widening it, so the spray leans as a unit. Combined with a low aperture it aims a tight bundle off-axis, which the frame own rotation would also do; this keeps that adjustment with the constraint instead.

Steps.tooltip: Number of evenly-spaced azimuthal positions on the cone rim. <= 0 inherits the parent connector's Spawn Capacity.

bRandomOffset.tooltip: Jitter each step's azimuth within its cell (centered)

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ContextConditi.name: Connector : Context Condition
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ContextConditi.purpose: Tests a growth context property against a threshold and prunes the whole variant pool when it fails. It gates a socket on where the run has got to rather than on where a variant landed, which is how a connector stops contributing past a depth.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ContextConditi.situation: A socket that should only participate for part of a run.

mechanism.text: The property is read once for the evaluation rather than per variant, so the answer is the same for all of them and the outcome is all or nothing. That is what separates it from the other filters: they thin a pool and this one empties it.

Property.tooltip: Which property of the growth context to evaluate
Property.semantics: Depth and placed count are the two that behave differently in a branching run: depth is local to the line being grown and placed count is global, so the same threshold gates a branch in one and the whole run in the other.

Comparison.tooltip: How to compare the property value against the threshold

hints.text: It prunes every variant or none, so a Context Condition above a generator is the cheaper placement: it decides once, before the variants exist, rather than after the pipeline has built them.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_HemisphereOffs.name: Connector : Hemisphere Offset
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_HemisphereOffs.purpose: A random offset inside a dome facing along the frame forward axis. The dome shape is the point: it scatters outward from the parent without ever putting a piece behind the surface it is attached to.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_HemisphereOffs.situation: Scatter off a face that must not push pieces back through it.

mechanism.text: One radius describes the hemisphere, its flat side on the frame plane and its dome along the forward axis. Every offset lands inside it, so the spread is denser near the middle than a box of the same reach would be.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Lattice.name: Connector : Lattice
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Lattice.purpose: A two-dimensional grid of variants across the frame right and up plane. It is the generator for arrays that read as a surface rather than as a spread: wall panels, window grids, facades.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Lattice.situation: One socket that should produce a field of pieces rather than a few.

mechanism.text: Counts and spacings on the two axes give the grid its shape, and the whole thing either centres on the frame origin or grows from it. Nothing rotates: every variant keeps the base orientation, so a lattice is a translation pattern and any turning has to come from a modifier below it.

CountX.tooltip: Number of positions along the frame's Right axis

CountY.tooltip: Number of positions along the frame's Up axis

SpacingX.tooltip: Spacing between positions along the Right axis

SpacingY.tooltip: Spacing between positions along the Up axis

bCenterGrid.tooltip: Center the grid on the frame origin
bCenterGrid.semantics: Centred, the frame origin sits in the middle of the field and an even count straddles it. Off, the origin is the first cell and the field grows along the positive axes, which is what you want when the socket marks a corner rather than a middle.

hints.text: Counts multiply. A three by three lattice is nine placements from one socket, and a ten by ten is a hundred, each of which still has to clear every filter below and every placement condition the module carries.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_LookAt.name: Connector : Look At
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_LookAt.purpose: Re-orients each variant so a chosen local axis aims at, or away from, a target. The target can be a world direction, a world point, the parent module, or the frame origin, and that last one is what lets a radial spread face outward or inward as a set.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_LookAt.situation: Pieces that should point at something rather than inherit the orientation the attachment gave them.

mechanism.text: Each variant is rotated individually so its chosen axis lines up with the resolved aim, blended by a strength. A degenerate aim, where the target sits exactly on the variant, is skipped rather than producing an arbitrary rotation.

Settings.tooltip: Per-variant look-at settings. Axis/target/strength; Mode defaults to Look At.

fields.name: Mode
fields.tooltip: Whether the re-orientation applies, and toward or away from the target

fields.name: Axis
fields.tooltip: Which local axis to aim at the target

fields.name: Target
fields.tooltip: What to aim at

fields.name: WorldDirection
fields.tooltip: World-space direction to aim at (Target = World Direction)

fields.name: WorldPosition
fields.tooltip: World-space point to aim at (Target = World Position)

fields.name: Strength
fields.tooltip: Blend strength (0 = no effect, 1 = full alignment)

Settings.semantics: Frame Origin is the target that turns a pattern into a composition: every variant of a ring aims at its centre, so the set faces inward, and Look Away turns the same ring outward. The other three targets aim at something outside the pattern instead.
Settings.trap: Strength blends toward the aim rather than switching it on, so a value below 1 leaves pieces partly facing their attachment orientation. That is the setting for a soft turn, and it is also why a Look At that seems not to have worked is worth checking here before the axis.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Preset.name: Connector : Preset
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Preset.purpose: Expands a **Constraint Preset** asset inline. It is how a pipeline authored once gets reused across connectors and modules, and it is what a Branch hands its two halves to.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Preset.situation: The same constraint pipeline wanted on more than one connector.

mechanism.text: The preset contents are flattened into the list before the pipeline runs, so what executes is one flat sequence and the preset boundary is invisible to everything below it. A preset containing a preset flattens the same way.

Preset.tooltip: Constraint preset asset to expand inline

hints.text: Because it flattens before running, order still reads top to bottom across the expansion. A modifier after a preset acts on whatever the last constraint inside it left, not on the preset as a unit.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Probability.name: Connector : Probability
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Probability.purpose: Randomly rejects a fraction of the variants. It is what turns a full, regular generator output into a sparse one, so a lattice becomes scattered panels and a ring becomes an incomplete one.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Probability.situation: A pattern that should read as partly filled rather than complete.

mechanism.text: Each variant is kept or dropped independently, and the draw is hashed from the candidate rather than taken from a running stream, so the same variant makes the same decision every run and the result is reproducible.

Chance.tooltip: Probability of keeping each variant (0 = reject all, 1 = keep all)
Chance.semantics: The probability of keeping, so lower is sparser. Because the decision is per variant and independent, a chance of 0.5 over a small pool routinely keeps all or none of it: the sparseness is only reliable once there are variants enough for the average to show.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ScaleRamp.name: Connector : Scale Ramp
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ScaleRamp.purpose: Scales the placement by a value read from the growth context, mapping a source range onto a scale range. It is how branches thin as they get further from their seed, without authoring a separate module for each size.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_ScaleRamp.situation: Structure that should taper, or grow, with how far along the run it is.

mechanism.text: A context property supplies the number, the two source values bound it, and the two scale values are what those bounds map to. Values outside the source range clamp rather than continuing, so the taper flattens out instead of inverting.

Source.tooltip: Which property of the growth context drives the scale
Source.semantics: Depth counts attachments and cumulative weight sums module weights, which diverge the moment a library mixes light and heavy pieces. Placed count is the whole run rather than this branch, so it makes later branches smaller than earlier ones regardless of their own length.

MinValue.tooltip: Source range minimum -- maps to MinScale

MaxValue.tooltip: Source range maximum -- maps to MaxScale

MinScale.semantics: The defaults run from 1 down to 0.5, so the ramp shrinks with depth. Swapping the two scales makes it grow instead, and nothing stops the pair being on either side of 1.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_SnapToGrid.name: Connector : Snap to Grid
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_SnapToGrid.purpose: Quantizes the attachment point onto a grid anchored at the frame origin. It exists to be placed after a positional modifier: scatter freely first, then pull the result onto a grid so the variation survives but the alignment comes back.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_SnapToGrid.situation: Variation that should still line up, so pieces read as placed rather than as dropped.

mechanism.text: The step sizes on the two frame axes define the grid and the offset shifts its origin on the plane. A step of 0 on an axis leaves that axis unquantized, so one axis can be snapped while the other stays free.

GridStep.tooltip: Grid step size along the frame's Right and Up axes, in world units (frame scale does not apply to grid quantization). 0 = no snap on that axis.
GridStep.semantics: World units, and frame scale does not reach it.
GridStep.trap: That is deliberate and it is the trap: scaling the working frame resizes every pattern above this and leaves the grid where it was, so a spread that was aligned before the scale is no longer aligned after it.

GridOffset.tooltip: Shift the grid origin on the frame plane

hints.text: Order is the whole of this one. Above a positional modifier it snaps the base placement and the modifier then scatters off the grid again; below it, the scatter is what gets quantized.

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Spiral.name: Connector : Spiral
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Spiral.purpose: A helix: rotation around the frame plus a progressive offset along its forward axis, with each variant turned to follow the curve. It is Arc Repeat that also climbs, and a spiral staircase is the shape it was built for.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_Spiral.situation: Anything that turns while it rises: stairs, ramps, a vine on a column.

mechanism.text: Total rotation is spread across the steps, and height per revolution converts that rotation into forward travel, so the two together decide the pitch. Radius sets how far out the helix runs. A total rotation under a full turn gives a partial flight rather than a shortened one.

TotalRotationDegrees.tooltip: Total rotation in degrees across all steps

HeightPerRevolution.tooltip: Height gained per full 360-degree revolution (along frame forward)
HeightPerRevolution.semantics: Rise is derived from rotation rather than from step count, so adding steps at a fixed total rotation makes a denser flight of the same height rather than a taller one. That is what keeps a staircase the right height while its tread count changes.

Radius.tooltip: Radius of the helix, in the frame's right/up plane

Steps.tooltip: Number of placement positions along the helix. <= 0 inherits the parent connector's Spawn Capacity.

bRandomOffset.tooltip: Jitter each step within its cell (centered, so the helix stays balanced)

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_SurfaceOffset.name: Connector : Surface Offset
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_SurfaceOffset.purpose: Slides the attachment point to a random spot in a rectangle on the frame right and up plane. It is the simplest way to stop a socket placing every piece in exactly the same relative position.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_SurfaceOffset.situation: Attachment that should vary across a face rather than land on one exact point.

mechanism.text: A width and a height describe a rectangle in the frame plane, and each variant is moved to a random point inside it. Orientation is untouched, so pieces stay square to the frame and only their position scatters.

Width.tooltip: Width of the offset rectangle (along the frame's Right axis)

Height.tooltip: Height of the offset rectangle (along the frame's Up axis)

FPCGExConnectorConstraint_VolumeOffset.name: Connector : Volume Offset
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_VolumeOffset.purpose: A random offset inside a box around the frame origin, oriented in frame space. Where Surface Offset scatters across a plane, this scatters through a volume, so pieces move toward and away from the parent as well as across it.
FPCGExConnectorConstraint_VolumeOffset.situation: Scatter that should have depth: foliage, debris, anything sitting off a surface rather than on it.

mechanism.text: One half-extent per axis describes the box, in frame-local terms where forward is the axis the connector points along. Each variant is moved to a random point inside it, with orientation untouched.

Extent.tooltip: Half-extent of the offset box in each axis (frame-local: X = forward, Y = right, Z = up)
Extent.semantics: Frame-local, so the first component runs along the connector forward axis and the other two across its plane. Zeroing the forward component reduces the box to the plane and makes this Surface Offset with a rectangle centred on the origin.

FPCGExConnectorConstraintFrame.name: Working Frame
FPCGExConnectorConstraintFrame.purpose: Every constraint resolves in a frame, and this is where that frame comes from. Radii, grids, cones and offsets are all expressed in it, so moving the frame moves the whole pattern without touching a single constraint. It is the setting to reach for when a spread is the right shape in the wrong place.
FPCGExConnectorConstraintFrame.situation: A pattern that comes out correct but oriented or centred somewhere other than intended.

mechanism.text: A source frame is picked, a local transform is applied on top of it, and an optional re-orientation aims it. Its rotation tilts the constraint out of the connector plane, its translation shifts the pattern pivot, and its scale multiplies the distances every constraint below measures.

Source.tooltip: Which mated frame the working frame derives from
Source.semantics: Parent Connector is the open connector being expanded and the ordinary answer. Child Connector shares that origin flipped about the parent up axis, which matters the moment a pattern should read from the arriving piece rather than the one it leaves. Child Module moves the origin to the placed module pivot, so a pattern is measured from the middle of the piece instead of from its socket.

LocalTransform.tooltip: Local offset applied to the source frame. Rotation tilts the constraint out of the connector plane, translation shifts the pattern/pivot, scale multiplies distances.
LocalTransform.semantics: Applied in frame-local space, so its three parts do three different jobs: rotation tilts the whole constraint out of the connector plane, translation moves the pattern pivot, and scale multiplies every distance the constraints below it measure. Scaling the frame is the cheapest way to resize a whole spread at once.
LocalTransform.trap: Frame scale does not reach grid quantization. A Snap to Grid step keeps its world-unit spacing whatever the frame scale is, so scaling a frame that ends in a snap changes the pattern and not the grid it lands on.

LookAt.tooltip: Opt-in re-orientation of the whole frame toward/away from a target

fields.name: Mode
fields.tooltip: Whether the re-orientation applies, and toward or away from the target

fields.name: Axis
fields.tooltip: Which local axis to aim at the target

fields.name: Target
fields.tooltip: What to aim at

fields.name: WorldDirection
fields.tooltip: World-space direction to aim at (Target = World Direction)

fields.name: WorldPosition
fields.tooltip: World-space point to aim at (Target = World Position)

fields.name: Strength
fields.tooltip: Blend strength (0 = no effect, 1 = full alignment)

LookAt.semantics: This aims the whole frame, where the Look At constraint aims each variant separately. Reach for it when a pattern should be oriented as a unit, and for the constraint when the pieces should each face something.

FPCGExGrammarBias_Affinity.name: Bias : Affinity
FPCGExGrammarBias_Affinity.purpose: Prefers modules that get on with their parent, read from **Affinity Map** assets. Affinity is a statement about what a module is placed next to, which only means anything once there is a neighbour, so this is the bias that turns an authored relationship table into a placement preference.
FPCGExGrammarBias_Affinity.situation: A library where some pieces belong beside each other and some do not, and saying so once beats writing it into every rule.

mechanism.text: For each candidate, the affinity between the parent module and that candidate is looked up and used as the weight. Several maps compose by multiplying, so a pair two maps both speak about ends up with the product rather than with whichever was read last. A pair no map mentions weighs neutral.

AffinityMaps.tooltip: Affinity map assets to use for biasing. Multiple maps compose multiplicatively.
AffinityMaps.semantics: Composing multiplicatively means a pair attracted in one map and repelled in another lands near neutral rather than one winning. Splitting a relationship table across maps is therefore a way to layer preferences, not a way to override them.

FPCGExGrammarBias_AttributeDriven.name: Bias : Attribute Driven
FPCGExGrammarBias_AttributeDriven.purpose: Scales one tagged family of candidates along growth depth, over a band you name. It is the bias for a piece that should appear at a particular part of a run: foundations near the seed, spires at the far end, and neither at the wrong depth.
FPCGExGrammarBias_AttributeDriven.situation: One category of module belongs at a particular depth band and nowhere else.

mechanism.text: Only candidates matching the predicate are touched; everything else weighs neutral. The connector growth depth is mapped across the band from Min Depth to Max Depth, and the curve is read at that position. Depths outside the band clamp to the nearest end rather than falling off, so the bias holds its edge values instead of lapsing.

Predicate.tooltip: Predicate selecting candidates the depth-driven scaling applies to.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

Predicate.semantics: This is what separates the bias from Depth Preference, which weights every candidate by depth. Here depth only decides the weight of the family the predicate names, and the rest of the library is untouched.

WeightCurve.tooltip: Weight multiplier over the depth band: 0 = Min Depth (and below), 1 = Max Depth (and above).

fields.name: Curve
fields.tooltip: Multiplier over the normalized [0,1] domain.

MinDepth.tooltip: Growth depth mapped to the curve's t=0 end.
MinDepth.semantics: The two depths define the band the curve is stretched across, so they are what the curve means rather than a filter. Narrowing the band sharpens the transition; widening it spreads the same curve over more of the run.

MaxDepth.tooltip: Growth depth mapped to the curve's t=1 end.

FPCGExGrammarBias_ConnectorIdentifier.name: Bias : Connector Identifier
FPCGExGrammarBias_ConnectorIdentifier.purpose: Reweights by connector identifier, the per-module socket name. Identifiers are authored per module rather than shared, so this matches by name across the library and is a naming-convention lever: call the front socket the same thing on every piece, and this can prefer it everywhere at once.
FPCGExGrammarBias_ConnectorIdentifier.situation: A naming convention already exists on the sockets and should drive where growth expands.

mechanism.text: One side of the attachment is tested against the identifier set, any match counting, and the multiplier lands on the matching side. Which side is tested is a setting, because the socket grown from and the socket attached by are different names on different modules.

Side.tooltip: Which side of the attachment is tested.
Side.semantics: Growing from tests the parent socket, which is a statement about where the run expands. The other side tests the candidate own socket, which is a statement about how a piece is oriented when it lands. They rarely want the same identifier list.

Identifiers.tooltip: Identifiers to prefer. ANY match counts (OR semantics).

WeightMultiplier.tooltip: Multiplier applied to matched candidates (or unmatched if bMatchIsMultiplier=false).

bMatchIsMultiplier.tooltip: Apply the multiplier to matched identifiers. Off applies it to unmatched ones instead.

hints.text: Identifiers are per module, so a name only some modules use biases only those and leaves the rest neutral. That is the mechanism working, and it is also how a typo turns into a bias that does nothing.

FPCGExGrammarBias_ConnectorPriority.name: Bias : Connector Priority
FPCGExGrammarBias_ConnectorPriority.purpose: Reads the priority authored on the connector itself and turns it into a preference. Where the other connector biases ask about type or name, this one asks what the cage author already said about which sockets matter, which makes it the bias that needs no configuration once priorities are authored.
FPCGExGrammarBias_ConnectorPriority.situation: Connector priorities are already authored and should shape a grammar as well as a plain growth.

mechanism.text: The priority on the connector being grown from is mapped onto the curve and read as a multiplier. The weight curve maps its input onto 0 to 1 and reads a multiplier off it, so reshaping the curve is how the preference is tuned rather than a single number. A library where no cage assigns priorities produces one flat value across the pool, and the bias goes neutral rather than picking arbitrarily.

WeightCurve.tooltip: Weight multiplier over priority: 0 = lowest, 1 = highest. Default favors high priority (0.5 -> 4).

fields.name: Curve
fields.tooltip: Multiplier over the normalized [0,1] domain.

bNormalizeAcrossPool.tooltip: Map the pool's own Priority range onto the curve's [0,1] domain, so the bias auto-tunes. Off maps absolute priority over Reference Priority instead.
bNormalizeAcrossPool.semantics: On, the pool own priority spread is stretched across the curve, so the bias auto-tunes to whatever range the library happens to use. Off measures absolute priority against the reference instead, which is what keeps two regions comparable when their pools differ.

ReferencePriority.tooltip: Priority delta the curve spans its [0,1] domain over; higher priorities saturate at the curve's t=1 end.

hints.text: It goes flat rather than wrong when nothing carries a priority. A bias that appears to be doing nothing here is usually a library where priorities were never authored.

FPCGExGrammarBias_ConnectorTypePref.name: Bias : Connector Type Preference
FPCGExGrammarBias_ConnectorTypePref.purpose: Reweights candidates by the type of the connector they would grow from, so a run can be steered to expand along one kind of socket before another. Type is authored on the connector set and shared across the library, which makes this the connector preference that survives a library change.
FPCGExGrammarBias_ConnectorTypePref.situation: A structure that should follow one kind of connection first, corridors before doors, beams before panels.

mechanism.text: The connector being grown from is tested against the preferred type list, any match counting, and the multiplier lands on the matching side. Everything else weighs neutral.

PreferredTypes.tooltip: Connector types to prefer. ANY match counts (OR semantics).

WeightMultiplier.tooltip: Multiplier applied to matched candidates (or unmatched if bMatchIsMultiplier=false).

bMatchIsMultiplier.tooltip: Apply the multiplier to matched connector types. Off applies it to unmatched ones instead.
bMatchIsMultiplier.semantics: Off, the multiplier lands on the types not listed, which is the shorter way to say anything but these. Below 1 that reads as a suppression of everything else rather than a boost of the listed types, and the two produce different results once other biases are in the product.

FPCGExGrammarBias_Cooldown.name: Bias : Cooldown
FPCGExGrammarBias_Cooldown.purpose: Penalises whatever was picked recently, for a number of steps. It is Pity Counter from the other direction: rather than rewarding what has been ignored, it suppresses what the run just placed, which is the shorter route to stopping the same piece appearing twice in a row.
FPCGExGrammarBias_Cooldown.situation: A run producing visible runs of one module, where spacing them out is all that is wanted.

mechanism.text: A pick puts its module, or everything sharing a tag with it, on cooldown for a number of steps, and anything on cooldown weighs the penalty instead of its own weight. Steps are counted in placements rather than in time, so a cooldown of three means the next three placements.

Predicate.tooltip: Which candidates drive the cooldown in tag mode. Ignored in per-module mode.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

CooldownSteps.tooltip: Number of OnPlacement ticks a module is held in cooldown after being picked.

PenaltyMultiplier.tooltip: Weight for candidates still on cooldown. 0.0 = effective veto; 0.25 = soft penalty.
PenaltyMultiplier.semantics: 0 is an effective veto while the cooldown lasts, which is the setting most people reach for and the one to be careful with: a cooldown longer than the number of alternatives can empty a pool. A soft value around 0.25 spaces things out without ever making a placement impossible.

bPerModule.tooltip: True = per-module-index cooldown; false = tag-based via Predicate.
bPerModule.semantics: Per module keys the cooldown to the exact module and ignores the predicate entirely. Tag mode keys it to the predicate instead, so picking one member of a family cools the whole family, which is what you want when the repetition being avoided is a look rather than a mesh.

hints.text: This rule has no placement scope. It measures how long since something was last picked, which is a temporal distance rather than set membership, so the field is hidden rather than missing.

FPCGExGrammarBias_DepthPreference.name: Bias : Depth Preference
FPCGExGrammarBias_DepthPreference.purpose: Weights candidates by how many attachments separate the connector they would grow from its seed. It shapes where a run spends its budget without replacing the growth strategy, so a grammar can favour filling out near the seed, or reaching away from it, while the strategy keeps deciding the order.
FPCGExGrammarBias_DepthPreference.situation: A silhouette that should be compact or reaching, expressed as a preference rather than as a hard depth cap.

mechanism.text: Depth in hops is mapped onto the curve and read as a multiplier. The weight curve maps its input onto 0 to 1 and reads a multiplier off it, so reshaping the curve is how the preference is tuned rather than a single number. A connector whose depth cannot be scored weighs neutral rather than being excluded.

WeightCurve.tooltip: Weight multiplier over depth: 0 = shallowest, 1 = deepest. Default favors shallow growth (4 -> 0.5).

fields.name: Curve
fields.tooltip: Multiplier over the normalized [0,1] domain.

WeightCurve.semantics: The default runs from 4 down to 0.5, which favours shallow growth. Flipping the endpoints is the whole of turning a compact bias into a reaching one.

bNormalizeAcrossPool.tooltip: Map the pool's own depth range onto the curve's [0,1] domain, so the bias auto-tunes. Off maps absolute depth over Reference Depth instead.
bNormalizeAcrossPool.semantics: On, the shallowest connector in the current pool sits at one end of the curve and the deepest at the other, so the bias re-tunes itself as the run gets deeper and always expresses a relative preference. Off, depth is measured against a fixed reference instead, which is what you want when shallow should mean shallow in absolute terms rather than shallow for now.

ReferenceDepth.tooltip: Hops over which the curve spans its [0,1] domain; deeper connectors saturate at the curve's t=1 end.

FPCGExGrammarBias_DistancePreference.name: Bias : Distance Preference
FPCGExGrammarBias_DistancePreference.purpose: The metric sibling of **Bias : Depth Preference**. It measures world-space distance from the connector to its branch seed rather than counting hops, which matters the moment a library mixes long and short modules and a hop stops being a fixed step.
FPCGExGrammarBias_DistancePreference.situation: A library of mixed-size pieces where counting attachments no longer describes how far the run has got.

mechanism.text: Distance in world units from the connector to its branch seed placement is mapped onto the curve and read as a multiplier. The weight curve maps its input onto 0 to 1 and reads a multiplier off it, so reshaping the curve is how the preference is tuned rather than a single number. A connector with no scorable distance weighs neutral.

WeightCurve.tooltip: Weight multiplier over distance: 0 = closest to the branch seed, 1 = farthest. Default favors compact growth (4 -> 0.5).

fields.name: Curve
fields.tooltip: Multiplier over the normalized [0,1] domain.

bNormalizeAcrossPool.tooltip: Map the pool's own distance range onto the curve's [0,1] domain, so the bias auto-tunes. Off maps absolute distance over Reference Distance instead.
bNormalizeAcrossPool.semantics: On, the nearest connector in the pool sits at one end of the curve and the farthest at the other, so the preference is always relative to the run as it stands. Off maps absolute distance over the reference instead, which is the setting when a real world distance is what matters.

ReferenceDistance.tooltip: World units over which the curve spans its [0,1] domain; farther connectors saturate at the curve's t=1 end.
ReferenceDistance.semantics: World units the curve spans its whole domain over, so anything farther saturates at the far end rather than continuing to scale. Setting it well below the reach of the structure flattens the bias across most of the run.

FPCGExGrammarBias_PityCounter.name: Bias : Pity Counter
FPCGExGrammarBias_PityCounter.purpose: Boosts matching candidates the longer they go unpicked, and resets a candidate the moment it is chosen. It is the bias against a draw that keeps overlooking something: variety enforced by growing pressure rather than by a quota.
FPCGExGrammarBias_PityCounter.situation: A library where some pieces keep losing the draw and the result reads repetitive because of it.

mechanism.text: Each eligible candidate carries a count of how many times it was passed over, and its weight is the factor raised to that count, so pressure compounds rather than accumulating evenly. A pick clears that candidate count. The cap is what stops a long drought from producing a weight nothing else can compete with.

Predicate.tooltip: Predicate that defines the eligible subset of candidates.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

Factor.tooltip: Geometric factor applied per miss: weight = pow(Factor, MissCount).
Factor.semantics: Geometric, so the pressure builds much faster than it reads: at the default of 1.5 a candidate passed over five times weighs about seven and a half times its neighbours. Small changes here matter more than they look.

MaxMultiplier.tooltip: Clamp on the cumulative multiplier to avoid runaway after long droughts.
MaxMultiplier.semantics: The ceiling on the accumulated multiplier, and it is what keeps the bias a preference. Without it a long enough drought produces a weight that no authored module weight can lose to, which turns a nudge into a guarantee.

FPCGExGrammarBias_Quota.name: Bias : Quota
FPCGExGrammarBias_Quota.purpose: Nudges the run toward a target proportion of placements matching a predicate. It is the bias for a mix rather than a count: a quarter of the pieces should be windows, roughly, without any particular number being required.
FPCGExGrammarBias_Quota.situation: A ratio that should hold across a region, where being close is good enough.

mechanism.text: The share of matching placements in scope is compared against the target, and candidates on the short side are boosted while the run is behind. It never vetoes and never forces, so a quota on a predicate the library cannot satisfy leans without ever getting there.

Predicate.tooltip: Predicate selecting which placements are counted toward the quota.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

TargetRatio.tooltip: Desired ratio of tagged placements within scope. 0..1.
TargetRatio.semantics: Measured against the placements the rule Scope covers, so the same 0.25 means a quarter of the region under Current region and a quarter of the whole run under Any placed before. Changing the scope changes what the ratio is a ratio of.

hints.text: Pair it with Constraint : Count when the proportion has to hold rather than merely tend. This bias shifts the odds; the constraint is what refuses.

FPCGExGrammarBias_Spatial.name: Bias : Spatial
FPCGExGrammarBias_Spatial.purpose: The soft form of **Constraint : Spatial**. It weights candidates by whether the connector they would grow from sits on the wanted side of a spatial channel, so a run leans toward a space instead of being confined to it.
FPCGExGrammarBias_Spatial.situation: Growth that should prefer a region without being forbidden from leaving it.

mechanism.text: The frontier connector is tested against the channel and weighed by which side it landed on. It scores the connector rather than the candidate, because at bias time no module has been chosen for the slot, so every candidate sharing a frontier slot shares one verdict.

Check.tooltip: The channel and side this bias prefers.

fields.name: ChannelKey
fields.tooltip: External spatial channel to test against. A channel nothing was baked into passes, so an unconnected pin never vetoes.

fields.name: Side
fields.tooltip: Which side of the channel the subject must be on. Disabled is the off switch, and the default.

fields.name: ProbeExtent
fields.tooltip: Probe size, in world units, for the point test. Larger tolerates a connector sitting just outside the region.

Check.semantics: The same channel and side vocabulary the constraint uses, so the two can be pointed at one channel and authored together: the bias to steer toward it, the constraint to enforce the boundary.
Check.trap: A channel nothing was baked into passes every test, so an unfed channel makes every connector look like a match and the bias contributes one flat value.

MatchWeight.tooltip: Weight for connectors on the wanted side.

MissWeight.tooltip: Weight for connectors on the other side. 0 is a soft veto at full Influence.
MissWeight.semantics: 0 is a soft veto at full Influence, which makes this the closest a bias comes to the constraint. Reach for the constraint when that is what you mean: a bias that vetoes is invisible in the diagnostics that report why a pool emptied.

FPCGExGrammarBias_TagWeight.name: Bias : Tag Weight
FPCGExGrammarBias_TagWeight.purpose: The plainest bias in the set: a flat multiplier on candidates matching a tag predicate, with everything else left neutral. Reach for it first, because most preferences turn out to be this one.
FPCGExGrammarBias_TagWeight.situation: Prefer or suppress a category, by however much, with nothing conditional about it.

mechanism.text: One predicate, one multiplier. Matching candidates take the multiplier and the rest weigh 1, or the other way round when the multiplier is pointed at the unmatched side.

Predicate.tooltip: Predicate that selects matching candidates. Empty predicate = no candidates match.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

Predicate.semantics: An empty predicate matches no candidates rather than all of them, so an unconfigured Tag Weight is inert rather than uniformly boosting.
Predicate.trap: That polarity is the reverse of Constraint : Count, whose empty predicate is also inert but whose bounds still apply. Here an empty predicate makes the whole bias do nothing.

WeightMultiplier.tooltip: Multiplier applied to matched candidates (or unmatched ones if bMatchIsMultiplier=false).

bMatchIsMultiplier.tooltip: Apply the multiplier to matched candidates. Off applies it to unmatched ones instead.
bMatchIsMultiplier.semantics: Off, the multiplier lands on everything the predicate did not match, which is the shorter way to say prefer everything except this. The two are not equivalent under Contrast, because normalising a spread of two values behaves differently depending on which side is the odd one out.

FPCGExGrammarBias_TargetProximity.name: Bias : Target Proximity
FPCGExGrammarBias_TargetProximity.purpose: Steers a run toward live target connectors: nearer scores higher, and optionally facing them counts too. It is the soft counterpart to **Constraint : Reach**, which refuses everything outside a corridor where this merely prefers the way in.
FPCGExGrammarBias_TargetProximity.situation: Growth that should find its way to something rather than be confined while doing so.

mechanism.text: Targets are resolved live against the current frontier. Each connector is scored by its distance to the nearest target through the curve, optionally scaled by how much it faces that target, and the score is slot-wide rather than per candidate. Nothing matching the selector leaves the bias neutral.

Selector.tooltip: Which live frontier connectors count as targets.

fields.name: ConnectorTypes
fields.tooltip: Connector types accepted as targets. Empty = any open connector.

fields.name: ModulePredicate
fields.tooltip: Only connectors whose module (per Module Scope) passes this predicate are targets. Empty = all.

fields.name: ModuleScope
fields.tooltip: Which module the predicate tests, relative to each candidate target connector.

fields.name: bExcludeOwnBranch
fields.tooltip: Multi-seed refinement: ignore targets on the same seed branch (through bridge merges) as the connector being grown from. A single-seed run is ONE branch -- this then excludes everything.

WeightCurve.tooltip: Weight multiplier over target distance: t=0 sitting on a target, t=0.5 at Reference Distance, t→1 asymptotically far. Default favors near (3 -> 0.5); a mid-range bump makes connectors hover at a ring around the target instead of beelining.

fields.name: Curve
fields.tooltip: Multiplier over the normalized [0,1] domain.

ReferenceDistance.tooltip: Distance at which the curve is sampled at its midpoint (t = 0.5); infinity maps to t = 1.
ReferenceDistance.semantics: The distance at which the curve is read at its midpoint, with infinity mapping to the far end, so it sets the scale of the approach rather than a cut-off. The curve shape decides the behaviour: a plain falloff beelines, while a mid-range bump makes connectors hover at a ring around the target instead of closing on it.

FacingInfluence.tooltip: How much a connector must also FACE the target: 0 = distance only, 1 = a connector pointing straight away from the target scores zero.
FacingInfluence.semantics: At 0 only distance counts, so a connector pointing directly away from a target scores as well as one pointing at it from the same place. At 1 pointing away scores zero. The default sits low deliberately, because facing is a weaker signal than proximity while a run is still far off.

bScoreProjectedPlacement.tooltip: Score each candidate by where the placed module's REMAINING connectors would land (full-frame mate projection), instead of by the connector grown from. Sees which module + attachment actually extends toward the target -- the difference between approaching and drifting past. Costs one transform per candidate tuple.
bScoreProjectedPlacement.semantics: It changes the question from where this connector is to where this module remaining connectors would end up, which is the difference between approaching a target and drifting past it. It costs a full mate projection per candidate, so it earns its place on runs that visibly overshoot and not by default.

FPCGExGrammarBias_TensorAlignment.name: Bias : Tensor Alignment
FPCGExGrammarBias_TensorAlignment.purpose: Reweights candidates by how well their connector aligns with a tensor field. Parameters are scoped to the region, so different parts of one grammar can respond to the same field differently. It is how a grammar follows a flow that a plain growth strategy would follow uniformly.
FPCGExGrammarBias_TensorAlignment.situation: One field, and parts of the grammar that should obey it more than others.

mechanism.text: Each connector caches its alignment with the field when it enters the frontier, and this bias only remaps that cached value, so it never samples the field in the hot path. Alignment is read through the two endpoint weights and a falloff exponent. With no tensors connected the bias goes neutral.

bAbsolute.tooltip: Score connectors aligned with OR against the field equally, so perpendicular scores lowest.
bAbsolute.semantics: On, a connector aligned against the field scores as well as one aligned with it and perpendicular scores lowest, which suits a field describing an axis rather than a direction. Off keeps the sign, so pointing upstream is penalised.

AlignedWeight.tooltip: Weight applied at perfect alignment (dot = 1, or |dot| = 1 when absolute).

MisalignedWeight.tooltip: Weight applied at the opposite end (dot = -1 signed, or perpendicular when absolute).

Power.tooltip: Falloff exponent on alignment before blending; above 1 sharpens the preference.
Power.semantics: A falloff exponent applied before blending, so above 1 the preference concentrates near perfect alignment and everything else flattens together. It is the dial for the difference between following a field loosely and hugging it.

hints.text: The Tensors pin lives on the growth node and Tensor Guidance has to be enabled there. This bias reads what that produced; it cannot bring a field in on its own.

FPCGExGrammarBiasBase.name: Bias Settings
FPCGExGrammarBiasBase.purpose: What every grammar bias carries on top of the shared rule settings. A bias reshapes the draw and forbids nothing, so its output is a multiplier per candidate: above 1 pushes a candidate up, below 1 pushes it down, and 1 means this bias has no opinion. These two settings decide how much of that opinion survives into the final weight.
FPCGExGrammarBiasBase.situation: Tuning how hard a bias leans without rewriting what it prefers.

mechanism.text: Every active bias produces one weight per candidate, and the executor multiplies them together, each lerped toward neutral by its own Influence. Two settings shape a bias contribution before that fold: Contrast sharpens or flattens the bias own spread, and Influence decides how much of the result is blended in. A bias that cannot score its input returns neutral rather than guessing.

Influence.tooltip: How strongly this bias applies: its contribution lerps toward neutral (1.0) by this factor before folding into the product with the other active biases. 0 leaves the bias inert.
Influence.semantics: It lerps this bias contribution toward neutral before the multiply, so it is a volume dial rather than a strength multiplier: at 0 the bias is inert and at 1 it applies exactly what it computed. Reach for it when a bias is right in kind but too loud next to the others.

Contrast.tooltip: Decisiveness of THIS bias alone: its weights are normalised and raised to this power before Influence blends them in, so a preference can be sharpened without touching authored module weight or the other biases. 1 changes nothing; 0 flattens the bias to pass-or-veto.
Contrast.semantics: It acts on this bias alone, normalising its weights and raising them to this power before Influence blends them in, so a preference can be sharpened without touching authored module weight or any other bias. 1 changes nothing. Above 1 turns a mild preference into a decisive one. 0 flattens the bias to pass or veto.

hints.text: A weight of 0 at full Influence does veto a candidate, but reach for a Runtime Filter constraint when a veto is what you mean. A bias that vetoes is invisible in the diagnostics that report why a pool emptied.

FPCGExGrammarConstraint_ClaimFacts.name: Constraint : Claim Facts
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_ClaimFacts.purpose: Refuses candidates by the claim state of the parent module connectors: how many of its sockets are already spent, and which ones. It is the connector-side sibling of **Constraint : Orbital Facts**, and the way to say that a module may only be grown from while it still has somewhere else to go.
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_ClaimFacts.situation: A placement that should depend on how much of its parent is already used up.

mechanism.text: A claim fact on the parent, a selection of that parent connectors, and a comparison, exactly as the connector filter poses it. The mask it reads is live rather than baked: it updates as growth consumes connectors and is restored on backtrack, so the answer reflects the run as it stands rather than as it started.

Fact.tooltip: Operand A -- the claim fact tested on the parent module.
Fact.semantics: Both facts are read against the parent alone. There is no candidate side here, because a candidate has not been attached yet and so has consumed nothing.

Selection.tooltip: Operand B -- which of the parent module's connectors take part in the test.
Selection.semantics: Identifiers and Types are the selections that survive a library change, because both are authored vocabulary. Indices are the parent own instance numbering, so the same number means a different socket on every module.

Identifiers.tooltip: Connector identifiers, matched against the parent module's instances.

ConnectorTypes.tooltip: Connector type names -- selects every instance of these types on the parent module.

Check.tooltip: How operand A is compared against operand B.

fields.name: Mode
fields.tooltip: Whether the two operands are compared bitwise, or by how many bits they share.

fields.name: Comparison
fields.tooltip: Bitflag comparison of A against B. A is the flags, B is the mask -- "Match (all)" therefore reads "A covers every selected bit".

fields.name: CountComparison
fields.tooltip: How the shared-bit count compares against the threshold.

fields.name: ThresholdType
fields.tooltip: Whether the threshold is an absolute bit count, or a fraction of the SELECTION's size.

fields.name: DiscreteThreshold
fields.tooltip: Number of bits to compare against.

fields.name: RelativeThreshold
fields.tooltip: Fraction of the selected bits to compare against -- 1.0 with an All selection means "every one".

fields.name: Rounding
fields.tooltip: How a relative threshold lands on a whole bit count.

fields.name: CountTolerance
fields.tooltip: Comparison tolerance, in bits.

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Invert the comparison result. Host-level fallbacks are unaffected.

hints.text: This reads the live consumed mask, so it sees connectors that growth spent moments ago in the same run. That is what separates it from a claim filter downstream, which reads whatever the finished result recorded.

FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Count.name: Constraint : Count
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Count.purpose: Bounds how many placements in the active scope match a tag predicate, from below, from above, or both. It is the constraint for a quantity that has to hold: at least two stairwells, at most one entrance, exactly three of something when both bounds meet.
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Count.situation: A count that has to come out right rather than merely be likely.

mechanism.text: The two bounds are checked at different moments, which is what makes them behave so differently. The maximum vetoes a matching candidate the moment placing it would exceed the cap, so it is felt during the run. The minimum cannot be judged until the scope is done, so it is checked when the region closes and fails there. Either bound set to -1 or, for the maximum, 0 meaning veto everything, drops out of the test.

Predicate.tooltip: Predicate selecting which placements count toward the bounds.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

MinCount.tooltip: Minimum required matching placements at scope close. -1 (or 0) = no lower bound.
MinCount.semantics: Checked at scope close only, so a run that never reaches the minimum spends its whole length looking healthy and then backtracks at the end. That is the expensive failure, and it is worth pairing a minimum with a bias that pushes toward the same predicate so the run is likely to satisfy it without being forced.

MaxCount.tooltip: Maximum allowed matching placements. -1 = no upper bound. 0 = veto on any match.
MaxCount.semantics: Checked as candidates are considered, so it never wastes work. 0 is meaningful rather than off: it vetoes any match at all, which is how a predicate gets banned from a region without a second constraint.
MaxCount.trap: -1 is the off value, not 0. Setting a maximum of 0 intending to disable the bound bans the predicate outright.

hints.text: What counts as in scope comes from the Scope field on the rule itself, and its cost is paid on every evaluation. A count over Owning module is free; the same count over Any placed before walks every placement each time a candidate is weighed.

FPCGExGrammarConstraint_DependsOn.name: Constraint : Depends On
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_DependsOn.purpose: Orders two kinds of placement without ordering the graph. Anything matching the dependent predicate is refused until something matching the required predicate has been placed in scope, so a landing can be made to exist before the stairs that need one.
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_DependsOn.situation: One thing has to exist before another may be placed, and the grammar is not the natural place to say so.

mechanism.text: Two predicates and one direction. A candidate matching the dependent predicate is vetoed while nothing in scope matches the required one, and the veto lifts permanently once something does. Candidates matching neither predicate are untouched, and the constraint never forces the required thing to be placed: it only refuses the dependent one until it is.

off_label.claim: Pointing both predicates at the same tag makes a placement wait for one of its own kind, which under a scope of Owning module reads as never first in a chain.
off_label.grounded_in: the dependent veto lifts on any scope member matching the required predicate, and nothing excludes a candidate from matching both

DependentPredicate.tooltip: Candidates matching this predicate are vetoed until the dependency is satisfied.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

RequiredPredicate.tooltip: A placement matching this predicate satisfies the dependency.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

hints.text: It never causes the required placement to happen. A dependency nothing in the grammar ever satisfies vetoes its dependents for the whole run, and the symptom is a module that never appears at all.

FPCGExGrammarConstraint_ForbidPair.name: Constraint : Forbid Pair
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_ForbidPair.purpose: Mutual exclusion between two kinds of module. While one side is present in scope, a candidate on the other side is refused, and the rule works the same way whichever side got there first.
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_ForbidPair.situation: Two things that must not appear together, where either could plausibly be placed first.

mechanism.text: Symmetric by construction: the constraint tests both predicates against both the candidate and the scope, so it does not matter which was authored first or which was placed first. What decides how far the exclusion reaches is the Scope on the rule, not the constraint.

off_label.claim: Setting both predicates to the same tag, with a scope of the owning module, expresses never adjacent to itself, which is otherwise awkward to say in connector rules.
off_label.grounded_in: the symmetric test with one predicate on both sides reduces to refusing a candidate whose match is already the immediate parent

FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Once.name: Constraint : Once
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Once.purpose: Lets one specific module appear at most once in the active scope. It names a module directly where **Constraint : Unique** matches by tag, so it is the one to reach for when the thing that must be singular is a particular piece rather than a category.
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Once.situation: Exactly one of a named module, and no way to express that as a tag.

mechanism.text: One module index, checked against the placed set in scope. Once that module is present, further candidates of it are refused, and nothing else is affected.

ModuleIndex.tooltip: Compiled module index that may appear at most once in scope. -1 = unset, the constraint is inert.
ModuleIndex.semantics: A compiled module index, which means it is a position in the library rather than a name, and -1 leaves the constraint inert.
ModuleIndex.trap: The index is resolved against the library the grammar runs on. Pointing a grammar at a different bonding rules asset silently re-aims this constraint at whatever module now sits at that index, which is why a tag and Unique survive a library change and this does not.

FPCGExGrammarConstraint_OrbitalFacts.name: Constraint : Orbital Facts
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_OrbitalFacts.purpose: Refuses candidates by an orbital fact of either the parent module or the candidate itself. It is the orbital vocabulary the filters and the connector gates use, brought inside a grammar, so a placement can be gated on what a module declares about its own sides or on what is actually around it.
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_OrbitalFacts.situation: A placement that should depend on the orbital shape of what it is attaching to.

mechanism.text: A fact on a subject module, a selection of orbitals, and a comparison between the two, exactly as the orbital filter poses it. The module facts read compiled masks and always have an answer. The two substrate facts, Occupancy and Vacant, read a real orbital substrate and can only be answered when the parent is a seed carrying one; where they cannot, the fallback answers instead of guessing.

Subject.semantics: Parent asks about the module being grown from, candidate asks about the one being considered. Parent is the one that reads like a rule about context; candidate is the one that reads like a rule about eligibility.

Fact.tooltip: Operand A -- the orbital fact tested on the subject module.
Fact.semantics: The module facts describe what a module declares and are always answerable. Occupancy and Vacant describe what is actually there, which a grown structure does not carry, so they only resolve off a seed parent that came from a solved cluster.

Selection.tooltip: Operand B -- which orbitals take part in the test.

OrbitalNames.tooltip: Orbital names, resolved against the growth run's orbital set. A name matching nothing selects nothing and warns.

Check.tooltip: How operand A is compared against operand B.

fields.name: Mode
fields.tooltip: Whether the two operands are compared bitwise, or by how many bits they share.

fields.name: Comparison
fields.tooltip: Bitflag comparison of A against B. A is the flags, B is the mask -- "Match (all)" therefore reads "A covers every selected bit".

fields.name: CountComparison
fields.tooltip: How the shared-bit count compares against the threshold.

fields.name: ThresholdType
fields.tooltip: Whether the threshold is an absolute bit count, or a fraction of the SELECTION's size.

fields.name: DiscreteThreshold
fields.tooltip: Number of bits to compare against.

fields.name: RelativeThreshold
fields.tooltip: Fraction of the selected bits to compare against -- 1.0 with an All selection means "every one".

fields.name: Rounding
fields.tooltip: How a relative threshold lands on a whole bit count.

fields.name: CountTolerance
fields.tooltip: Comparison tolerance, in bits.

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Invert the comparison result. Host-level fallbacks are unaffected.

Fallback.tooltip: What an unanswerable fact yields (substrate facts off a seed parent, or a missing orbital payload). Error is treated as Fail here -- a constraint's answer is a veto, and severity handling already owns the consequences.
Fallback.semantics: What an unanswerable fact yields, which is the ordinary case for a substrate fact in a grammar. Pass lets the constraint lapse where it cannot answer; Fail turns it into a requirement that the substrate exist. Error resolves to Fail here, because a constraint answer is a veto and severity already owns the consequences.

bMatchVariants.tooltip: On: the selection rotates with the subject module's registered variant (via the payload's symmetry snapshot), so "N" means the variant's N-image. Off (strict): the authored orbitals are absolute for every variant. Folded per-instance rotations are invisible either way -- a folded module reads as its base.
bMatchVariants.semantics: On, the authored orbital selection rotates with the subject module registered variant, so naming a side means that side of however the module landed. Off, the authored orbitals are absolute for every variant, which is what you want when the rule is about world direction rather than about the module own frame.
bMatchVariants.trap: Folded per-instance rotations are invisible either way. This setting speaks only for registered variants.

FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Reach.name: Constraint : Reach
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Reach.purpose: A corridor constraint. Candidates whose frontier connector sits farther than a distance from every live target are refused, which keeps a run inside a tube around whatever it is heading for rather than letting it wander.
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Reach.situation: Growth that has somewhere to be, and should not spread away from the route while getting there.

mechanism.text: Targets are resolved live against the current frontier through the target selector, and the test is a world-space distance from the connector being grown from to the nearest of them. With no live target the constraint vetoes nothing at all, so it lapses rather than blocking when its targets are gone.

Selector.tooltip: Which live frontier connectors count as targets.

fields.name: ConnectorTypes
fields.tooltip: Connector types accepted as targets. Empty = any open connector.

fields.name: ModulePredicate
fields.tooltip: Only connectors whose module (per Module Scope) passes this predicate are targets. Empty = all.

fields.name: ModuleScope
fields.tooltip: Which module the predicate tests, relative to each candidate target connector.

fields.name: bExcludeOwnBranch
fields.tooltip: Multi-seed refinement: ignore targets on the same seed branch (through bridge merges) as the connector being grown from. A single-seed run is ONE branch -- this then excludes everything.

Selector.semantics: The same live-target machinery the target biases use, so a target is a connector on the current frontier rather than a fixed point in the world. That is what lets a corridor follow a structure being built rather than a place chosen in advance.

MaxDistance.tooltip: Corridor radius: candidates growing from a connector farther than this from every target are vetoed.
MaxDistance.semantics: World units, measured connector to target, and it bounds where growth may expand from rather than how far a module may reach. A corridor narrower than the modules produces a run that refuses everything and stops early.

hints.text: No live target means no veto. A selector that matches nothing turns this constraint off rather than refusing everything, so a corridor that stops constraining is usually a target that stopped existing.

FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Spatial.name: Constraint : Spatial
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Spatial.purpose: The keep-in and keep-out rule, scoped to whatever node or region hosts it. It refuses candidates by where they are relative to a named spatial channel, which is how a grammar is confined to a room, kept out of a volume, or held along a wall without any module carrying a placement condition of its own.
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Spatial.situation: A region of the grammar that must build inside, or outside, a space you supplied.

mechanism.text: What gets tested depends on the channel it answers on, and the two ask genuinely different questions. Runtime Filter tests the frontier connector, which is a point, and is cheap enough to run per candidate. Placement and Exit Validation test the candidate footprint, which is a volume, so they can refuse a piece that fits at its origin and sticks out once placed.

Check.tooltip: The channel and side this constraint tests.

fields.name: ChannelKey
fields.tooltip: External spatial channel to test against. A channel nothing was baked into passes, so an unconnected pin never vetoes.

fields.name: Side
fields.tooltip: Which side of the channel the subject must be on. Disabled is the off switch, and the default.

fields.name: ProbeExtent
fields.tooltip: Probe size, in world units, for the point test. Larger tolerates a connector sitting just outside the region.

Check.semantics: Names the channel and which side of it counts as passing. Channels are registered in project settings and fed on the External Domains pin of the growth node.
Check.trap: A channel nothing was baked into passes every test rather than failing it, so a mistyped channel name reads as a constraint that is quietly doing nothing.

FootprintExtentOffset.tooltip: Signed inflation of the tested footprint. Negative shrinks it, tolerating a shallow breach. Read on the Placement and Exit Validation channels.
FootprintExtentOffset.semantics: Signed inflation of the tested footprint, so a negative value shrinks it and tolerates a shallow breach of the boundary. Read on the Placement and Exit Validation channels only, because Runtime Filter tests a point and a point has no extent to inflate.

hints.text: There is a soft form of the same question. Bias : Spatial weights candidates by which side they sit on instead of refusing them, and the two are often authored together: the bias to steer, this to enforce.

FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Unique.name: Constraint : Unique
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Unique.purpose: Once anything matching the predicate is placed in the active scope, later matches are refused. It is Once expressed by tag rather than by module, so it makes a whole category singular instead of one specific piece.
FPCGExGrammarConstraint_Unique.situation: One boss room per floor, one entrance per building, one of a kind rather than one named thing.

mechanism.text: A predicate and the placed set in scope. The first match through is kept and every later one is vetoed, so which module gets to be the unique one is decided by the ordinary draw rather than by this constraint.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

hints.text: Scope is what makes this per floor rather than per run. Under Current region it resets each time the region reopens; under Any placed before it holds for the whole result.

FPCGExGrammarConstraintBase.name: Constraint Settings
FPCGExGrammarConstraintBase.purpose: What every grammar constraint carries on top of the shared rule settings: when it is consulted, and what happens when it refuses. A constraint is a hard condition, so its answer is a veto rather than a preference, and the difference between the three channels is which thing it is asked about and how much a refusal costs.
FPCGExGrammarConstraintBase.situation: Deciding when a constraint should be asked, and how hard its failure should hit.

mechanism.text: A constraint answers on every channel it is authored for, and the three ask different questions. Runtime Filter is asked per candidate during selection and can empty the pool, which is the only failure that escalates. Placement is asked per resolved pose, and a refusal there means try the next pose. Exit Validation is asked once, when the hosting region closes, about everything the region placed.

EvalChannels.tooltip: Which channels this constraint answers on.
EvalChannels.semantics: A multi-select rather than a choice, and the default is Exit Validation alone. Runtime Filter is the cheap channel and the only one whose failure can escalate at Severity. Placement is the expensive one, because a single candidate fans out to several poses and each is offered separately.
EvalChannels.trap: A constraint type only implements some of the three. Authoring a channel the type does not support is caught by the compile lint rather than silently ignored, so a constraint that refuses to compile is usually asking about a channel it cannot answer on.

Severity.tooltip: What happens on failure. Default inherits the hosting region's severity.
Severity.semantics: Read on Runtime Filter and Exit Validation only. Skip warns and carries on, the three Backtrack values undo progressively more, and Abort stops the run. A Placement refusal never reaches this at all: the walk swallows it and tries the next pose, which is why a veto that has to be able to backtrack belongs on Runtime Filter.

bOverrideRegionSeverity.tooltip: Whether to override the hosting region's DefaultSeverity.
bOverrideRegionSeverity.semantics: Off, the value above is ignored and the hosting region decides, which is what keeps a region consistent. Turn it on for the one constraint in a region that should hit harder or softer than its neighbours.

FPCGExGrammarCorridorParams.name: Corridor
FPCGExGrammarCorridorParams.purpose: The target-seeking behaviour **Seek** and **Route** share. Both grow a corridor toward a live target and try to close it with a join module, and these five settings decide which targets count, how big a loop has to be, and what happens when the join never lands.
FPCGExGrammarCorridorParams.situation: Tuning how a corridor picks its target and what an unfinished one leaves behind.

mechanism.text: A target is a live frontier connector rather than a fixed point, resolved as the run stands. The corridor grows toward the nearest eligible one and attempts a join when it comes within range. What separates Seek from Route is how they get there: Seek steers greedily, Route solves the corridor before committing it.

bExcludeOwnBranch.tooltip: Multi-seed refinement: ignore targets on this node's own seed branch (through bridge merges). Self-targeting within a branch is governed by Min Target Hops; other narrowing is authored upstream by routing a Filter node into the Target pin.
bExcludeOwnBranch.semantics: A multi-seed refinement: it keeps a corridor from targeting its own branch, following bridge merges, so seeking reaches across to another structure rather than folding back into this one.

bReachIsSuccess.tooltip: Reaching Close Distance counts as success even when no join module could span the remaining gap (join modules are the rule set's BridgeOnly modules).
bReachIsSuccess.semantics: It decides whether arriving counts, or only joining does. On, a corridor that reached its target but found no module able to span the last gap is still a success and children still dispatch. Off, the same run reads as a failure.

MinTargetHops.tooltip: Minimum loop size: a target must be MORE than this many modules away in the placement tree. Raise for bigger loops; 0 = only the same module is excluded.
