MinTargetHops.semantics: A minimum loop size, counted in modules through the placement tree rather than in world distance. It is what stops a corridor closing onto something a step away and producing a loop too small to read as one. 0 excludes only the module itself.

bKeepPartial.tooltip: Keep the corridor placed when no join was made; off rolls the whole attempt back.
bKeepPartial.semantics: What happens to the modules already placed when no join was made. On they stay, which leaves a corridor running toward something it never reached. Off rolls the whole attempt back, which is the setting when a partial corridor would read as a mistake.

ClosingDescriptor.tooltip: Modules the closing join draws from, REPLACING the rule set's Bridge Only pool. Leave untouched to use that pool. A module named here closes whether or not it carries a Bridge Only connector, the same contract a Join's descriptor has. The node's own Descriptor stays the CORRIDOR pool.

fields.name: ModuleNames
fields.tooltip: Module name whitelist (empty = any module)

fields.name: TagPredicate
fields.tooltip: Tag predicate selecting matching modules (RequireAll/RequireAny/Exclude clauses).

fields.name: ConnectorRequirements
fields.tooltip: Connector signature requirements

fields.name: bExactMatch
fields.tooltip: If true, module must have no additional connectors beyond what requirements specify

ClosingDescriptor.semantics: Replaces the rule set Bridge Only pool for the closing join rather than narrowing it. A module named here closes whether or not it was authored as Bridge Only, which is how a corridor closes with an ordinary piece.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_BeginRegion.name: Begin Region
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_BeginRegion.purpose: Opens a span of grammar that a set of rules applies to. Everything downstream is inside the region until a matching **End Region**, and the biases and constraints attached here shape every placement in between.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_BeginRegion.situation: A rule that should apply to a stretch of the grammar rather than to one node.

mechanism.text: A region is a span rather than a container: nodes are not parented to it, they are downstream of it. Regions resolve outermost first and each declares how it combines with what it inherited, separately for biases and constraints. Stateful rules attached here create fresh state each time the region opens.

RegionName.tooltip: Display name; pairing prefers RegionId and falls back to this.
RegionName.semantics: Pairing prefers a stable identity and falls back to this name, so renaming a region does not usually unpair it. The name is also what a nested region Selective Mute targets, which is the reason to set it on anything an inner region might want to switch off.

RegionColor.tooltip: Display colour for the hull overlay and pill accent. Randomly assigned from the editor's region palette on creation, user-editable through the standard colour picker. The default is that palette's first entry.
RegionColor.semantics: Editor only. It tints the hull overlay and the pill accent so nested regions stay readable at a glance, and it is assigned from the editor palette on creation rather than meaning anything at run time.

hints.text: The rules themselves live on the graph node rather than in this payload, under Rule Payload. Rule Settings covers what every one of them carries.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Branch.name: Branch
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Branch.purpose: Runs every child, in parallel, from the same parent. Where a Sequence chains its children, a Branch deals the incoming connectors out among them, so each arm builds from its own share of the frontier.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Branch.situation: Several things that should grow from one place at once.

mechanism.text: The connectors arriving on the input are dealt to the arms round-robin, so each arm gets a share rather than the whole frontier. With more arms than connectors the deal runs dry, and what a starved arm receives is the one setting here.

SurplusArmScope.tooltip: Arms are dealt the incoming connectors round-robin. This is what an arm gets once the deal runs dry -- more arms than connectors. Ignored when the Branch's own input is unscoped: every arm is unscoped then.
SurplusArmScope.semantics: It only speaks for arms the deal could not reach, so a Branch with at least as many incoming connectors as arms never consults it.
SurplusArmScope.trap: It is ignored outright when the Branch own input carries no scope. Every arm is then unscoped and sees the whole frontier, which is a different shape of result from any value here.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Bridge.name: Join
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Bridge.purpose: Connects frontier connectors across branches with a spanning module. It is the grammar way of closing a loop deliberately, where growth own bridging finds coincidences opportunistically.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Bridge.situation: Two parts of a structure that should be joined because the design says so rather than because they happened to meet.

mechanism.text: Candidate pairs are gathered from the frontier, filtered by branch and by depth, and each accepted pair gets a spanning module placed between it. Join places modules but is not part of the spawn family: a bridge consumes one connector at each end and has no notion of hosting several children, which is why the multi-spawn settings are absent here.

PairScope.tooltip: Which connectors the pair search may draw from. Ignored when the incoming edge carries no scope -- every open connector is then a candidate whatever this says.
PairScope.semantics: Which connectors the pair search may draw from.
PairScope.trap: It is ignored outright when the incoming edge carries no scope. Every open connector is then a candidate whatever this says, which is the usual reason a Join reaches somewhere unexpected.

DepthMode.semantics: A second axis on top of the branch test, filtering pairs by how far apart in the placement tree the two ends sit. It is the setting that separates a short-circuit from a long loop when both are cross-branch.

MinDepthDelta.tooltip: Minimum depth difference for pair filtering (DepthRange mode)

MaxDepthDelta.tooltip: Maximum depth difference for pair filtering (DepthRange mode)

bCrossBranchOnly.tooltip: Only bridge connectors from different branches (prevents self-loops)
bCrossBranchOnly.semantics: On by default, and it is what stops a Join closing a branch onto itself and producing a loop that adds nothing. Turning it off is for the case where a branch genuinely should close on itself.

MaxBridges.tooltip: Maximum number of bridges to place (0 = unlimited)
MaxBridges.semantics: Counted per evaluation of this node rather than for the run, so a Join inside a Repeat places up to this many on every pass.

DistanceTolerance.tooltip: Spatial tolerance for the closing join module (fraction of module connector distance).
DistanceTolerance.semantics: A fraction of the spanning module own connector-to-connector distance rather than a world distance, so it scales with the piece. A module authored with a span pair is judged against that pair instead.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Choice.name: Choice
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Choice.purpose: Picks one child at random, by weight, and runs only that one. It is how a grammar carries alternatives: three ways a room can continue, one of them taken.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Choice.situation: One of several continuations, chosen rather than combined.

mechanism.text: A weighted draw selects a single option pin and the rest are not evaluated at all. Because only one arm runs, a Choice is also the natural checkpoint for backtracking: undoing to a Choice and taking a different arm is what Branch scope backtracking does.

Weights.tooltip: Per-child weights (parallel to option pins, NOT to emitted edges -- the emit expands these per linked edge and the continuation edge takes a neutral 1.0).
Weights.semantics: Parallel to the option pins rather than to the edges the node emits, which matters because the emit expands a pin per linked edge and the continuation edge takes a neutral value. Reading the weights as per-edge is how a Choice appears to ignore them.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_EndRegion.name: End Region
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_EndRegion.purpose: Closes the nearest open region of the same name. It is optional: an unclosed region runs to the end of the grammar, which is a supported way to say from here on rather than an authoring mistake.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_EndRegion.situation: A region whose rules should stop applying partway through.

mechanism.text: Closing is what triggers a region Exit Validation constraints, so where an End Region sits decides when those are checked and what they see. Regions are matched by identity rather than by position, so an inner region can legitimately outlive an outer one.

RegionName.tooltip: Name-based pairing fallback, used when PairedBeginId is unset. GetOptions drives the picker on UPCGExGrammarEndRegionNode -- without it the field is free text and GetBeginRegionOptions() becomes dead code.
RegionName.semantics: A fallback used when the stable pairing is unset, and the editor drives it from a picker of the open regions rather than leaving it free text. Typing a name no Begin Region uses leaves this node closing nothing.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Fill.name: Fill
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Fill.purpose: Grows until the frontier is exhausted rather than until a count is reached. Where **Growth** places a range of modules, Fill places as many as it can and stops when there is nowhere left to build.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Fill.situation: A space that should be filled out rather than a run of a given length.

mechanism.text: The loop keeps placing while open connectors remain, bounded only by the safety limits. Because exhaustion is the intended end, the caps here are guards against a runaway rather than the thing that shapes the result.

MaxGrowthDepth.tooltip: Maximum growth depth from starting frontier (0 = unlimited)

MaxPlacements.tooltip: Cap on modules placed in one evaluation (0 = unlimited). Independent of Max Growth Depth -- whichever fires first stops the loop.

FillMaxModules.tooltip: Safety cap on total modules placed (prevents runaway growth)
FillMaxModules.semantics: A safety cap rather than a budget: a Fill that stops here has been cut off rather than finished, and the result is a partly filled space with a frontier still open. Reaching it regularly means the limits are shaping the result, which is what Growth is for.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Gate.name: Filter
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Gate.purpose: Narrows the frontier without placing anything. It is how a grammar says build only here: a Filter passes some of the connectors it was handed downstream and drops the rest, and everything after it sees only what survived.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Gate.situation: A section of grammar that should only work on part of what is available.

mechanism.text: Two independent narrowings run here, and they anchor at opposite ends. The tag predicate asks what is around each candidate connector, anchored at that connector own owner. The structural test asks whether the connector owner is in scope relative to the placing module. A connector has to clear both to pass.

MaxConnectors.tooltip: Maximum number of connectors to pass downstream (0 = unlimited)
MaxConnectors.semantics: A hard cap applied after both narrowings, so it thins whatever survived rather than choosing what survives. Which connectors it keeps is not a preference, so pair it with a bias upstream when the choice matters.

ModulePredicate.tooltip: Drops frontier connectors whose module (per Module Scope) fails this predicate. Empty = keep all.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

ModuleScope.tooltip: History scope the tag predicate tests across, anchored at each candidate connector's OWN owner: what is around this socket? Keep In Scope below takes the same scope from the opposite anchor, the module being built from, and asks where the socket is instead.
ModuleScope.semantics: Anchored at each candidate connector own owning module, so it answers what is around this socket. That is the opposite anchor from the structural test below, which is anchored at the placing module.

KeepInScope.tooltip: Membership scope for the structural filter.
KeepInScope.semantics: The structural half: it keeps only connectors whose owning module is inside a scope measured from the placing module. Use it to confine a section to one branch or one seed without expressing that as a tag.

hints.text: The class is named Gate in source and displays as Filter. The book uses the display name, and this Filter is a grammar node rather than a PCGEx point filter.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_GraphInput.name: Graph Input
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_GraphInput.purpose: The source-side boundary of a subgraph. It emits whatever arrives on the matching input pin of the **Subgraph** node referencing this grammar, which is how a reusable fragment receives its frontier.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_GraphInput.situation: A grammar meant to be referenced, that needs an entry point other than a Seed.

mechanism.text: The boundary name is what pairs this node with a pin on the referencing node, so naming is the whole of the wiring. During flatten the boundary is erased and the caller frontier connects straight through to whatever this fed.

BoundaryName.tooltip: Name this boundary exposes on a referencing Subgraph node's pin.
BoundaryName.semantics: It becomes the pin label a referencing Subgraph node shows, so it is user-facing rather than internal. Renaming it after a grammar is already referenced breaks the pairing at the call site.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_GraphOutput.name: Graph Output
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_GraphOutput.purpose: The sink-side boundary of a subgraph. Everything reaching it is merged and handed out through the matching output pin of the **Subgraph** node referencing this grammar.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_GraphOutput.situation: A reusable grammar fragment that has to hand its frontier back to its caller.

mechanism.text: Several internal flows may reach one Graph Output, and what leaves the boundary is their union, exactly as a Merge would produce. The boundary itself is erased at flatten, so nothing about it survives into the compiled graph.

BoundaryName.tooltip: Name this boundary exposes on a referencing Subgraph node's pin.
BoundaryName.semantics: Pairs with a pin on the referencing node by name, the same way the input boundary does. A grammar can expose several outputs, and each needs its own name for the caller to tell them apart.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Growth.name: Growth
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Growth.purpose: Runs a small growth loop inside one node, placing several modules from the frontier rather than one. It is the node for a stretch of structure whose exact extent does not matter: some corridor, a few storeys, a handful of pieces.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Growth.situation: A run of modules where the count is a range rather than a number.

mechanism.text: The loop places from the frontier until a limit stops it, and there are four that can: a depth from the starting frontier, a cap on placements in this evaluation, and the minimum and maximum count. Whichever fires first ends the loop, and whether falling short of the minimum counts as success decides if the children downstream run at all.

MaxGrowthDepth.tooltip: Maximum growth depth from starting frontier (0 = unlimited)
MaxGrowthDepth.semantics: Counted from the frontier this node started with rather than from the seed, so a Growth deep in a grammar still measures its own reach. 0 lifts it and leaves the count limits to stop the loop.

MaxPlacements.tooltip: Cap on modules placed in one evaluation (0 = unlimited). Independent of Max Growth Depth -- whichever fires first stops the loop.

GrowthMin.semantics: A floor on what counts as having worked rather than a target the loop tries to reach, so a frontier that runs dry below it does not keep trying.

bPartialCountsAsSuccess.tooltip: Treat a pass that placed fewer than Growth Min as a success anyway: children still dispatch. Off, falling short of Growth Min silently skips this node's entire child subtree.
bPartialCountsAsSuccess.semantics: Off, a pass that placed fewer than the minimum skips this node whole child subtree, and it does so without a warning.
bPartialCountsAsSuccess.trap: That silent skip is the usual reason a section of a grammar appears to have been ignored. The modules it placed are still there, which makes it read as a partial result rather than a refusal.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Merge.name: Merge
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Merge.purpose: Fan-in. It waits for every path feeding it to finish, then unions their frontiers into one. It is how several arms of a grammar come back together before a shared continuation.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Merge.situation: Work that should only start once everything before it is done.

mechanism.text: A Merge is a barrier: it does not run until every upstream path has drained, and what it emits is the union of what they all left open. That makes it the node that turns parallel arms back into a single line, and the node whose downstream section runs once rather than once per arm.

hints.text: Under Grammar Growth on Sequential execution a post-Merge section runs once per assignment rather than once in total, because each seed is a separate run. Parallel is the mode where a Merge means what it looks like it means.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Module.name: Module
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Module.purpose: Places one module matching its descriptor. It is the simplest thing a grammar does and the node most graphs are mostly made of: put a piece here.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Module.situation: One module, at one place, chosen by what it has to satisfy rather than by name.

mechanism.text: The descriptor resolves to a candidate pool, the biases in scope reweight it, the constraints veto from it, and one module is drawn from what survives. Everything the node carries comes from the shared contracts above it, which is why this page has no settings of its own.

hints.text: A Module node with an empty descriptor places anything that fits the socket. That is a working grammar producing arbitrary results rather than an error, so a descriptor is worth setting even when the library is small.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Optional.name: Optional
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Optional.purpose: Runs its body, or does not, on a probability roll. It is the lightest way to make part of a grammar occasional without expressing it as a Choice between something and nothing.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Optional.situation: A step that should happen sometimes.

mechanism.text: One roll per evaluation decides whether the body runs at all. A body that does not run is not a failure and nothing downstream is skipped because of it, which is what separates Optional from a placement that quietly fell through.

Probability.tooltip: Probability the body runs at all.
Probability.semantics: Rolled per evaluation, so an Optional inside a Repeat rolls again on every pass rather than once for the loop. That is usually what makes a repeated structure read as varied rather than uniform.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_PlacementBase.name: Module Descriptor
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_PlacementBase.purpose: What a placing node asks the library for. A descriptor names modules by connector requirement and tag rather than by name, which is what decouples a grammar from any one rules asset: the same graph runs against any library whose modules satisfy it.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_PlacementBase.situation: Deciding what a placement node is allowed to draw from.

mechanism.text: The descriptor is resolved per placement against the library the growth is running on, producing a candidate pool. Everything downstream of that, the biases that reweight the pool and the constraints that veto from it, operates on what the descriptor let through, so a descriptor that matches nothing makes every rule above it moot.

fields.name: ModuleNames
fields.tooltip: Module name whitelist (empty = any module)

fields.name: TagPredicate
fields.tooltip: Tag predicate selecting matching modules (RequireAll/RequireAny/Exclude clauses).

fields.name: ConnectorRequirements
fields.tooltip: Connector signature requirements

fields.name: bExactMatch
fields.tooltip: If true, module must have no additional connectors beyond what requirements specify

Descriptor.semantics: Matching by requirement and tag rather than by module name is the whole point: a grammar written against descriptors survives a library being rebuilt, renamed or extended. Naming exact modules is possible and gives that up.
Descriptor.trap: An empty descriptor matches the whole library rather than nothing, so an unconfigured placement node places anything that fits the socket. That reads as a working grammar producing arbitrary results.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Prune.name: Prune
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Prune.purpose: Removes placed modules that led nowhere and hands their sockets back to the frontier. It is the clean-up node: a grammar that grows speculatively can undo the parts that came to nothing rather than shipping dead ends.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Prune.situation: A run that produces stubs, corridors to nowhere, or branches that stopped one module in.

mechanism.text: Candidate placements are examined against what their subtree contains, and one whose subtree holds nothing qualifying is retracted. Cascading re-examines after each pass, which is what walks a whole dangling chain back rather than removing only its tip. Retracted modules give their connectors back, so what was pruned becomes available to build on again.

Descriptor.tooltip: Which placements are examined, out of those owning the incoming connectors. Empty = all of them. Prune is NOT a placement payload: this descriptor selects EXISTING placements to examine rather than a pool to place from, so it keeps its own field and its "Consider" label.

fields.name: ModuleNames
fields.tooltip: Module name whitelist (empty = any module)

fields.name: TagPredicate
fields.tooltip: Tag predicate selecting matching modules (RequireAll/RequireAny/Exclude clauses).

fields.name: ConnectorRequirements
fields.tooltip: Connector signature requirements

fields.name: bExactMatch
fields.tooltip: If true, module must have no additional connectors beyond what requirements specify

Descriptor.semantics: This one selects existing placements to examine rather than modules to place, which is why Prune is not part of the placement family despite carrying a descriptor. Empty examines every placement owning an incoming connector.

DeadEndDescriptor.tooltip: What a candidate's subtree must contain to count as leading somewhere. Empty = any child at all.

fields.name: ModuleNames
fields.tooltip: Module name whitelist (empty = any module)

fields.name: TagPredicate
fields.tooltip: Tag predicate selecting matching modules (RequireAll/RequireAny/Exclude clauses).

fields.name: ConnectorRequirements
fields.tooltip: Connector signature requirements

fields.name: bExactMatch
fields.tooltip: If true, module must have no additional connectors beyond what requirements specify

DeadEndDescriptor.semantics: What a subtree has to contain for its root to count as leading somewhere. Empty means any child at all, so the test is merely did anything follow. Naming something here turns it into did anything worthwhile follow, which is the more useful question.

bSubtreeSearch.tooltip: Search the whole subtree rather than direct children only.

MaxSubtreeDepth.tooltip: How deep the subtree search goes (0 = unlimited).

MaxRetractions.tooltip: Cap on retractions per evaluation (0 = unlimited).

bCascade.tooltip: Keep re-examining until nothing more qualifies -- this is what walks a dangling chain.
bCascade.semantics: On by default, and it is the setting that matters: without it only the immediate dead ends go, and the chain behind them stays. With it, retracting a tip exposes its parent as a dead end and the walk continues back.

bBondsCountAsProgress.tooltip: A live bridge bond counts as leading somewhere, even though a bond adds no child link.
bBondsCountAsProgress.semantics: A bridge bond adds no child link, so without this a module whose only outcome was closing a loop reads as a dead end and gets retracted. On by default for exactly that reason.

bSettleFirst.tooltip: Drain the pending BFS queue before evaluating. Off by default -- the drain is global.
bSettleFirst.semantics: Off by default because the drain it performs is global rather than local to this node, so turning it on makes a Prune wait for the whole pending queue rather than only for the work feeding it.

OutputScope.semantics: What the node hands downstream: only the connectors it freed, or a wider set. Freed only is what makes a Prune followed by a placement rebuild exactly what was removed.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Repeat.name: Repeat
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Repeat.purpose: Runs its body a number of times drawn between two bounds. It is the loop, and with a **Yield** inside it the frontier each pass produces becomes the input of the next.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Repeat.situation: A structure that should continue for a while rather than a fixed number of steps.

mechanism.text: The count is drawn once per evaluation, between the minimum and maximum, and the body then runs that many times. What each pass starts from depends on whether the body contains a Yield: without one the passes all start from the same frontier, and with one they chain.

RepeatMin.semantics: Equal bounds make the count exact, which is the way to express a fixed number of storeys or bays. A minimum of 0 lets the body be skipped entirely, which Optional expresses more directly for a single pass.

hints.text: The node carries one setting beyond this payload, Body Frontier Kind, on the graph node itself. It decides which open connectors each pass of the body may build from.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Route.name: Route
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Route.purpose: Solves an exact corridor to a target before committing any of it. Where **Seek** steers one placement at a time and may fail partway, Route searches virtual placements for a whole path and only builds once it has one, so it either produces a corridor that reaches or it produces nothing.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Route.situation: A connection that has to land exactly, where a corridor that stops short is worse than no corridor.

mechanism.text: A search explores candidate poses toward the target, bounded by an expansion budget and a length cap, and no path within budget is a first-class outcome rather than an error. What it finds is then committed, and a committed module that lands too far from the pose it was solved at abandons the corridor rather than shipping something the search never validated.

DistanceTolerance.tooltip: Spatial tolerance for the closing join module (fraction of module connector distance).

CloseDistance.tooltip: Bridge-close distance clamp. The search only aims at gaps the rule set's BridgeOnly modules can actually span (span pairs scaled through their Min/Max Scale, rigid pairs at their authored connector distance); this caps how far out that band reaches. 0 = the spannable bands alone decide (with no BridgeOnly modules at all, 0 = exact mates only).

MateTolerance.tooltip: Exact-mate position tolerance, world units: the corridor head must land this close to a target it can mate (compatible types both ways, polarity, facing).
MateTolerance.semantics: How close the corridor head has to land to a target it can mate with, in world units, on top of the compatibility and facing tests. It is the difference between a corridor that arrives and one that arrives correctly.

bPartialCountsAsSuccess.tooltip: Treat a route that never solved as a success anyway: children still dispatch. Off, an unsolved route silently skips this node's entire child subtree.

MaxExpansions.tooltip: Search expansion budget -- "no path within budget" is a first-class outcome, not an error.
MaxExpansions.semantics: The search budget, and running out is a normal answer rather than a failure to report. Raising it buys more thorough searching at a cost paid on every evaluation, including the ones that were going to succeed anyway.

HeuristicWeight.tooltip: 1 = optimal-length corridors (admissible A*); higher = faster, near-minimal.
HeuristicWeight.semantics: 1 searches for the shortest corridor and pays for it. Above 1 finds a near-minimal one sooner, which is usually the better trade once corridors are longer than a few modules.

PoseEpsilonPosition.tooltip: Search dedup position grid, world units: how far apart two poses must be to count as distinct while searching. Coarser explores less. 0 = auto from the module set's reach.
PoseEpsilonPosition.semantics: The grid the search treats two poses as the same on. Coarser explores less and finds a corridor sooner at the cost of missing tighter ones, and 0 derives it from the module set own reach, which is the sensible default.

PoseEpsilonRotation.tooltip: Search dedup rotation buckets, degrees. Coarser explores less.

DriftTolerancePosition.tooltip: How far a committed module may land from the pose it was solved at before the corridor is abandoned, world units. Raise it when spatial constraints deliberately move placements (jitter, look-at); the search is unaffected. 0 = auto from the module set's reach.
DriftTolerancePosition.semantics: How far a committed module may end up from the pose it was solved at before the whole corridor is abandoned.
DriftTolerancePosition.trap: Connector constraints that deliberately move placements, a jitter or a look-at, push every module off its searched pose. A Route through those needs this raised or it discards corridors that were fine.

DriftToleranceRotation.tooltip: Rotational counterpart of Drift Tolerance Position, degrees. 0 demands the exact searched rotation.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Seed.name: Seed
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Seed.purpose: The only entry point a grammar has. Execution starts at a Seed node and nowhere else, nothing is inferred from connectivity, and a grammar with no Seed node does not compile. It adopts a pre-placed seed module matching its descriptor and grows its subtree from there.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Seed.situation: Every grammar. There is no graph without one.

mechanism.text: Seed points arriving on the growth node are matched to Seed roots before growth starts, and each adopted point becomes the root of that node subtree. A grammar may carry several Seed nodes, and which one a given point runs is decided by the weights here unless a per-point override names one.

Weight.tooltip: Relative odds this seed is picked when several roots compete for one seed point.
Weight.semantics: Relative odds when several Seed roots compete for one seed point, so it only matters in a grammar with more than one entry point. A per-point Seed Root Override on the growth node pins a point to a root by name and bypasses the draw entirely.

hints.text: A seed point that adopts a module records the Seed node that placed it, which is what Valency : Load Properties reads to resolve per-node property overrides. Renaming a Seed node after a result is generated breaks that association on the next run.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Seek.name: Seek
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Seek.purpose: Grows a corridor toward a live target and joins when it comes in range. It steers greedily, one placement at a time, which makes it the cheaper corridor node and the one that copes with a target that moves as the run proceeds.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Seek.situation: A route to somewhere, where getting there matters more than the corridor being optimal.

mechanism.text: Each iteration places the module that best improves the distance to the nearest target, optionally weighing how much a connector faces it. Progress is measured per iteration, and a run of iterations that fails to improve gives up rather than wandering. Once inside the close distance a join is attempted with a spanning module.

MaxGrowthDepth.tooltip: Maximum growth depth from starting frontier (0 = unlimited)

MaxPlacements.tooltip: Cap on modules placed in one evaluation (0 = unlimited). Independent of Max Growth Depth -- whichever fires first stops the loop.

DistanceTolerance.tooltip: Spatial tolerance for the closing join module (fraction of module connector distance).

bGrowFromBothEnds.tooltip: Grow a second corridor FROM the targets toward this one at the same time, alternating heads until they meet -- far more robust than one greedy head. Children inherit both corridors.
bGrowFromBothEnds.semantics: Grows a second corridor back from the target at the same time, alternating heads until the two meet. It is far more robust than one greedy head, because each side only has to solve half the route, and children inherit both corridors.

CloseDistance.tooltip: Distance within which a join is attempted toward the nearest target.

FacingInfluence.tooltip: How much the steering also favors connectors FACING the target (0 = distance only).
FacingInfluence.semantics: At 0 the steering is distance alone, so a connector pointing away from the target competes with one pointing at it from the same place. Raising it makes the corridor commit to a direction earlier, which helps on a clear run and hurts when the route has to turn.

MinProgress.tooltip: Minimum best-distance improvement per iteration to count as progress.
MinProgress.semantics: The improvement in best distance an iteration has to make to count as progress, in world units.

NoProgressLimit.tooltip: Consecutive no-progress iterations before the seek gives up. Placing a module consumes its connector, so the next iteration often starts farther out -- leave routing slack.
NoProgressLimit.semantics: Consecutive fruitless iterations before the seek gives up. Leave slack here: placing a module consumes its connector, so the next iteration often starts farther out than the last one ended, and a limit of one or two reads as a seek that refuses to route.

bPartialCountsAsSuccess.tooltip: Treat a seek that never joined as a success anyway: children still dispatch. Off, an unjoined seek silently skips this node's entire child subtree.
bPartialCountsAsSuccess.semantics: Off, a seek that never joined skips this node whole child subtree silently, and the corridor it did place stays. That combination is the usual reason a grammar produces a route to nowhere with nothing on the end of it.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Sequence.name: Sequence
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Sequence.purpose: Runs its children in order, handing each one what the last produced. It is the plainest flow node and the backbone of most grammars: do this, then this, then this.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Sequence.situation: Steps that have to happen in a fixed order.

mechanism.text: Children are evaluated one after another, and the frontier each produces becomes the input of the next. A child that fails stops the chain at that point rather than skipping to the next, so a Sequence is as strong as its weakest step unless the steps are marked optional.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_SpawnBase.name: Multi Spawn
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_SpawnBase.purpose: Whether one connector may host more than one child. Most placement is one module per socket, and a connector authored with a spawn capacity above one can carry several: these three settings are what lets a node use that capacity.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_SpawnBase.situation: A socket authored to take several children, on a node that should fill it.

mechanism.text: Off, every connector takes one child and the capacity authored on it is ignored. On, a connector may be revisited up to its capacity or up to the cap set here, whichever is lower. Join does not derive from this at all: it places spanning modules and has no multi-spawn notion.

bSupportMultiSpawn.tooltip: Allow connectors with SpawnCapacity > 1 to host multiple child modules
bSupportMultiSpawn.semantics: The capacity itself is authored on the connector, so turning this on does not create capacity where none was authored. It only stops the node ignoring what is already there.

MultiSpawnMaxPerConnector.tooltip: Maximum placements per multi-spawn connector (0 = use connector's SpawnCapacity)
MultiSpawnMaxPerConnector.semantics: 0 defers to the connector own capacity, which is the setting that keeps authoring in one place. A non-zero value caps below that, and never above it.

bPrioritizePartialSpawns.tooltip: Boost priority of partially-consumed connectors so they expand before fresh ones
bPrioritizePartialSpawns.semantics: It changes which connector the node reaches for next, preferring one that is already partly filled over an untouched one. That tends to complete sockets rather than starting many, which reads as a denser result at the same placement count.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Subgraph.name: Subgraph
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Subgraph.purpose: Runs another grammar inline. The referenced graph is expanded into this one before anything executes, so a subgraph is a way of composing at authoring time rather than a call at run time.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Subgraph.situation: A section of grammar wanted in more than one place, or a graph grown too large to read.

mechanism.text: The reference is resolved and flattened during compile, and the compiled data carries no trace of the boundary. What survives is one flat graph, which is why a subgraph costs nothing at run time and why an unresolvable reference is a compile error rather than a missing step.

SubgraphSource.tooltip: Whether the referenced grammar is a separate asset or lives inside this one.
SubgraphSource.semantics: External references a standalone asset, so several grammars can share it. Embedded points at a sub-grammar this asset owns outright, which keeps a graph self-contained at the cost of reuse.
SubgraphSource.trap: An embedded reference that no longer resolves fails the compile with an error naming the node, and so does a subgraph that reaches back into a grammar already being flattened. A cycle is caught rather than hung.

EmbeddedSubgraphRef.tooltip: Embedded sub-asset reference, owned by this asset's EmbeddedSubgraphs.

RuleScope.tooltip: Whether the inlined body sees the parent's enclosing region rules.
RuleScope.semantics: Whether the inlined body sees the region rules enclosing the Subgraph node. Inheriting makes a subgraph behave as though its contents were pasted in place; not inheriting makes it a clean room, which is what you want for a fragment that should behave identically wherever it is used.

FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Yield.name: Yield
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Yield.purpose: A sink inside a **Repeat** body. It captures the frontier passing through it so the next iteration starts from there, which is what turns a loop that repeats in place into one that builds outward.
FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_Yield.situation: A repeated body where each pass should continue from the last.

mechanism.text: Whatever reaches a Yield is held as the next iteration input rather than passed onward, so a Yield ends the branch it sits on. A Repeat body with no Yield starts every pass from the same frontier, which repeats a structure rather than extending one.

FPCGExGrammarRuleBase.name: Rule Settings
FPCGExGrammarRuleBase.purpose: The settings every grammar rule carries, biases and constraints alike, so they are documented once here rather than on each of the twenty-three. A rule attaches either to a single node as an inline rule or to a **Begin Region**, and these five settings behave the same way in both places.
FPCGExGrammarRuleBase.situation: Reading what the fields above a rule own settings do, whichever rule you are looking at.

mechanism.text: A rule is data. What it does is decided by its own type; what this block decides is whether it participates at all, what it counts when it does, and what happens to its running state when control flow forks. Nothing here can veto or reweight anything on its own.

RuleName.tooltip: Name used by diagnostics and as a Selective Mute target. Not an identifier -- flattened copies of one rule legitimately share it.
RuleName.semantics: It exists for two jobs: naming the rule in diagnostics, and giving a nested region something to switch off through Selective Mute. That second one is why a rule any nested region might want to silence is worth naming, and why the name is not an identifier: flattened copies of one rule legitimately share it.

bEnabled.tooltip: Disabled rules are skipped at runtime as if they weren't authored.
bEnabled.semantics: A disabled rule is skipped as though it had never been authored, which makes it the way to park a rule while testing rather than deleting and re-authoring it.

BranchStatePolicy.tooltip: Whether this rule's state is shared across branch arms or forked per arm. Forked requires the state type to override Clone() -- without it, it degrades to Shared.
BranchStatePolicy.semantics: It only means anything for a rule that keeps a running tally, and it decides what happens to that tally when a Branch or Choice forks. Shared pools every arm into one count. Forked hands each arm its own copy, which is what you want when the arms should not be able to exhaust each other quota.
BranchStatePolicy.trap: Forked needs the rule state type to support being copied. Where it does not, the rule falls back to Shared and warns rather than failing, so a quota that seems to be leaking across arms is worth checking here first.

Scope.tooltip: Which placed modules count as "present" for this rule, relative to the frontier connector. Hidden on rule types that do not read the placed set.
Scope.semantics: It selects a slice of the run placement history relative to the connector being considered, and only rules that ask a question about what has already been placed show the field at all. The costs differ by orders of magnitude and they are paid per evaluation: Owning module is constant, Ancestor chain is bounded by tree depth, and the region-wide and run-wide scopes walk every placement every time a candidate is weighed.
Scope.trap: This is not the scope carried on a wire. Edge scope selects open connectors and decides where a node may build; this selects placed modules and decides what a rule counts. The editor calls both of them scope.

ActiveWhere.tooltip: Optional spatial precondition, tested at the frontier connector. While it fails this rule does not PARTICIPATE -- a constraint vetoes nothing, a bias contributes neutral. It never produces a veto or a penalty of its own; that is what separates it from a spatial rule. Read only on connector-anchored channels. Placement ignores it (the pose gate holds a strictly better anchor) and Exit Validation ignores it (no candidate, no connector).

fields.name: ChannelKey
fields.tooltip: External spatial channel to test against. A channel nothing was baked into passes, so an unconnected pin never vetoes.

fields.name: Side
fields.tooltip: Which side of the channel the subject must be on. Disabled is the off switch, and the default.

fields.name: ProbeExtent
fields.tooltip: Probe size, in world units, for the point test. Larger tolerates a connector sitting just outside the region.

ActiveWhere.semantics: A place rather than a set: it switches the rule on only where the frontier connector sits on the named side of a spatial channel, and leaves it inert everywhere else. Inert means genuinely absent, so a constraint vetoes nothing and a bias contributes neutral, and it never produces a veto or a penalty of its own.
ActiveWhere.trap: It is read on connector-anchored evaluation only. A constraint answering on Placement or Exit Validation ignores it, because neither of those has a frontier connector to test.

FPCGExValencySourceConfig.name: Filter Sources
FPCGExValencySourceConfig.purpose: The block every Valency point filter opens with, and the question all four have to answer before they can test anything: where does the **Valency Map** come from. They are ordinary PCGEx point filters, so anything taking a filter takes these, and this is the one thing that makes them their own family.
FPCGExValencySourceConfig.situation: Wiring any of the Valency filters, whatever it is testing.

mechanism.text: A filter resolves an entry to a module, which takes a map, and it reads that map either from the node evaluating it or from a pin of its own. Suffixes work the same way: inherited from the host by default, or named explicitly when there is no host to inherit from.

MapSource.tooltip: Where the Valency Map that resolves entries to modules comes from.
MapSource.semantics: Host Context works when the consuming node is a Valency node that already took a map, which covers most uses: vtx filters on a solve or a growth, seed filters, pattern gating. Pin is for everywhere else.
MapSource.trap: A filter set to Host Context on a node that consumes no map has nothing to resolve against. Reach for Pin whenever the filter is not sitting inside a Valency node.

bInheritSuffix.tooltip: Read the entry layer the host node operates on instead of naming one explicitly.
bInheritSuffix.semantics: Taking the layer name from the host rather than restating it is what keeps a filter working when the host is retargeted. Turning inheritance off exposes the name so it can be set by hand, which is the Pin-mode case and rarely anything else.

hints.text: The orbital and connector filters add their own inheritance switches for the substrate and claim layers, on the same principle. They are documented on those pages, because only those two read those layers.

UPCGExAffinityMapAsset.name: Affinity Map
UPCGExAffinityMapAsset.purpose: How strongly given modules prefer each other, expressed as predicate pairs with a weight. Above 1 is attraction and below it is repulsion. It is a statement about what a module is placed next to, which is why it is consumed by growth, by a solve, and by the grammar Affinity bias rather than by a bias node.
UPCGExAffinityMapAsset.situation: A library where some pieces belong beside each other and saying so once beats writing it into every rule.

mechanism.text: Entries pair two predicates and a weight, and are symmetric by default, so stating that two things like each other does not need saying twice. Where several entries match one module pair, the reconciliation setting decides what the pair is worth rather than the last match winning.

Entries.tooltip: Predicate-pair affinity entries. Symmetric by default.

fields.name: SourcePredicate
fields.tooltip: Predicate qualifying the parent module.

fields.name: TargetPredicate
fields.tooltip: Predicate qualifying the candidate module.

fields.name: Weight
fields.tooltip: Affinity weight. 1.0 = neutral, >1.0 = attraction, <1.0 = repulsion, 0.0 = soft veto.

fields.name: bSymmetric
fields.tooltip: When true, the reverse direction (Target→Source) uses the same weight unless explicitly overridden.

Entries.semantics: Symmetric by default and clearable per entry, which is what expresses a relation that genuinely runs one way. Because both sides are predicates rather than module names, one entry can speak about whole families at once.

Reconciliation.tooltip: How multiple matching entries are combined into a single module-pair weight.
Reconciliation.semantics: It only fires where more than one entry matches a pair, so a map whose entries never overlap behaves identically at every value. The geometric mean default keeps a strong attraction and a strong repulsion from cancelling into an accidental neutral the way an average would.

UPCGExChannelMapAsset.name: Channel Map
UPCGExChannelMapAsset.purpose: Typed values on modules, under named channels: numbers, vectors, colours or names, assigned by tag predicate. **Valency : Bias (Channel)** then matches a per-Vtx attribute against them, which is how a colour painted onto a cluster picks matching modules without a separate bias per value.
UPCGExChannelMapAsset.situation: A per-position value already exists and the modules should follow it.

mechanism.text: Each channel is independently typed and resolved, so one asset can carry a colour channel and a numeric one side by side. A channel carries its own match and miss weights, and individual entries can override them, so the weighting is authored with the values rather than on the node reading them.

Channels.tooltip: Channels, each independently typed and resolved.

fields.name: ChannelName
fields.tooltip: Display / fallback identifier the Bias (Channel) node binds to when it carries no channel id.

fields.name: Type
fields.tooltip: Value type; drives the query-attribute read type and the distance semantics.

fields.name: Reconciliation
fields.tooltip: How a module matching several entries resolves to a single value.

fields.name: DefaultWeighting
fields.tooltip: Weighting applied to every entry that does not override it.

fields.name: NoMatchBehavior
fields.tooltip: What modules matching no entry receive. Independent of the entry curves' t=1 end, which applies to modules that DO carry a value but sit far from the queried one.

fields.name: NoMatchWeight
fields.tooltip: Multiplier for modules matching no entry. 1 is neutral, above boosts, below suppresses.

fields.name: Entries
fields.tooltip: Predicate-to-value assignments. Modules matching no entry carry no value on this channel.

Channels.semantics: Typed per channel, and the consuming node reads its query attribute as whatever type the channel declares, so a colour channel needs a colour attribute rather than a name that spells one. A channel also distinguishes a value that failed to match from a module the channel says nothing about at all, which are different weights.

UPCGExConstraintPreset.name: Constraint Preset
UPCGExConstraintPreset.purpose: A reusable bundle of connector constraints. Authoring the same pipeline on twenty connectors is how a library becomes unmaintainable, and this is the way out: author it once, point the connectors at the asset.
UPCGExConstraintPreset.situation: The same constraint pipeline wanted in more than one place.

mechanism.text: The list executes in order when expanded, exactly as an inline list would, because the expansion is flattened into the host list before the pipeline runs. Nothing about a preset survives into execution as a unit, which is what keeps its behaviour identical to pasting the same constraints in place.

Constraints.tooltip: Constraints in this preset (executed in list order when expanded)
Constraints.semantics: Order matters here for the same reason it matters inline: the list is a pipeline. A preset that ends in a filter thins whatever the host list hands it, and a preset that ends in a generator hands the host list more variants than it started with.

hints.text: A preset can contain a Preset constraint, and the flattening resolves through. That makes composition possible and also makes a cycle possible, so a preset that references itself is worth avoiding rather than testing.

UPCGExCreateValencyBiasSettings.name: Valency : Bias
UPCGExCreateValencyBiasSettings.purpose: Makes some modules likelier at some positions. It boosts or suppresses whatever matches a tag predicate, by a weight that is either a constant or read per Vtx from an attribute, and applies only where its own filters pass. A bias reshapes a draw and never forbids anything, so a biased module that fits nowhere is still never placed and one nothing prefers can still turn up.
UPCGExCreateValencyBiasSettings.situation: A preference that varies across a cluster: taller pieces toward the perimeter, one family favoured on the ground floor.

mechanism.text: The node produces a factory the consumer runs per position. At each position the filters decide whether this bias participates at all, and where it does, every module matching the predicate has its draw weight multiplied by the weight and every other module is left alone. Several bias nodes on one pin compose by multiplication, so a module boosted by one and suppressed by another ends up with the product.

off_label.claim: Because the weight reads per Vtx, anything that produced a per-position number drives it: a noise field, a distance, the floor index Planar Partition writes. One bias node then varies continuously across a cluster without any of it being authored on the modules.
off_label.grounded_in: the weight is a shorthand selector read either as a constant or from a per-vtx attribute

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: Cluster-node filters deciding where this bias applies. Unconnected, it applies at every position.

outputs.label: Bias
outputs.note: The factory. Wire it to the Biases pin on Valency : Solve, a growth node, or Valency : Find Patterns.

TargetPredicate.tooltip: Modules matching this predicate are biased; all others stay neutral.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

TargetPredicate.semantics: The what, where the filter pin is the where, and the two are independent. Prefer tall modules is a weight; prefer tall modules near the perimeter is the same weight with a filter, and neither half has to know about the other. Modules the predicate does not match stay at their authored weight rather than being penalised.

Weight.tooltip: Multiplier on matched modules: 1 is neutral, above boosts, below suppresses (>= 0; negative attribute values clamp to 0). Constant, or a per-vtx attribute value used directly.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

Weight.semantics: A multiplier on the module's own weight, so 1 is neutral, above boosts and below suppresses. It never reaches zero from an attribute: negative values clamp to 0, which does forbid the module at that position, so a signed attribute driving this needs remapping before it gets here.

hints.text: Two settings come from the shared bias provider and sit above the ones here. Priority orders resolution and is cosmetic while biases combine by multiplying, since the product is the same whatever the order. Quiet When Inactive suppresses the per-cluster warning a bias raises when it resolves to nothing, which is right when one node feeds many clusters and only some carry the attribute it reads, and wrong while you are still checking the node is wired correctly.

UPCGExCreateValencyChannelBiasSettings.name: Valency : Bias (Channel)
UPCGExCreateValencyChannelBiasSettings.purpose: Biases by matching a value rather than by naming a tag. A **Channel Map** gives modules typed values under named channels, and this node reads a per-Vtx attribute and prefers the modules whose channel value matches it. That is how a colour painted onto a cluster picks matching modules, or a numeric gradient selects along a scale, without authoring a separate bias per value.
UPCGExCreateValencyChannelBiasSettings.situation: A per-position value already exists and the modules should follow it.

mechanism.text: At each position the query attribute is read as whatever type the channel declares, and every module is weighted by how its own channel value compares: matched, missed, or not covered by the channel at all, each carrying its own weight from the channel definition. The channel's weights are authored on the map, so this node is where the comparison happens rather than where the preference is decided. Filters on the node's own pin decide where any of it applies.

inputs.label: Filters
inputs.note: Cluster-node filters deciding where this bias applies. Unconnected, it applies at every position.

outputs.label: Bias
outputs.note: The factory. Wire it to the Biases pin on Valency : Solve, a growth node, or Valency : Find Patterns.

ChannelMap.tooltip: Channel Map asset holding the channel to match against.
ChannelMap.semantics: The channel definition is copied out of the asset when the factory is built and the asset itself is not kept, so a later edit to the map reaches this node on the next execution rather than during one.

Channel.tooltip: Name of the channel to read from the Channel Map. Fallback when Channel Id is unset or stale -- but an OVERRIDDEN name wins outright, since overriding it is the only way to retarget this node.
Channel.semantics: The name is the fallback and the id is what normally resolves the channel, which is what makes an asset-side rename harmless. Overriding the name from data wins outright, because overriding it is the only way to retarget this node at runtime.

ChannelId.tooltip: Stable channel id -- wins over Channel (name) so asset-side renames do not break this node, unless the name is overridden. Meant to be written by the channel picker UI, not by hand.
ChannelId.semantics: Written by the channel picker rather than by hand. Typing one in is how a node ends up resolving a channel that no longer exists while the name beside it looks correct.

QueryAttribute.tooltip: Per-vtx attribute compared against the channel's per-module values; read as the channel's declared type.
QueryAttribute.semantics: Read as the channel's declared type, so the attribute has to carry values of that type: a channel of colours needs a colour attribute, not a name that spells one. Where the attribute is absent the bias resolves to nothing on that cluster, which is what the quiet setting governs.

Strength.tooltip: Blends this node toward neutral: 1 applies the channel's authored weighting as-is, 0 drops the bias from the solve entirely. Above 1 exaggerates it past what the channel authored.
Strength.semantics: Blends the whole node toward neutral: 1 applies the channel's authored weighting as it stands, and 0 drops the bias from the solve entirely rather than applying a neutral multiplier. Above 1 exaggerates the channel past what it authored, which is the dial to reach for when a match should dominate rather than merely lead.

UPCGExGrammarGraphNodeBase.name: Grammar Node Settings
UPCGExGrammarGraphNodeBase.purpose: Every node in a grammar graph carries these, whatever it does. A grammar is a graph of instructions rather than a set of rules to satisfy, and these four settings decide what a node is called, whether the run may proceed without it, and which of the connectors reaching it are eligible in the first place.
UPCGExGrammarGraphNodeBase.situation: Reading the fields above a grammar node own settings, whichever node it is.

mechanism.text: A node receives open connectors on its input edge and passes some set of them on. Before its own behaviour runs, the connector filters narrow what it was handed, so a node only ever sees the sockets it was told to consider. What it does with those is the payload underneath, and every node type has its own.

NodeName.semantics: Read by diagnostics and by anything that reports which node placed a point, so it is worth setting on the nodes whose output you expect to inspect. Valency : Load Properties resolves per-node property overrides through the placing node, and this is the name that identifies it there.

bRequired.tooltip: Whether this node is required (failure = hard error)
bRequired.semantics: It decides what a failure costs. A required node that cannot do its job fails the run at the severity the region declares; an optional one is skipped and the walk carries on past it. Most flow nodes want the default, and a placement whose absence would make the rest meaningless wants this on.

ConnectorTypeFilter.tooltip: Connector type filter stored as TypeIds for rename safety (empty = any)
ConnectorTypeFilter.semantics: Narrows the incoming frontier by connector type before the node runs, so a node can be confined to one kind of socket without a Filter node in front of it. Type is authored on the connector set and shared across the library, so this survives a library change.

ConnectorIdentifierFilter.tooltip: Connector identifier filter applied to the FROM read (empty = off). Identifiers are per-module socket names, so this matches by NAME across all modules -- a naming-convention lever.

fields.name: Mode
fields.tooltip: How the identifier set is interpreted.

fields.name: Identifiers
fields.tooltip: Identifiers to test against (empty = filter off).

ConnectorIdentifierFilter.semantics: The same narrowing by socket name rather than type. Identifiers are per module, so a name only some modules use narrows to those and leaves the rest out, which is the point when a naming convention already exists.

Payload.tooltip: Per-type authored data -- one FPCGExGrammarNodePayload_* struct, the same one the asset stores. This IS the node's type-specific state: subclasses declare no mirrored UPROPERTYs, so CompileGraphToAsset / BuildGraphFromAsset move it in a single assignment each way. HideStructType suppresses the struct-type picker row (ShowOnlyInnerProperties is ignored by FInstancedStruct's customization -- it is honoured only for plain struct members like the payloads' own field groups); StructTypeConst locks the type, which the node owns.
Payload.semantics: The node type own settings, shown inline underneath. Which struct sits here is what makes a node a Growth rather than a Seek, and it is the thing every page in this section documents.

UPCGExGrammarGrowthFactory.name: Grammar Growth
UPCGExGrammarGrowthFactory.purpose: Replaces the growth strategy with a **Structural Grammar**: an authored graph that says what to place, in what order, and under what conditions. It sits in the same details-panel slot as **BFS Growth**, **DFS Growth** and **Random Growth**, and it takes that slot over completely, so a grammar never runs alongside a strategy. Everything else about a growth run is unchanged: the same modules, the same budgets, the same spatial conditions, the same output.
UPCGExGrammarGrowthFactory.situation: The structure has a recipe, and expressing that recipe as connector rules and a frontier ordering would be indirect at best.

mechanism.text: The grammar graph is the growth loop. Execution enters at a Seed node and follows the wires, and each placement node it reaches asks the library for a module by connector requirement and tag rather than by name, so one grammar runs against any library that satisfies its descriptors. Which seed point runs which Seed root is resolved before growth starts, and a run that cannot satisfy a placement undoes work and retries within the scope you allow it.

off_label.claim: Every placed point records the grammar node that placed it, so wiring the result into Valency : Load Properties turns a grammar into a way of tagging output by role: a corridor node and a room node write distinguishable points without a single attribute being authored on the modules.
off_label.grounded_in: the per-point PCGEx/V/Grammar attribute the grammar path writes, which Load Properties reads to resolve per-node property overrides

GrammarAsset.tooltip: The grammar asset defining the structural recipe
GrammarAsset.semantics: The graph is compiled once per execution, before any point is grown, so an authoring error surfaces as one error on the node rather than as a strange result. A grammar with no Seed node does not compile: execution starts nowhere else and nothing is inferred from connectivity.

BacktrackScope.tooltip: How far back to undo when placement fails
BacktrackScope.semantics: Local retries the failed placement with a different candidate and leaves everything already placed alone. Branch rewinds to the last Branch or Choice checkpoint and takes the other way, which is the setting that lets an alternative arm actually be tried. Global throws the whole run away and restarts it from a different random draw, so it is the one that changes the result everywhere rather than locally.

MaxBacktrackDepth.tooltip: Maximum backtracking depth (0 = no backtracking, -1 = unlimited)
MaxBacktrackDepth.semantics: 0 turns retrying off, so the first placement that cannot be satisfied ends that line. The ceiling is 32, and depth is counted in undo steps rather than in modules, so a Branch scope reaching back over a long run still spends one step.

bAllowPlaceholders.tooltip: Allow placeholder modules when descriptor resolution finds no candidates
bAllowPlaceholders.semantics: It answers the case where a placement node asks for something the library does not contain. Off, that placement fails and backtracking takes over; on, a stand-in of the configured size is placed and the run continues. Useful while a grammar is ahead of the library it will eventually run against.

PlaceholderBounds.semantics: Half-extents in world units. Placeholders occupy space like any other placement, so bounds far off the real module size make a grammar validate against a footprint layout it will never reproduce once the modules exist.

ExecutionMode.tooltip: How assignments dispatch when the grammar has several Seed roots, or the input several points.
ExecutionMode.semantics: Parallel is what makes cross-seed work possible: every assignment runs in one pass, so a Merge or a Join can reach across seeds and a post-Merge section runs once for the lot. Sequential runs each assignment on its own, which is what you want when seeds should not see each other, and it runs any post-Merge section once per assignment rather than once in total.

bShareSpatialData.tooltip: Sequential-only: share PlacedFootprints across runs so growths don't overlap and Bridges can span seeds.
bShareSpatialData.semantics: Sequential only, and on by default. It keeps the placed footprints in one pool across runs, so a later seed sees an earlier seed's structure and refuses to grow through it. Turning it off makes runs blind to each other, which is how independent structures end up interpenetrating.

bShareFrontiers.tooltip: Carry the frontier across runs, so later seeds can see earlier seeds' open connectors.
bShareFrontiers.semantics: Sequential only, and on by default. It carries open connectors forward, so a later seed can expand from what an earlier one left open. That is also the only way a bridge can span two seeds in this mode.

SeedRootOverride.tooltip: Per-point override pinning a seed to a grammar Seed root by name. Anything that doesn't match a root falls back to a deterministic random pick.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

SeedRootOverride.semantics: A per-point name pinning that seed to a grammar Seed root, for the case where the input points already know what they are. Anything that matches no root falls back to the ordinary deterministic pick, so a partial column of names is valid and only the named points are pinned.

hints.text: The pattern and bridge settings above this section still apply. A grammar replaces the frontier ordering, not the rest of the strategy contract.

UPCGExGrammarSpawnNodeBase.name: Placing Node Settings
UPCGExGrammarSpawnNodeBase.purpose: What a node that places modules carries on top of the shared node settings. Two things: the rules that apply to its own placements, and the property values those placements are stamped with.
UPCGExGrammarSpawnNodeBase.situation: Attaching a rule or a property value to one node rather than to a whole region.

mechanism.text: Both settings reach every placement the node makes and nothing else. An inline rule behaves exactly as a region rule does, with one difference in lifetime: a region creates fresh state each time it opens, while an inline rule keeps its state per node for the whole run, so a node evaluated many times accumulates across all of them.

InlineRules.tooltip: Inline rules -- applied to placements made by this node. Common authored data, not payload data: BeginRegion hosts the same field under its own name, and both reach the emit through GetMutableInlineRules.

fields.name: Biases
fields.tooltip: Selection biases hosted by this region or node.

fields.name: BiasReconciliation
fields.tooltip: How biases combine with the inherited active set when this region opens.

fields.name: BiasMuteTargets
fields.tooltip: Inherited bias rule names to mute. Only read when Bias Reconciliation is Selective Mute.

fields.name: Constraints
fields.tooltip: Hard constraints hosted by this region or node.

fields.name: ConstraintReconciliation
fields.tooltip: How constraints combine with the inherited active set when this region opens.

fields.name: ConstraintMuteTargets
fields.tooltip: Inherited constraint rule names to mute. Only read when Constraint Reconciliation is Selective Mute.

fields.name: DefaultSeverity
fields.tooltip: Severity inherited by every constraint here that doesn't override it, so one policy can be set region-wide.

fields.name: bOverrideSlotSelection
fields.tooltip: Replace the inherited slot-selection settings for this region or node. Innermost declaration wins, and an inline declaration outranks every region.

fields.name: SlotReduction
fields.tooltip: How each frontier slot's weight is reduced from the candidates it hosts.

fields.name: SlotSelection
fields.tooltip: How the slot is drawn once slots are weighted.

fields.name: SlotSharpness
fields.tooltip: Exponent on the normalised slot weights. 1 matches Proportional; higher concentrates the draw.

InlineRules.semantics: The same biases and constraints a Begin Region carries, scoped to this node alone. Reach for a region when several nodes should share one rule and its state; reach for an inline rule when the rule belongs to this step.
InlineRules.trap: Moving a stateful rule between the two changes when its counters reset, which is rarely what the move was for. A pity counter inline accumulates across every evaluation of that node; the same counter on a region starts over each time the region opens.

PropertyOverrides.tooltip: Per-node value overrides against the owning asset's Grammar Properties schema. Applied to every placement this node makes; resolved downstream by Valency : Load Properties.

fields.name: Overrides
fields.tooltip: Overrides array - parallel with schema (same size, same order)

PropertyOverrides.semantics: Per-node values against the grammar own property schema, applied to every placement this node makes. Only enabled rows take part, and Valency : Load Properties is what turns them into attributes on the points.

UPCGExProbeValencyProviderSettings.name: ✱ Probe : Orbital
UPCGExProbeValencyProviderSettings.purpose: A probe that connects points along the directions an **Orbital Set** defines, so the cluster it helps build is already shaped like the set a solve will use. It is the bridge between the PCGEx probing system and Valency: a 4-direction set produces grid-like connectivity, a hex set hex connectivity, and the same set then drives the solve without either half being retuned.
UPCGExProbeValencyProviderSettings.situation: A loose point cloud that has to become a cluster whose connections line up with a bonding direction set.

mechanism.text: Per point, every direction in the set is considered separately and each one claims at most one neighbour, so a point ends up with no more connections than the set has directions. A neighbour qualifies for a direction when it sits inside the search radius and within the set's angle threshold of that direction. A neighbour already claimed, by another direction here or by another probe on the same run, is skipped, so one neighbour never serves two directions.

off_label.claim: The connectivity it produces is orbital-shaped but carries no orbital data, so a Valency : Write Orbitals pass against the same set still has to run before a solve. What this probe buys there is that almost every edge matches on the first try.
off_label.grounded_in: the probe emits plain cluster edges and writes no orbital attributes, while the solve reads the substrate Write Orbitals or Lattice produces

outputs.label: Probe
outputs.note: The factory. Wire it to the Probes pin on Cluster : Connect Points or Cluster : Connect Vtx.

fields.name: SearchRadius
fields.tooltip: Search radius.

fields.name: SearchRadiusOffset
fields.tooltip: A convenient static offset added to the attribute value.

fields.name: OrbitalSet
fields.tooltip: The orbital set defining orbitals and matching parameters

fields.name: Favor
fields.tooltip: What matters more?

hints.text: The angle threshold lives on the orbital set, so it is shared with everything else reading that set. Widening it to make this probe connect more also widens what Write Orbitals will match later, which is usually what you want and is worth knowing before you change it.

UPCGExStructuralGrammarAsset.name: Structural Grammar
UPCGExStructuralGrammarAsset.purpose: The asset a grammar-driven growth runs. It holds a graph of instructions rather than a set of rules to satisfy, so it says what to place, in what order and under what conditions, and it is edited in its own graph editor rather than in a details panel. **Grammar Growth** is what points a growth node at one.
UPCGExStructuralGrammarAsset.situation: A structure that has a recipe, where the order things get built in is part of the design.

mechanism.text: The graph is compiled once per execution, before any point is grown, and the compile is where authoring errors surface. Execution enters at a Seed node and follows the wires: nothing is inferred from connectivity, and a grammar with no Seed node does not compile. What the asset itself carries beyond the graph is the vocabulary the graph draws on, a connector set for its dropdowns, a property schema its placement nodes can override, and any sub-grammars it owns.

FriendlyName.tooltip: Title shown by Subgraph nodes referencing this asset. Empty falls back to the asset name.
FriendlyName.semantics: Read by Subgraph nodes referencing this asset, so it is the name a caller sees rather than the name in the Content Browser. Empty falls back to the asset name, which is usually what you want until two subgraphs need telling apart at the call site.

ExposedInterfaces.tooltip: Exposed interface names for subgraph composition

EmbeddedSubgraphs.tooltip: Sub-grammars owned by this asset, referenced by Subgraph nodes set to Embedded. Removing one that is still referenced compiles a "missing embedded ref" diagnostic.
EmbeddedSubgraphs.semantics: Sub-grammars this asset owns outright, as opposed to referencing an asset that stands on its own. A Subgraph node set to Embedded picks from this list. A subgraph that reaches back into an asset already being flattened is caught as a cycle and reported the same way, so a loop is a compile error rather than a hang.
EmbeddedSubgraphs.trap: Removing one a Subgraph node still references fails the compile rather than degrading: the node reports that its Embedded Subgraph Ref failed to resolve, as an error, and the grammar does not run until it is repointed.

ConnectorSet.tooltip: Connector set defining available connector types for dropdown population
ConnectorSet.semantics: It populates the connector type dropdowns while authoring and nothing more, so it is a convenience for the editor rather than a binding on the run. The set the growth actually uses comes from the bonding rules the node was given.

GrammarProperties.tooltip: Property schema module-placing nodes can override per node (same machinery as collection properties: inline declaration + imported schema assets). Compile bakes a name-deduped prototype registry into CompiledData; per-point resolution happens in Valency : Load Properties through the node-property provider interface.

fields.name: Schemas
fields.tooltip: Schema array (locals -- always take precedence over imported entries with matching names)

fields.name: ImportedSchemas
fields.tooltip: Imported schema assets, resolved in array order after locals. Hard refs -- assets stay loaded as long as the owning collection exists. Recursion through imported assets' own ImportedSchemas is supported with cycle detection.

fields.name: ImportOverrides
fields.tooltip: Per-entry value overrides for imported entries. EditAnywhere is required so the detail panel's GetChildHandle can reach this property's children -- the registered FPCGExPropertySchemaCollectionCustomization takes over rendering entirely (CustomizeChildren controls every visible row), so this never appears as a top-level array editor in the inspector. The array is kept parallel with the imports-only schema via ReconcileImportOverrides (which delegates to FPCGExPropertyOverrides::SyncToSchema). UE per-instance UPROPERTY delta serialization handles three-layer composition: asset default -> template (collection on CDO) -> instance (collection on actor instance). Each layer overrides the previous via bEnabled toggles on individual entries. Locals do not appear here -- they are edited in-place on Schemas.

GrammarProperties.semantics: The schema every module-placing node in this graph can override per node, declared inline or imported from Property Schema assets. Its defaults are one of the two tiers **Valency : Load Properties** consults, which is how a value authored here reaches the points.

PreviewBondingRules.tooltip: Optional bonding rules for editor preview -- enables candidate count badges on Module nodes
PreviewBondingRules.semantics: Editor only. It enables candidate count badges on Module nodes, so a descriptor that matches nothing in the library you intend to use shows up while authoring instead of at run time. It binds nothing at execution.

UPCGExValencyAssetStagingSettings.name: Valency : Staging
UPCGExValencyAssetStagingSettings.purpose: The step between a resolved result and something that spawns. A solve or a growth produces points that know which module they are, and nothing that puts anything in the world; this node turns each module into a collection entry pick and emits the Collection Map a PCGEx spawner needs. Valency's job finishes at the pick, and which spawner follows is a PCGEx question.
UPCGExValencyAssetStagingSettings.situation: A finished Valency result that has to become meshes, actors or level instances.

mechanism.text: Each point's entry is resolved through the Valency Map to a module, that module's asset reference is resolved to a collection entry, and the pick is written onto the point.
