Where a module refers to a whole collection rather than one entry, that collection's own weighted picker runs and descends through nested sub-collections until it reaches a real asset, drawn from the point's own seed so the choice is stable per point. The points come back with a second attribute added, and the Collection Map travels on its own pin.

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The resolved points. Any point set carrying a Valency entry will do; a cluster is not required.

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: What the entry hashes mean. Take it from the node that produced the points.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, each now carrying a collection entry pick alongside the entry it arrived with.

outputs.label: Map
outputs.note: The Collection Map a PCGEx spawner needs to turn picks into assets.

EntrySuffix.tooltip: Suffix for the ValencyEntry attribute to read (e.g. "Main" -> "PCGEx/V/Entry/Main")
EntrySuffix.semantics: Named on both ends, here and on the node that produced the points, and they have to agree.
EntrySuffix.trap: A mismatch is not a silent no-op: the attribute is missing and the run stops with an error naming exactly which one it looked for. Default to Main at both ends unless there is a reason not to.

StagingLayer.tooltip: Collections-side staging layer the resolved picks are written to (unrelated to Entry Suffix, which is the Valency-side input). None = default layer (PCGEx/CollectionEntry); otherwise the layer name is appended (PCGEx/CollectionEntry/<layer>).
StagingLayer.semantics: This one is on the collections side and has nothing to do with Entry Suffix, which names the Valency-side input. It is what lets two staging passes write two independent picks onto the same points, for a downstream that spawns each layer separately.

bApplyLocalTransforms.tooltip: If enabled, applies the module's local transform offset to the point's transform

bStageConsumed.tooltip: Also stage points that a pattern absorbed. They remain in the cluster, but the pattern's own output already represents them, so staging both double-spawns.
bStageConsumed.semantics: A position a pattern absorbed stays in the cluster, still carrying an entry, while the pattern's own output already represents it. Off, those points are written an explicitly invalid pick and spawn nothing, which is what you want. On, both appear, occupying the same space.

fields.name: ScaleToFitMode
fields.tooltip: How scaling is applied to fit within target bounds. None = no scaling, Uniform = same scale all axes, Individual = per-axis control.

fields.name: ScaleToFit
fields.tooltip: Uniform scaling strategy. Fill = stretch to fill, Min = fit smallest axis, Max = fit largest axis, Avg = average.

fields.name: ScaleToFitX
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for X axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitY
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Y axis when using Individual mode.

fields.name: ScaleToFitZ
fields.tooltip: Scaling strategy for Z axis when using Individual mode.

ScaleToFit.semantics: The standard PCGEx fitting controls, applied so a staged point's bounds can be reconciled with the asset going into them. It does nothing until a fit mode is chosen, and on Valency output the bounds it reads are whatever the producing node left, which is the module's own staging bounds when that node applied its transform policy.

UPCGExValencyBacktrackingSolverFactory.name: Backtracking Solver
UPCGExValencyBacktrackingSolverFactory.purpose: The one strategy that takes a decision back. The other three commit a module and live with it, so a tight library eventually paints a position into a corner and leaves a hole there. This one keeps every commit on a stack, and when a position runs out of candidates it undoes recent commits and works through the alternatives it skipped. Given enough attempts it completes assignments the greedy strategies cannot.
UPCGExValencyBacktrackingSolverFactory.situation: A tight library where the other strategies leave holes you believe are avoidable.

mechanism.text: It visits the most-constrained undecided position first, the same ordering as the default, and tests a candidate before committing: a module that would leave a neighbour with nothing is discarded and the next one tried. When a position exhausts its candidates the last commit is undone, the narrowing it caused is restored, and the search resumes from the next untried module there. Every trial counts against the step budget, and running out of budget or of alternatives stops the search where it stands and hands the rest to the filler sweep. One seeded stream drives the whole search, so a given seed reproduces exactly.

off_label.claim: A run that finishes fast and leaves the same holes the entropy solver produced has exhausted its alternatives rather than its budget, which points at a library with no answer instead of a budget worth raising.
off_label.grounded_in: Solve distinguishes an exhausted decision stack from hitting MaxBacktrackSteps and warns separately for each before the filler sweep

MinimumSpawnWeightBoost.tooltip: Weight boost multiplier for modules that need more spawns to meet minimum.
MinimumSpawnWeightBoost.semantics: It multiplies a module's draw weight while that module is behind on its minimum. Candidates are tried in the order that same weighted draw produces, so a boosted module is not only likelier to be picked, it is likelier to be reached first when the search comes back to retry a position.

MaxBacktrackSteps.tooltip: Maximum placement attempts before giving up and falling back to fillers. Raise for hard instances.
MaxBacktrackSteps.semantics: Counted in placement attempts, not in positions, so a cluster of a few hundred positions can burn the default million on a library that keeps dead-ending. The count is per cluster and the search is single-threaded, which is where the cost of this strategy shows. Hitting the ceiling is not an error: the search stops where it is and the filler sweep covers the rest, so the output reads as a partly solved cluster rather than a failure.

hints.text: Confirm the problem is dead ends before reaching for this. A hole caused by a module nobody authored an adjacency for is not a dead end, and no amount of backtracking finds a piece that does not exist.

UPCGExValencyBondingClusterGrowthSetting.name: Valency : Grow Cluster
UPCGExValencyBondingClusterGrowthSetting.purpose: Grows onto a cluster whose modules are already resolved, starting from whatever connectors those modules left open. It is where the two connection models meet: solve a structure with orbitals, then extend it with connectors. Who resolved the input does not matter, only that the Vtx carry readable modules.
UPCGExValencyBondingClusterGrowthSetting.situation: A solved layout that needs things attached to it, where the attachments should follow from what is already there rather than from a fresh set of seeds.

mechanism.text: Every input Vtx is read back as a resolved module, and the ones the vtx filters pass become seeds whose free connectors enter the frontier. Growth then runs exactly as it does from points, and the placed modules are appended to the input cluster rather than forming a new one: everything that arrived comes out in place, with the new Vtx added and flagged. A seed with no free connectors left is demoted to a non-seed rather than reported.

off_label.claim: Chaining the node onto its own output with a filter on the grown flag grows only what the previous pass added, which builds a structure in generations without maintaining a separate filter per pass.
off_label.grounded_in: the grown flag is written per Vtx on the extended cluster and the emitted Valency Map carries both the input and the grown entries

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of the cluster to extend. Every Vtx is read back as a resolved module.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Also what Orbital Inference reads to work out which connectors are already spent.

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Resolves what the input entries mean. The map this node emits supersedes it.

inputs.label: Vtx Filters
inputs.note: Picks the seeds. Passing Vtx grow from their open connectors, failing Vtx are non-seeds. Nothing wired means every resolved Vtx seeds.

inputs.label: External Domains
inputs.note: Any spatial data, routed to a channel by its SpatialChannel tag. Untagged data lands on the fallback channel.

inputs.label: Tensors
inputs.note: Tensor fields steering which frontier connector expands next. Shown normally while Tensor Guidance is enabled, and under Advanced otherwise.

inputs.label: Overrides : Strategy
inputs.note: Attribute sets overriding properties on the chosen strategy by name.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The input Vtx, unmoved, plus one new Vtx per grown module.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: The input edges plus one per attachment this pass made.

outputs.label: Valency Map
outputs.note: Input entries and grown entries together. Chain this one onward; the input map resolves only the original modules.

outputs.label: Bridges
outputs.note: One point per bridge recorded during the pass, at the midpoint, carrying the two modules it joined.

OpenConnectorSource.tooltip: What counts a connector as already consumed -- growth only expands genuinely open ones.
OpenConnectorSource.semantics: Growth expands genuinely open connectors, so it has to work out which ones the input already spent, and the right answer depends on where the cluster came from. Connector Claims reads the per-Vtx mask a growth pass writes. Edge Connector Attributes reads per-edge connector data and falls back to inference when it is absent. Orbital Inference works it out from the cluster edges themselves, which is what a solve leaves behind. All Open spends nothing, so growth may attach into connectors that are already connected.
OpenConnectorSource.trap: The default reads an attribute a solve never writes, and a missing attribute is taken to mean everything is open. Solve output fed straight in on defaults therefore grows back through its own connections. Switch to Orbital Inference for anything that came from a solve.

GrowthStrategy.semantics: A class picker, not a wire, and the same set of strategies the point-seeded node offers. A grammar goes in this slot too, with the input cluster acting as context rather than as a set of grammar roots.

Budget.tooltip: Growth budget controlling expansion limits. MaxTotalModules caps NEW modules only -- pre-existing vtx re-read from the input cluster never consume it.

fields.name: MaxTotalModules
fields.tooltip: Hard cap on total placed modules

fields.name: MaxDepth
fields.tooltip: Max distance from any seed

fields.name: MaxWeightPerSeed
fields.tooltip: Cumulative module weight budget per seed (-1 = unlimited)

fields.name: bStopOnFirstFailure
fields.tooltip: Stop a branch if no placement found for a socket

fields.name: MaxCandidatesPerConnector
fields.tooltip: Maximum candidate transforms to attempt per connector (constraint budget)

Budget.semantics: Max Total Modules caps what this pass adds and never counts the input, so a budget of fifty means fifty new pieces whatever arrived. Max Depth is measured from each seed, so a Vtx deep inside the input structure still starts at depth zero for this pass.

AffinityMaps.tooltip: Affinity maps that bias module selection based on tag relationships between parent and candidate.
AffinityMaps.semantics: Read between the parent module and the candidate, so what the input structure is made of steers what attaches to it.

bExistingModulesCountTowardSpawnLimits.display: Existing Modules Count Toward Spawn Limits
bExistingModulesCountTowardSpawnLimits.tooltip: Every input vtx resolved against the consumed rule set (seed or not) records into per-module/group spawn limits, so growth can't re-place a capped module the existing structure already contains.
bExistingModulesCountTowardSpawnLimits.semantics: This runs the opposite way to the budget: every input Vtx resolved against the ruleset records against its module's limits, seed or not, so a module already used ten times in the input has ten fewer uses left. Extending a result repeatedly means each pass inherits the tally of every pass before it, which is worth being deliberate about.

BoundsInflation.tooltip: Global bounds padding in world units (cm). Positive = gap between modules.
BoundsInflation.semantics: World units, applied globally, so a positive value opens a gap between neighbours. It changes what overlap conditions see, which makes it the quickest lever when a pass stops far short of its budget because every candidate collides with the structure it is growing off.

TensorGuidance.tooltip: Tensor-field guidance. Active when tensors are connected to the optional "Tensors" pin -- see Bonding (Gen) for semantics.

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Master toggle. Guidance only activates when this is enabled AND tensors are connected.

fields.name: Influence
fields.tooltip: How strongly alignment reweights frontier selection; 0 leaves it alone (the gate still applies). Shapes the Random strategy only -- BFS/DFS consume alignment by rank.

fields.name: bAbsolute
fields.tooltip: Score connectors aligned with OR against the field equally, so perpendicular scores lowest. Reorders alignment rank, so it affects every strategy.

fields.name: Power
fields.tooltip: Falloff exponent on alignment before weighting; above 1 sharpens the preference. Shapes the Random strategy only -- BFS/DFS consume alignment by rank.

fields.name: bPruneAgainstField
fields.tooltip: Hard gate: connectors below Prune Threshold never enter the frontier, so growth cannot expand against the field. Connectors with no effector in range are never pruned.

fields.name: PruneThreshold
fields.tooltip: Alignment below which connectors are pruned. -1 prunes nothing, 0 prunes anything opposing.

fields.name: TensorHandlerDetails
fields.tooltip: Tensor sampling, applied to the flattened sample on top of each tensor's own mutations.

TensorGuidance.semantics: It has to be enabled here before the Tensors pin moves out of Advanced, and connecting a tensor without enabling this changes nothing.

bNonSeedsAsObstacles.tooltip: Register non-seed resolved modules' footprints as placement obstacles, so growth avoids overlapping the existing structure.
bNonSeedsAsObstacles.semantics: Registers the footprints of everything the filters rejected, so growth will not place through the parts of the structure it was not asked to extend. Turning it off is what lets new growth pass through the existing structure, which is occasionally the point and usually a mistake.

bNonSeedsInPool.tooltip: Add non-seed modules to the growth history, so grammar sees them and growth can bridge back into the existing structure. They are never frontier-expanded nor made grammar roots.
bNonSeedsInPool.semantics: Puts the rejected modules into the growth history without making them expandable, so a bridge can reach back into the existing structure and a grammar can see what is already there. They never sprout anything themselves either way.

fields.name: bApplyLocalTransforms
fields.tooltip: If enabled, applies module's local transform offset to output points

fields.name: ModuleNameAttributeName
fields.tooltip: Attribute name for the resolved module name

fields.name: DepthAttributeName
fields.tooltip: Attribute name for growth depth

fields.name: SeedIndexAttributeName
fields.tooltip: Attribute name for seed index

fields.name: bOutputBridges
fields.tooltip: Emit a separate point set of bridge midpoints, carrying their start and end modules.

fields.name: bOutputConnectorData
fields.tooltip: Write raw connector indices to edges (for connector-level pattern matching)

fields.name: bOutputConnectorClaims
fields.tooltip: Write a per-vertex mask marking connectors consumed by a parent-child connection, so downstream nodes can skip the ones already wired.

GrownFlagAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the grown-vtx flag
GrownFlagAttributeName.semantics: Everything from the input reads false and everything this pass added reads true, which is what lets the two halves be partitioned, spawned differently, or fed back in as the seeds of a further pass.

ExternalDomains.tooltip: External spatial constraints baked from the "External Domains" pin -- see Bonding (Gen).

fields.name: TagPrefix
fields.tooltip: Tag prefix that identifies the channel key on a tagged data. "SpatialChannel:Bounds" -> channel "Bounds". Inputs without any matching tag fall back to FallbackChannel.

fields.name: FallbackChannel
fields.tooltip: Channel used when a tagged data has no <TagPrefix>:* tag. The data is still baked -- it just lands on this channel. Default = "Default".

fields.name: SplineFidelity
fields.tooltip: Spline-sampling fidelity (squared-distance threshold) forwarded to FPCGSplineStruct::ConvertSplineToPolyLine. Smaller = denser outline.

fields.name: Projection
fields.tooltip: Projection frame for spline -> Polygon bakes. Normal mode reads the spline data's own projection (with FBestFitPlane fallback); BestFit computes the plane from sampled points. Mirrors FPolyPath's behavior.

fields.name: ZMin
fields.tooltip: Z band lower extent for spline -> Polygon bakes. Constant or @Data attribute.

fields.name: ZMax
fields.tooltip: Z band upper extent for spline -> Polygon bakes. Constant or @Data attribute.

ExternalDomains.semantics: Baking settings for whatever arrives on the External Domains pin. A channel nothing was baked into passes every test rather than failing it, so a mistyped tag reads as no constraint at all.

hints.text: The emitted Valency Map supersedes the one that came in, because the grown modules add entries to it. A downstream node handed the input map instead resolves the original modules and loses everything this pass added.

UPCGExValencyBondingGenerativeSettings.name: Valency : Grow Points
UPCGExValencyBondingGenerativeSettings.purpose: Builds structure that did not exist before it ran. Each input point is a seed, and the node grows outward from it by mating connectors, one module at a time, until a budget stops it. What comes back is an ordinary cluster, so the same data a solve consumes is what a growth produces, and passes chain freely. Only connectors take part: growth never reads orbitals.
UPCGExValencyBondingGenerativeSettings.situation: A handful of points that have to become buildings, corridors, pipe runs or vegetation, with nothing to fill in and everything to create.

mechanism.text: One structure per seed point. Each seed is given a starting module, its open connectors enter the frontier, and the chosen strategy repeatedly takes one, finds a module whose connector mates with it, and adds whatever that module left open. Two connectors are consumed per attachment, so a four-socket module contributes three frontier entries rather than four. The run ends when the frontier empties or a budget stops it, and every placed module becomes one Vtx with edges recording what it attached to.

off_label.claim: One seed point with a budget of one module makes this a placement node: it resolves a single module by name and writes it out as a posed point with a Valency entry, which is a cheap way to stamp library pieces without authoring a growth at all.
off_label.grounded_in: Max Total Modules caps the run at any value from 1, and the seed pass alone resolves a module, writes its entry and applies its transform

off_label.claim: The Bridges output is a point set of midpoints carrying their two end modules, so it doubles as a report on how connected a run came out without reading the cluster itself.
off_label.grounded_in: the bridge output pass emits one point per recorded bridge with its start and end module attributes

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: Seed points. One structure grows from each.

inputs.label: External Domains
inputs.note: Any spatial data. Tag it SpatialChannel:Name to route it to a named channel; untagged data lands on the fallback channel. Splines bake to extruded prisms, points to oriented boxes.

inputs.label: Tensors
inputs.note: Tensor fields steering which frontier connector expands next. Shown normally while Tensor Guidance is enabled, and under Advanced otherwise.

inputs.label: Overrides : Strategy
inputs.note: Attribute sets overriding properties on the chosen strategy by name.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: One point per placed module, posed at its attachment and carrying its Valency entry.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One edge per attachment, so the result is a cluster every cluster node downstream accepts.

outputs.label: Valency Map
outputs.note: Required by anything that has to resolve what the entries mean.

outputs.label: Bridges
outputs.note: One point per bridge recorded during the run, at the midpoint, carrying the two modules it joined.

BondingRules.tooltip: The bonding rules data asset (required). Connector set is inferred from this.
BondingRules.semantics: Required here, unlike on a solve: there is no Valency Map coming in to read a library from. The connector set is taken from the asset, so it is never configured separately.
BondingRules.trap: Only modules carrying connectors can take part. A library authored for solving, with orbitals and no connectors, grows nothing and reports no error worth the name.

GrowthStrategy.semantics: A class picker, not a wire. It decides which open connector expands next, which is the single largest influence on the silhouette of the result, and swapping it is cheaper than any amount of rule tuning. A grammar goes in this same slot and replaces the ordering entirely.

fields.name: MaxTotalModules
fields.tooltip: Hard cap on total placed modules

fields.name: MaxDepth
fields.tooltip: Max distance from any seed

fields.name: MaxWeightPerSeed
fields.tooltip: Cumulative module weight budget per seed (-1 = unlimited)

fields.name: bStopOnFirstFailure
fields.tooltip: Stop a branch if no placement found for a socket

fields.name: MaxCandidatesPerConnector
fields.tooltip: Maximum candidate transforms to attempt per connector (constraint budget)

Budget.semantics: The four limits stop different things. Max Total Modules bounds the whole run, so several seeds compete for one pool. Max Depth bounds how far a single line may reach, which is what gives breadth without long runs. Max Weight Per Seed spends module weight, so heavy pieces are both likelier to be drawn and more expensive to place, and -1 turns it off. Max Candidates Per Connector caps how many candidate poses are tried at one connector before growth gives up on it, which matters when connector constraints generate many poses and most are rejected.

AffinityMaps.tooltip: Affinity maps that bias module selection based on tag relationships between parent and candidate.
AffinityMaps.semantics: Read between the parent module and the candidate, so affinity here shapes what attaches to what, unlike a solve where it is read across a finished neighbourhood.

bSeedsCountTowardSpawnLimits.tooltip: Seed modules record into per-module/group spawn limits, so growth can't re-place a capped module already used as a seed. A seed whose module is at cap re-rolls to another valid candidate (placed anyway when none exists).
bSeedsCountTowardSpawnLimits.semantics: With it on, a seed whose module is already at its cap re-rolls to another valid candidate, and is placed anyway when no other candidate exists. Turning it off lets the seed pass spend a capped module and leaves growth unable to place it again, which is the shape you want when the seeds are meant to be distinct from what grows off them.

BoundsInflation.tooltip: Global bounds padding in world units (cm). Positive = gap between modules.
BoundsInflation.semantics: World units, applied globally to every module's bounds, so a positive value opens a gap between neighbours and a negative one lets them nest. It changes what overlap conditions see, so it is also the quickest lever when a run stops far short of its budget because everything collides.

TensorGuidance.tooltip: Tensor-field guidance, active when the Tensors pin is connected: frontier connectors are favored or pruned by how well they align with the field.

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Master toggle. Guidance only activates when this is enabled AND tensors are connected.

fields.name: Influence
fields.tooltip: How strongly alignment reweights frontier selection; 0 leaves it alone (the gate still applies). Shapes the Random strategy only -- BFS/DFS consume alignment by rank.

fields.name: bAbsolute
fields.tooltip: Score connectors aligned with OR against the field equally, so perpendicular scores lowest. Reorders alignment rank, so it affects every strategy.

fields.name: Power
fields.tooltip: Falloff exponent on alignment before weighting; above 1 sharpens the preference. Shapes the Random strategy only -- BFS/DFS consume alignment by rank.

fields.name: bPruneAgainstField
fields.tooltip: Hard gate: connectors below Prune Threshold never enter the frontier, so growth cannot expand against the field. Connectors with no effector in range are never pruned.

fields.name: PruneThreshold
fields.tooltip: Alignment below which connectors are pruned. -1 prunes nothing, 0 prunes anything opposing.

fields.name: TensorHandlerDetails
fields.tooltip: Tensor sampling, applied to the flattened sample on top of each tensor's own mutations.

TensorGuidance.semantics: It has to be enabled here before the Tensors pin moves out of Advanced, and connecting a tensor without enabling this changes nothing. What guidance does depends on the strategy: BFS orders within a ring by alignment, DFS dives along the field, and Random turns its uniform draw into a weighted one.

SeedModuleNameAttribute.tooltip: Attribute on seed points for module name filtering (empty = no filtering)
SeedModuleNameAttribute.semantics: Read per seed point, and a value of None means no request for that point. A name that matches modules restricts that seed to them and deliberately bypasses any seed mask a grammar root would otherwise impose.

bSkipOnUnknownSeedName.tooltip: When the seed name attribute matches no module: off = warn and fall back to the full candidate pool, on = warn and leave the point unseeded.
bSkipOnUnknownSeedName.semantics: Both settings warn. What differs is whether an unmatched name is a typo you want to see as a missing structure, which is on, or a soft preference that should still grow something, which is off.

SeedTagAttribute.tooltip: Attribute on seed points for tag-based filtering (empty = no filtering)
SeedTagAttribute.semantics: Documented in the tooltip as tag-based seed filtering.
SeedTagAttribute.trap: Nothing reads it in this build. The property is declared and never consulted, so a name here filters nothing. Use Seed Module Name Attribute for per-seed narrowing.

EntrySuffix.tooltip: Suffix for the ValencyEntry attribute name (e.g. "Main" -> "PCGEx/V/Entry/Main")
EntrySuffix.semantics: It names the attribute the resolved modules are written to, so it is what lets two independent growth results sit on one dataset without overwriting each other. Every downstream consumer has to be pointed at the same suffix or it finds nothing.

Output.tooltip: Output/attribute toggles shared with the cluster-sourced growth node

fields.name: bApplyLocalTransforms
fields.tooltip: If enabled, applies module's local transform offset to output points

fields.name: ModuleNameAttributeName
fields.tooltip: Attribute name for the resolved module name

fields.name: DepthAttributeName
fields.tooltip: Attribute name for growth depth

fields.name: SeedIndexAttributeName
fields.tooltip: Attribute name for seed index

fields.name: bOutputBridges
fields.tooltip: Emit a separate point set of bridge midpoints, carrying their start and end modules.

fields.name: bOutputConnectorData
fields.tooltip: Write raw connector indices to edges (for connector-level pattern matching)

fields.name: bOutputConnectorClaims
fields.tooltip: Write a per-vertex mask marking connectors consumed by a parent-child connection, so downstream nodes can skip the ones already wired.

Output.semantics: Depth is written by default and module name is not, which is the pair worth changing first: depth is what you filter and colour by while dialling a run in, and the module name is what makes a result readable when it goes wrong. Connector data and claims are on by default because the nodes that continue a growth need them.

bOutputUnsolvableSeeds.tooltip: If enabled, output seeds that couldn't be resolved to modules
bOutputUnsolvableSeeds.semantics: Advertised as emitting the seeds that resolved to no module.
bOutputUnsolvableSeeds.trap: Nothing reads it in this build, and no such output is produced at any setting. A seed that resolves to nothing grows nothing and leaves no trace.

GraphBuilderDetails.tooltip: Graph builder output configuration (edge position, solidification, cluster filtering)
GraphBuilderDetails.semantics: The ordinary PCGEx cluster output configuration, applied to the cluster this node builds. Its minimum-cluster-size filtering is the one to reach for when a run leaves single-module stubs you would rather discard.

ExternalDomains.tooltip: External spatial constraints baked from the External Domains pin, each shape landing in the channel named by its SpatialChannel tag. Queried by the Spatial Domain condition.

fields.name: TagPrefix
fields.tooltip: Tag prefix that identifies the channel key on a tagged data. "SpatialChannel:Bounds" -> channel "Bounds". Inputs without any matching tag fall back to FallbackChannel.

fields.name: FallbackChannel
fields.tooltip: Channel used when a tagged data has no <TagPrefix>:* tag. The data is still baked -- it just lands on this channel. Default = "Default".

fields.name: SplineFidelity
fields.tooltip: Spline-sampling fidelity (squared-distance threshold) forwarded to FPCGSplineStruct::ConvertSplineToPolyLine. Smaller = denser outline.

fields.name: Projection
fields.tooltip: Projection frame for spline -> Polygon bakes. Normal mode reads the spline data's own projection (with FBestFitPlane fallback); BestFit computes the plane from sampled points. Mirrors FPolyPath's behavior.

fields.name: ZMin
fields.tooltip: Z band lower extent for spline -> Polygon bakes. Constant or @Data attribute.

fields.name: ZMax
fields.tooltip: Z band upper extent for spline -> Polygon bakes. Constant or @Data attribute.

ExternalDomains.semantics: Baking settings for whatever arrives on the External Domains pin. The channels themselves are registered in project settings, and a channel nothing was baked into passes every test rather than failing it, so a mistyped tag reads as no constraint at all.

hints.text: Growth checks nothing spatially unless something asks it to. Two modules that mate perfectly can occupy the same space, and the run will place them there. Overlap is refused by placement conditions authored on the modules, or by a grammar rule, and by nothing on this node.

UPCGExValencyBondingRules.name: Bonding Rules Asset
UPCGExValencyBondingRules.purpose: The module library, and the only Valency asset a PCG graph consumes directly. It is assembled from several kinds of source rather than authored by hand: cages gathered through a Context Volume, Module Cages that publish themselves, the collection importer, and any contribution provider a project adds. Every generation node reads one.
UPCGExValencyBondingRules.situation: The library a solve or a growth draws its modules from.

mechanism.text: A compile pass walks the contributions, turns each into a module, and deduplicates the result, so two identical cages become one module. What lands in the asset is the compiled list plus the sets it was compiled against. Editing a level does not leave the asset stale indefinitely: the editor tracks staleness, refreshes on load, and runs a per-tick pass while the Valency editor mode is active.

OrbitalSet.tooltip: Orbital set defining the orbitals for this ruleset. Hard reference -- always loaded with the asset.
OrbitalSet.semantics: A hard reference, so it is always loaded with the asset rather than resolved later. It is also what every downstream consumer falls back to when a node names no set of its own.

ConnectorSet.tooltip: Connector set defining connector types and compatibility rules. Hard reference.
ConnectorSet.semantics: Also a hard reference. A library can carry both sets, and the common shape is exactly that: orbitals carrying the structure and a handful of connectors for whatever attaches to it.

Modules.tooltip: Module definitions -- populated by Compile from cache contributions.

fields.name: Asset
fields.tooltip: The asset to spawn (mesh, actor, data asset, etc.)

fields.name: LocalTransforms
fields.tooltip: Transform variants relative to the spawn point, one picked per point from its seed. Populated when the source cage had bPreserveLocalTransforms enabled.

fields.name: MaterialVariant
fields.tooltip: Material variant for this module. Empty Overrides = no variant.

fields.name: Settings
fields.tooltip: Module settings (weight, spawn constraints)

fields.name: PlacementPolicy
fields.tooltip: How the solver treats this module during placement

fields.name: bHasPlacementBoundsOverride
fields.tooltip: Whether a cage component overrode the collision bounds. Affects solver overlap tests only -- output point bounds are untouched, and Bounds Inflation does not apply on top.

fields.name: PlacementBoundsOverride
fields.tooltip: Cage-local AABB used as the collision/overlap bounds when bHasPlacementBoundsOverride.

fields.name: Bounds
fields.tooltip: Visual bounds driving the mesh-fitting transform during staging. Distinct from the collision override and from AuthoredFootprint.

fields.name: AuthoredFootprint
fields.tooltip: Growth-time authored spatial footprint (OBBs, polygons, channels), sourced from the cage.

fields.name: ModuleName
fields.tooltip: Optional module name, from the source cage. Used to pre-assign fixed picks to vertices; empty means it cannot be fixed-picked by name.

fields.name: OrbitalMask
fields.tooltip: Bitmask indicating which orbitals this module has (bits set = orbital exists)

fields.name: BoundaryOrbitalMask
fields.tooltip: Bitmask indicating which orbitals connect to boundaries/null cages (nothing may sit there)

fields.name: WildcardOrbitalMask
fields.tooltip: Bitmask indicating which orbitals connect to wildcards (something must sit there)

fields.name: AcceptAnyOrbitalMask
fields.tooltip: Bitmask of orbitals that accept ANY neighbour. Where a bit is CLEAR, OrbitalNeighbors is authoritative -- and an empty list there means "accepts nothing", not "accepts everything". See PCGExValency::DeriveAcceptAnyMask.

fields.name: OrbitalNeighbors
fields.tooltip: Valid neighbor module indices per orbital. Key = OrbitalName, Value = array of valid module indices

fields.name: PropertyOverrides
fields.tooltip: Per-module property overrides, parallel to UPCGExValencyBondingRules::DefaultProperties. Cage-authored properties seed this as enabled overrides, and are re-synced to the schema at compile so they survive renames and reorders.

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Gameplay tags from source cage and mirrored palettes.

fields.name: Connectors
fields.tooltip: Typed connection points mapping to orbital indices, from the cage's connector components. The alternative to direction-based orbital assignment.

fields.name: SpanPairs
fields.tooltip: Scalable connector spans for bridge modules -- two connectors plus their scale limits.

fields.name: ConnectorTransformStrategy
fields.tooltip: How connector offsets move from cage space to the target space at compile. Empty = no transform, i.e. cage-relative.

Modules.semantics: Populated by the compile from cache contributions rather than authored here. Reading it is how you check what a compile actually produced; editing it is overwritten by the next rebuild.

CategoryTagRoot.tooltip: Tag root mapped to generated-entry Category ('Category.Walls' -> "Walls"), else the asset type. Informational only -- the solver never reads it.
CategoryTagRoot.semantics: Informational. It maps a tag root onto the generated entry Category so a collection reads tidily downstream, and the solver never consults it, so no placement behaviour follows from changing it.

bUseExternalAssets.tooltip: Externalize the generated collection as a standalone uasset a Variant Collection can source. Pipeline-managed -- overwritten each rebuild, never hand-edited.
bUseExternalAssets.semantics: Externalises the generated collection so a Variant Collection can source it. The written assets are pipeline-managed and overwritten on every rebuild, so nothing hand-edited there survives.

ExportFolder.tooltip: Where externalized assets are written. Empty warns and falls back to embedded for that rebuild.
ExportFolder.semantics: An empty folder is not an error: the rebuild warns and falls back to embedding for that pass, so the symptom is a collection that quietly stopped being external rather than a failed compile.

LevelContributors.tooltip: Levels this asset draws cage data from. Dropped manually, or auto-registered by volumes that target this asset -- module cages never register themselves.

fields.name: Level
fields.tooltip: Soft reference to the level -- most levels aren't loaded when the consumer asset is.

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Temporarily exclude this contributor, keeping its shadow and flags for later re-enable.

LevelContributors.semantics: Dropped in by hand, or auto-registered by a Context Volume that targets this asset.
LevelContributors.trap: A Module Cage never registers itself here. Which rules asset consumes one is that asset decision, so a Module Cage that appears to contribute nothing is usually missing from this list.

ContributionProviders.tooltip: Compile-time payload sources beyond direct level contributors: the built-in collection importer, or any user-defined UPCGExValencyContributionProvider subclass. Never reaches cooked builds.
ContributionProviders.semantics: Compile-time sources beyond direct levels: the built-in collection importer, or a project own subclass. None of it reaches a cooked build, so a provider is an authoring-time route into the library and never a runtime one.

LevelBoundsEvaluator.tooltip: Bounds evaluator for synthetic level entries. Fallback only -- a cage override or a source collection's per-entry bounds wins.
LevelBoundsEvaluator.default:
Cast<UPCGExBoundsEvaluator>(
		ObjectInitializer.CreateDefaultSubobject(this, TEXT("LevelBoundsEvaluator"),
		                                         UPCGExBoundsEvaluator::StaticClass(), EvalClass, false, false))

LevelContentFilter.tooltip: Content filter applied to the generated collection's synthetic level entries.
LevelContentFilter.default:
Cast<UPCGExActorContentFilter>(
		ObjectInitializer.CreateDefaultSubobject(this, TEXT("LevelContentFilter"),
		                                         UPCGExActorContentFilter::StaticClass(), FilterClass, false, false))

fields.name: Schemas
fields.tooltip: Schema array (locals -- always take precedence over imported entries with matching names)

fields.name: ImportedSchemas
fields.tooltip: Imported schema assets, resolved in array order after locals. Hard refs -- assets stay loaded as long as the owning collection exists. Recursion through imported assets' own ImportedSchemas is supported with cycle detection.

fields.name: ImportOverrides
fields.tooltip: Per-entry value overrides for imported entries. EditAnywhere is required so the detail panel's GetChildHandle can reach this property's children -- the registered FPCGExPropertySchemaCollectionCustomization takes over rendering entirely (CustomizeChildren controls every visible row), so this never appears as a top-level array editor in the inspector. The array is kept parallel with the imports-only schema via ReconcileImportOverrides (which delegates to FPCGExPropertyOverrides::SyncToSchema). UE per-instance UPROPERTY delta serialization handles three-layer composition: asset default -> template (collection on CDO) -> instance (collection on actor instance). Each layer overrides the previous via bEnabled toggles on individual entries. Locals do not appear here -- they are edited in-place on Schemas.

DefaultProperties.semantics: The values a module falls back to when its cage authored none. Valency : Load Properties reads this as one of its two defaults tiers, which is what lets a property exist on every point without being authored on every cage.

bCompileOnRebuild.tooltip: Compile during BuildFromCages and serialize the result with the asset.

bAutoRebuildOnStale.tooltip: Auto-refresh from PostLoad / asset-registry hooks when upstream dependencies change.
bAutoRebuildOnStale.semantics: Off, the asset holds whatever it last compiled until you rebuild it by hand, which is the setting for a library that should stop moving while a graph is being tuned around it.

bEntryDedupIncludesModuleName.tooltip: Include the module name (mirrored as grammar Symbol) in generated-entry identity. Off, modules producing identical entry content merge into one shared entry even when their names differ (first module's name wins); on, differing names keep separate entries.
bEntryDedupIncludesModuleName.semantics: Off, two modules whose entry content is identical merge into one shared entry even when their names differ, which keeps a generated collection small. On, the name participates in identity and near-identical modules stay separate, which is what you want when something downstream reads the module name.

hints.text: A great deal of the refresh automation is gated on the Valency editor mode being active. Compiling from a level that is open without that mode on is the usual reason a rebuild appears to have missed a cage.

UPCGExValencyBondingSettings.name: Valency : Solve
UPCGExValencyBondingSettings.purpose: Fills a cluster you already have: one module per Vtx, chosen so that every orbital facing a neighbour accepts what sits there. Nothing moves, nothing is added and nothing is removed, so the count in equals the count out and the answer arrives on the points as a Valency entry. Which strategy walks the cluster is picked in the details panel, and everything else on the node narrows or steers the outcome.
UPCGExValencyBondingSettings.situation: A cluster carrying orbital data that has to become an arrangement of modules obeying a library of bonding rules.

mechanism.text: Each Vtx becomes one position holding the modules whose orbital mask fits the orbitals that Vtx actually has. The chosen strategy commits positions one at a time, narrowing the neighbours each commit rules out, until nothing is left to decide. Positions the main pass cannot fill go to a filler sweep, and whatever fillers cannot cover is marked unsolvable. A pass that leaves unsolvable positions or unmet minimums is re-run from a derived seed, and the best attempt is what reaches the output.
steps: Positions outside the vtx filters, or excluded by Solve Target, are set aside as fixed context before anything is decided.
Fixed picks are applied, and every remaining position is narrowed against them.
Fillers cover what is left, and anything still empty is marked unsolvable.

off_label.claim: Chaining two of these covers the finish-the-rest case: a first pass over part of the cluster, then a second with no filters and Solve Target on Unsolved Only, which completes the remainder without maintaining an inverted filter set.
off_label.grounded_in: SolveTarget UnsolvedOnly keeps any Vtx carrying a decodable entry as fixed context, and the output Valency Map feeds straight back into the input pin

off_label.claim: With the transform policy on, output points come back posed and bounded like staged points, so a solve can feed a mesh spawner directly when all you need is the asset in place.
off_label.grounded_in: the resolved module asset delta is composed onto the point transform and the module staging bounds replace the point bounds

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of every cluster to solve. One position per Vtx.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Each Edges dataset that finds its Vtx is one cluster and one solve.

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Supplies the orbital substrate written by Write Orbitals or Lattice. With no Bonding Rules asset set on the node, the library comes from here too.

inputs.label: Vtx Filters
inputs.note: Narrows which Vtx are re-solved. A failing Vtx keeps whatever module it arrived with and becomes fixed context for its neighbours.

inputs.label: FixedPickFilters
inputs.note: Narrows which Vtx are eligible for a fixed pick. Read only while Enable Fixed Picks is on, and tucked under Advanced otherwise.

inputs.label: Biases
inputs.note: Valency : Bias and Valency : Bias (Channel) nodes. They reshape the per-position draw and forbid nothing.

inputs.label: Overrides : Strategy
inputs.note: Attribute sets overriding properties on the chosen strategy by name, so a strategy setting can be driven from data.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The same Vtx, each carrying the entry for its resolved module, plus the unsolvable marker when that is on.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: Forwarded unchanged. A solve never touches connectivity.

outputs.label: Valency Map
outputs.note: This solve's rules and orbital substrate, for Staging, Load Properties, Find Patterns and Write Connectors downstream.

Solver.semantics: A class picker, not a wire: the strategy is chosen here and its own settings appear inline underneath it. Swapping strategies keeps everything above and below intact, so trying another one costs a dropdown.

AffinityMaps.tooltip: Affinity maps that bias module selection based on tag relationships.
AffinityMaps.semantics: Configured on the node rather than on the strategy, so the same maps survive a strategy swap. Several maps combine into one table before the solve starts.

GuidancePatterns.tooltip: Patterns steering module selection toward desired topologies. Connector or Cage assets.
GuidancePatterns.semantics: Each candidate is scored by how much of a pattern it would complete around its position, and that score folds into the draw as a weight multiplier. Guidance stays a preference throughout: a pattern nothing can complete costs nothing and never fires.

GuidanceStrength.tooltip: How strongly patterns influence module selection (0 = off, 1 = equal to module weight).
GuidanceStrength.semantics: At 0 the patterns are skipped outright, which is the cheap way to compare a guided result against an unguided one without unwiring anything.

SolveTarget.tooltip: Which vtx the solve is allowed to (re-)solve. Unsolved Only keeps vtx inheriting a valid module as fixed context.
SolveTarget.semantics: It narrows by what a position already carries, where the vtx filters narrow by what a filter says about it. Both narrow and neither widens the other, so Unsolved Only on a filtered pass shrinks that pass further and never reaches back for Vtx the filters rejected. On input carrying no modules the two values behave identically.
SolveTarget.trap: A position counts as solved only when its entry decodes under the rules this pass is solving with. In a map carrying several rule sets, an entry written under a different one reads as nothing here, so Unsolved Only leaves that position eligible and re-solves it. The node warns and names the count.

UnsolvedEntryHandling.tooltip: What happens to a solve-eligible vtx's inherited ValencyEntry when the solve leaves it without a module.
UnsolvedEntryHandling.semantics: It speaks only for positions this pass was allowed to solve. A position kept as fixed context by Solve Target or by a filter passes its entry through untouched either way. Clear is what makes a failed position read as empty downstream instead of as whatever it used to be.

LockedVtxMode.tooltip: What a vtx-filter-locked vtx WITHOUT a decodable module means to the solver.
LockedVtxMode.semantics: It speaks only for filter-locked Vtx carrying no readable module. Treat As Empty clears the orbital bits facing those positions on their neighbours, so a neighbour has to accept a boundary there. Ignore leaves the neighbours unconstrained, which is the setting for a hole a later pass will fill.

FixedPicks.tooltip: Fixed pick configuration (active when Enable Fixed Picks is on)

fields.name: FixedPickAttribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute holding the module name to pre-assign. Empty = no fixed pick for that vertex.

fields.name: FixedPickSelectionMode
fields.tooltip: How to select when multiple modules match the fixed pick name

fields.name: IncompatibleFixedPickBehavior
fields.tooltip: Behavior when fixed pick module doesn't fit the node's orbital configuration

fields.name: bWarnOnUnmatchedFixedPick
fields.tooltip: Warn when fixed pick name doesn't match any module

fields.name: bWarnOnIncompatibleFixedPick
fields.tooltip: Warn when fixed pick module doesn't fit orbital configuration (only when Skip behavior)

fields.name: bDefaultFixedPickFilterValue
fields.tooltip: Default filter value when no fixed pick filters are connected (true = all points eligible)

FixedPicks.semantics: The attribute holds a module name, and an empty value means no pick for that Vtx. A pick is applied before the strategy runs and then propagated, so neighbours are narrowed against it rather than left to discover it. Positions kept as fixed context by Solve Target are skipped.

bUseForwardChecking.tooltip: Reject a module if committing it would empty an unresolved neighbor's candidate set. Greatly reduces interior dead-ends that fall back to filler.
bUseForwardChecking.semantics: The test looks one hop out: a candidate is refused when committing it would leave an unresolved neighbour with an empty candidate set, and refusal costs only a retry. Off restores the older behaviour, where a legal-looking commit can strand the position beyond it and the filler sweep absorbs the damage.

MaxSolveRestarts.tooltip: Extra re-seeded attempts when the first leaves unsolvable nodes or unmet minimums; the best is kept. Each retry derives its seed from the base one, so output stays reproducible.
MaxSolveRestarts.semantics: Attempts are compared on unsolvable count first and unmet minimums second, and the best one reaches the output. A clean pass stops the loop immediately, so raising this costs nothing on a library that solves and one whole extra solve per attempt on one that does not.

bValidateSpawnFeasibility.tooltip: Check minimum-spawn feasibility up front and error if the tileset is over-constrained. Diagnostic only -- it never changes solving.
bValidateSpawnFeasibility.semantics: It runs once, before the first attempt, and reports as warnings rather than stopping the node. Leave it on while a ruleset is still being shaped: it names an impossible minimum before the solve, instead of leaving you to read holes afterwards.

bUsePerClusterSeed.tooltip: Vary the solve per cluster by mixing a content hash of its point seeds into the solve seed. Still deterministic -- the same points always solve the same way, whatever the ordering.
bUsePerClusterSeed.semantics: Without it, every cluster in one execution solves from the same seed, so identical clusters come out identical. Mixing in a hash of each cluster's own point seeds separates them while keeping every one reproducible, and reordering the inputs changes nothing.

bOutputUnsolvableMarker.tooltip: If enabled, output an attribute marking unsolvable nodes
bOutputUnsolvableMarker.semantics: Written per Vtx, true only where the solve genuinely ran out of options.
bOutputUnsolvableMarker.trap: Filter-locked positions are skipped by the writer, so they carry false whether or not they hold a module. Read the marker as a report on the positions this pass solved, never as a census of empty ones.

UnsolvableAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the unsolvable marker

bPruneUnsolvable.tooltip: If enabled, prune nodes that failed to solve
bPruneUnsolvable.semantics: It gathers the unsolvable points and stops there.
bPruneUnsolvable.trap: Nothing is removed. The removal step is unimplemented in this build, so the setting is inert and the output still carries every unsolvable point. Filter on the unsolvable marker downstream to drop them.

bApplyConnectorTransformPolicy.tooltip: Move output points to each resolved module's asset pose, matching the generative path. Off keeps them at their input cage transform. Cage-Relative modules never move.
bApplyConnectorTransformPolicy.semantics: It also replaces each point's bounds with the resolved module's staging bounds, so transform and bounds stay in one frame and the points read like staged ones. A position kept as fixed context is skipped, because the pass that placed its module already posed it.

hints.text: The orbital substrate has to exist before a solve. A cluster straight out of a connect node carries none, and the solve has nothing to fit modules against. Run Valency : Write Orbitals or Valency : Lattice first, and take the Valency Map from there.

UPCGExValencyConnectorFilterProviderSett.name: ✱ Filter : Connectors
UPCGExValencyConnectorFilterProviderSett.purpose: The connector-side sibling of the orbitals filter, asking which of a point's connectors are still open and which a structural connection already spent. Since claims are what growth writes as it builds, this is mostly a filter for results: finding the pieces that still have somewhere to build, or the ones that are fully consumed.
UPCGExValencyConnectorFilterProviderSett.situation: Aiming a second growth pass at the parts of a structure that still have a free socket.

mechanism.text: Operand A is a claim fact, read per point. Operand B names which of that point's connectors take part, and the comparison between them decides the verdict. Both operands live in the module's own instance space, so the same selection resolves to a different set of instances on every module: Types picks whatever instances of those types each module happens to carry, and an index means the module's nth connector rather than anything global.

off_label.claim: Claimed with an All selection and a count comparison of every bit finds the modules with nothing left open, which is the set a further growth pass can skip entirely.
off_label.grounded_in: the count mode compares shared bits against a threshold bounded to the instances the resolved module actually has

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Resolves entries to modules and supplies the connector set the claim layer is named by. Always needed by this filter, and required on the pin in Pin mode.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: An ordinary point filter factory, accepted anywhere a filter pin is.

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Where the entry layer, the resolving Valency Map and the claim layer come from.

fields.name: Fact
fields.tooltip: Operand A -- the connector fact tested at each point.

fields.name: Selection
fields.tooltip: Operand B -- which of the module's connectors take part in the test.

fields.name: Identifiers
fields.tooltip: Connector identifiers, matched against each module's own instances. An identifier matching nothing on any module selects nothing and warns.

fields.name: ConnectorTypes
fields.tooltip: Connector type names -- selects every instance of these types on each module.

fields.name: ConnectorIndices
fields.tooltip: Raw module-local instance indices. Out-of-range entries select nothing on that module.

fields.name: Check
fields.tooltip: How operand A is compared against operand B -- the shared Valency fact-check machinery.

fields.name: NoModuleFallback
fields.tooltip: Result for points carrying no module. Honored as-is -- Invert does not flip fallbacks.

fields.name: UnresolvedFallback
fields.tooltip: Result for entries whose rule set is not in the resolved map (merged maps, mismatched wiring).

fields.name: ConsumedFallback
fields.tooltip: Result for pattern-consumed points (absorbed by a pattern -- they place nothing).

UPCGExValencyConnectorSet.name: Connector Set
UPCGExValencyConnectorSet.purpose: The connector type table, the compatibility between every pair of types, and the polarity rules. It is the asset to settle early: connector instances are authored individually on each module, and they all resolve their meaning through this one table.
UPCGExValencyConnectorSet.situation: Deciding what kinds of connection exist and which of them accept each other.

mechanism.text: Up to 63 types, with bit 63 of the compatibility mask reserved. Compatibility is set per type, so the table grows with the square of the type count and a large set is a real authoring commitment. Everything downstream reads type identity from here, which is why a bridge module drawn from a different set connects to nothing.

LayerName.tooltip: Layer name - for multi-layer connector systems, determines attribute naming
LayerName.semantics: It names the attributes this set writes, the connector-side counterpart to the orbital set identifier. A consumer inheriting its claim layer resolves it through whichever set the source knows, so leaving this at the default is what keeps that inheritance working.

ConnectorTypes.tooltip: Connector type definitions, max 63 (bit 63 of the compatibility mask is reserved). Compatibility between them is set per type. Scripted mutation (editor-utility BP/Python) that bypasses property-change events MUST call EDITOR_Recompile afterwards -- the compiled CompatibilityMatrix is index-mapped and does not self-heal until the asset reloads.

fields.name: ConnectorType
fields.tooltip: Connector type name - used for compatibility matrix lookup and matching

fields.name: CompatibleTypeIds
fields.tooltip: Types this one may ATTACH ONTO, by TypeId (rename-proof). DIRECTIONAL: growth tests the CANDIDATE's row against the open parent type, so a fallback type can list everything while nothing grows onto it; bridges and cage links require both rows.

fields.name: DefaultOffset
fields.tooltip: Default transform offset relative to module origin (can be overridden per-module)

fields.name: DebugColor
fields.tooltip: Debug visualization color

fields.name: DefaultConstraints
fields.tooltip: Default constraints applied to all connectors of this type (can be overridden per-instance)

fields.name: IconIndex
fields.tooltip: Visual icon index (0-63). -1 = auto-assign from array position.

ConnectorTypes.semantics: Compatibility is authored per type and is what growth and bridging both consult.
ConnectorTypes.trap: Bridging needs both types to accept each other, where growth only needs the one being grown from to accept. A one-way row steers growth perfectly well and never bridges, which is worth checking before the geometry when two parts refuse to join.

hints.text: Scripted mutation that bypasses the property-change path leaves the compiled compatibility stale. Reach for Recompile after any editor-utility or Python edit to this table.

UPCGExValencyConstraintSolverFactory.name: Constraint Solver
UPCGExValencyConstraintSolverFactory.purpose: Visits positions in the same fewest-candidates order the default does, and spends its effort on hitting minimum spawns. It keeps a running count of how many positions each module could still be placed in, weighs that against what the module's minimum still owes, and lets the resulting pressure scale how hard the draw leans toward it. A module with no spare positions left is committed without a draw at all.
UPCGExValencyConstraintSolverFactory.situation: A library with minimums that have to be met, where the result must contain specific things and not merely be valid.

mechanism.text: Alongside the ordinary candidate sets the solver holds a slot budget: for every module, how many undecided positions it still fits. Each pick reads that budget as pressure, and a module whose spare positions have run out is committed on the spot. Below that point the pressure scales a multiplier on the module's weight, so an urgent module competes harder without being forced. The same budget is what lets the solve report a library as unsatisfiable, when some module needs more positions than the cluster can ever offer it.

UrgencyBoostMultiplier.tooltip: Urgency weight boost -- higher prioritizes constrained modules more aggressively.
UrgencyBoostMultiplier.semantics: The boost scales with pressure rather than replacing the weight: a module at half its available positions leans about half as hard as one at the brink. The default of 10 sits deliberately far above the ordinary minimum-spawn boost, which is the reason to reach for this solver at all. Higher crowds out unpressured modules and flattens variety; down near 1 the solve behaves much like the entropy one.

MinimumSpawnWeightBoost.tooltip: Fallback weight boost for modules needing minimum spawns (used when urgency < 1.0)
MinimumSpawnWeightBoost.semantics: It reaches the filler sweep, where the shared weighted draw applies it to any filler still owing a minimum.
MinimumSpawnWeightBoost.trap: It does not reach the main pass at all. Urgency replaces it there by design, so changing this value leaves an ordinary solve looking identical and only moves the fillers. Urgency Boost Multiplier is the dial that changes how the solve itself leans.

UPCGExValencyEntropySolver.name: Entropy Solver
UPCGExValencyEntropySolver.purpose: The strategy **Valency : Solve** runs unless you pick another. It decides the position with the fewest surviving candidates first, because a position with little freedom left is the one a later commit can still ruin, while a roomy one will still be roomy in a hundred steps. One setting, and it only tilts the draw toward modules still owing minimum spawns.
UPCGExValencyEntropySolver.situation: The ordinary solve: a cluster to fill from a library, with no order of your own to impose.

mechanism.text: Every position starts holding the modules whose orbital mask fits it. The solver takes the position with the smallest surviving candidate set, draws one module from it by weight, and narrows the neighbours that choice rules out. Equal candidate counts go to the position with the higher share of already-decided neighbours, then to the lower Vtx index, so the order is reproducible for a given seed. Whatever the pass leaves undecided goes to the filler sweep, and what fillers cannot cover comes back marked unsolvable.

off_label.claim: At a Minimum Spawn Weight Boost of 1 the minimum-spawn preference is off and the draw is the library weights alone, which is the cleanest way to see what a tileset does before quotas start bending it.
off_label.grounded_in: SelectWeightedRandom multiplies by MinimumSpawnWeightBoost only when the tracker reports the module behind on its minimum, and the property clamps at 1

MinimumSpawnWeightBoost.tooltip: Weight boost multiplier for modules that need more spawns to meet minimum
MinimumSpawnWeightBoost.semantics: It multiplies a module's draw weight for as long as that module is behind on its minimum, and stops the moment the quota is met. Partitioned limits count per partition, so a module can be boosted in one partition and drawn at plain weight in another. It shifts odds, so a minimum only one position could ever satisfy is still missed.

UPCGExValencyFindBridgesSettings.name: Valency : Find Bridges
UPCGExValencyFindBridgesSettings.purpose: Bridging as its own pass, run after the fact on a cluster whose modules are already resolved. Where a growth run bridges opportunistically while it builds, this one looks at a finished result and places bridge modules wherever two genuinely open connectors accept each other. It works on solve output as readily as on growth output, which is what makes it the way to add circulation to a solved layout.
UPCGExValencyFindBridgesSettings.situation: A resolved cluster whose parts sit near each other but are not joined, and should be.

mechanism.text: Every Vtx is read back as a resolved module, and the connectors the input has not already spent become bridge candidates. Pairs are formed either by proximity, by walking the existing edges, or both, and each accepted pair gets a bridge module placed between it. The cluster is extended in place: the input Vtx and edges come back unchanged with the bridge modules and their edges added, and the emitted Valency Map carries the new entries alongside the old ones.

off_label.claim: Edge Guided with a bridge module authored as a plain connector turns this into a way of thickening an existing cluster: every edge that can carry one gets a piece placed along it, which is a topology-driven decoration pass rather than a bridging one.
off_label.grounded_in: the edge-guided pass walks existing edges and bridges their endpoints remaining open connectors, capped per edge by Max Bridges Per Edge

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of the cluster to bridge. Every Vtx is read back as a resolved module.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Blind search skips endpoints these already join, and Edge Guided walks them.

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Resolves what the input entries mean, and supplies the library unless Bridge Bonding Rules names another.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The input Vtx, unmoved, plus one new Vtx per placed bridge module.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: The input edges plus the two edges each bridge adds, joining it to the modules at both ends.

outputs.label: Valency Map
outputs.note: Input entries and bridge entries together. Chain this one onward; the input map does not know the bridges exist.

SearchMode.tooltip: How bridge-eligible connector pairs are found.
SearchMode.semantics: Blind Search pairs open connectors by proximity and skips endpoints an edge already joins, so it finds connections the topology does not have. Edge Guided walks the edges instead and bridges what their endpoints left open, so it can only reinforce connections that already exist. Both runs the edge-guided pass first and blind search over whatever is still open afterwards, which is deliberate: topology gets first claim on the connectors.

OpenConnectorSource.tooltip: What counts a connector as already consumed -- only open ones become bridge candidates.
OpenConnectorSource.semantics: The same four ways of deciding what the input already spent that Grow Cluster offers, and the same consequence: only connectors this reports as open become candidates.
OpenConnectorSource.trap: The default reads the claim mask a growth pass writes, and a missing attribute is taken to mean everything is open. On solve output that makes every connector a candidate, including the ones already carrying an edge. Switch to Orbital Inference for anything that came from a solve.

BridgeSearchRadius.tooltip: Search radius for compatible connector pairs. Blind search only -- edges bound the other pass.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

BridgeSearchRadius.semantics: World units between the two open connectors, and it bounds blind search only, since edges bound the other pass. It reads as a constant or from an attribute, so the reach can vary across a cluster.

MaxBridgesPerEdge.tooltip: Max bridges placed over a single existing edge in the edge-guided pass. 0 = unlimited.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

MaxBridgesPerEdge.semantics: Applies to the edge-guided pass, where one existing edge can support several bridges between the connectors its endpoints left open. 0 lifts the cap entirely. It reads as a constant or from an attribute, and where that attribute lives is the next setting.

BridgeCapSource.tooltip: Where Max Bridges Per Edge is read from when it is attribute-driven.
BridgeCapSource.semantics: Vtx reads the cap from the edge's two endpoints and applies the smaller of them, so a Vtx that should carry few bridges limits every edge touching it. Edge reads it from the edge point, which is the setting for a cap authored per connection rather than per position.

DistanceTolerance.tooltip: Distance tolerance for bridge modules without span pairs (0..1 fraction of module connector distance).
DistanceTolerance.semantics: A fraction of the bridge module's own connector-to-connector distance, not a world distance, so it scales with the piece rather than with the cluster. It governs bridge modules that carry no authored span pair, where the gap has to be judged against the module rather than measured against an authored one.

BridgeBondingRules.tooltip: Rules to source bridge modules from; null uses the Valency Map's. Must use the same Connector Set as the solved modules.
BridgeBondingRules.semantics: Left empty, bridges come from whatever library the Valency Map resolves to, which is the ordinary case. Naming a separate asset is for keeping bridge pieces out of the library the structure itself was built from.
BridgeBondingRules.trap: A separate asset has to use the same Connector Set as the solved modules. A different one produces connector types that mean nothing to the structure, and nothing bridges.

bCheckBoundsOverlap.tooltip: If enabled, check placed bridge bounds against existing modules and skip overlapping bridges.
bCheckBoundsOverlap.semantics: A bridge occupies space like any other placement, and this is what refuses one that would sit inside an existing module. Turning it off is how bridges end up buried, and turning it on with bridge pieces authored larger than the gaps they span is how a run finds pairs and places none.

bApplyConnectorGates.tooltip: Honor per-connector conditional gates when collecting open endpoints, consistent with growth and Write Connectors. Off = bridge endpoints ignore gates entirely.
bApplyConnectorGates.semantics: Keeps this pass consistent with growth and Write Connectors, which both honour gates. Off, a gated connector counts as open here and not there, so the same cluster reports different open sets to different nodes.

bUpdateConnectivityAttributes.tooltip: Write bridge consumption back into the connectivity attributes, so chained claim-aware nodes see it.
bUpdateConnectivityAttributes.semantics: Writes the consumption back, so a following claim-aware node sees the connectors this pass spent. Leaving it off makes a second bridging pass, or a following Grow Cluster on Connector Claims, treat every bridged connector as still open.

GraphBuilderDetails.tooltip: Graph builder output configuration for bridge edges (edge position, solidification, cluster filtering)
GraphBuilderDetails.semantics: The ordinary PCGEx cluster output configuration, applied to the extended cluster rather than to the bridges alone.

hints.text: Bridging is an undirected meeting, so both connector types have to accept each other. A one-way compatibility pair steers growth perfectly well and never bridges. Where two parts refuse to join, check both rows of the compatibility table before looking at the geometry.

UPCGExValencyGrowthBFSFactory.name: BFS Growth
UPCGExValencyGrowthBFSFactory.purpose: Expands the frontier in rings: every connector at one distance from the seed is spent before any connector further out is touched. The result fills outward evenly and stays compact, so a budget that runs out mid-run leaves a smaller version of the same shape rather than one long arm and nothing else. It supports seed patterns.
UPCGExValencyGrowthBFSFactory.situation: A structure that should read as a mass around its seed, filling out from the middle.

mechanism.text: Frontier entries are ordered by how many attachments separate them from their seed, closest first. Within one ring, connectors authored with a higher priority go first, and tensor guidance breaks what is still tied so that the best-aligned connector in a ring expands before the rest. Ordering by distance is the whole of the strategy: which module lands on the connector, and whether it is allowed to, are decided elsewhere.

off_label.claim: Because a ring completes before the next one starts, cutting a run short with Max Total Modules gives a usable smaller structure, which makes this the strategy to grow with while dialling a budget in.
off_label.grounded_in: the frontier heap orders on depth ascending before any other key, so every entry at depth n is popped before any at depth n plus one

hints.text: Connector priority only separates connectors within one ring here. A high-priority connector two attachments out still waits for every connector one attachment out, whatever its priority.

UPCGExValencyGrowthDFSFactory.name: DFS Growth
UPCGExValencyGrowthDFSFactory.purpose: Follows one line as far as it will go before coming back for anything else, so structures come out as tendrils and corridors rather than as a mass. Reach is what this buys: a budget spent depth first puts the far end of the structure a long way from its seed. It supports seed patterns.
UPCGExValencyGrowthDFSFactory.situation: Corridors, vines, pipe runs, anything whose point is to get somewhere rather than to fill a space.

mechanism.text: The frontier is a stack, and the connector taken next is the one most recently added, which is always a connector on the module just placed. Growth therefore runs outward until the current line has nothing left open, then unwinds to the most recent unspent connector and carries on from there. When tensor guidance is active the newly opened connectors are stacked worst-aligned first, so the best-aligned one is on top and the tendril follows the field.

off_label.claim: Stopping a run early leaves one or two long arms and most of the structure unbuilt, so a budget dialled in on this strategy has to be judged on the finished run rather than on a truncated one.
off_label.grounded_in: the LIFO frontier pops the most recently pushed connector, so depth is exhausted before breadth and Max Total Modules cuts across an unfinished line

hints.text: Long thin runs fold back on themselves readily, so this is the strategy where footprint overlap conditions earn their keep. Without one, a corridor happily grows back through the room it came from.

UPCGExValencyGrowthFactory.name: Growth Strategy
UPCGExValencyGrowthFactory.purpose: The shared base every growth strategy is built on, and where the settings they all have in common are declared. It never appears in the palette on its own: a strategy is picked in the details panel of **Valency : Grow Points** or **Valency : Grow Cluster**, and what it adds to this base is the one decision of which open connector comes off the frontier next. Everything on this page is the same whichever strategy you picked, including under a grammar.
UPCGExValencyGrowthFactory.situation: Reading what the pattern and bridge settings on a growth strategy do, without caring which strategy is selected.

mechanism.text: Growth places modules and this base decides three things around that: which arrangements are forbidden, which arrangement each seed starts from, and how separate branches get joined back together. The pattern slots are checked at placement time, so a candidate completing a rejection pattern is refused and growth tries something else. Bridging runs alongside the main loop: connectors that meet are always recorded, and searching for pairs to span is opt-in.

RejectionPatterns.tooltip: Patterns that forbid certain topologies during growth. Accepts both Connector and Cage pattern assets.
RejectionPatterns.semantics: A veto expressed as an arrangement rather than as a connector rule, for the shapes that are individually legal and collectively wrong. Refusal costs only the candidate: growth tries the next module and carries on. Both Connector and Cage pattern assets are accepted.

SeedPatterns.tooltip: Patterns stamped as pre-built module groups from seed points. Connector or Cage assets.
SeedPatterns.semantics: Stamped from the seed points as pre-built groups, so growth starts from an authored arrangement rather than one module. A stamp is transactional: one member refused by a placement condition abandons the whole arrangement, so a stamp landing half inside a region reads as no stamp at all.
SeedPatterns.trap: The row is hidden on any strategy that does not support seeding, and Random Growth is one of them. Move the same setup to BFS or DFS if the row is not there.

bEnableActiveBridging.tooltip: Enable active bridge searching during growth. When false, only natural (overlap) bridges are detected.
bEnableActiveBridging.semantics: Natural bridging, where two open connectors that happen to meet are recorded and consumed, is always on and costs nothing. This is the other kind: a search for pairs within a radius, scored, with a module placed to span the winner. It needs a module authored with a placement policy of Bridge Only, because ordinary growth modules are excluded from spanning.

BridgeSearchRadius.tooltip: Search radius for bridge candidates -- connectors this close, on different branches, pair up.
BridgeSearchRadius.semantics: World units, measured between the two open connectors, and only pairs on different branches are gathered. Widening it grows the candidate set quadratically in a dense frontier, which is where active bridging starts to cost real time.

BridgeOverlapTolerance.tooltip: Overlap tolerance for natural bridge detection (world units). Tight tolerance for accidental overlaps.
BridgeOverlapTolerance.semantics: This one governs natural bridging, so it applies whether or not the active search is on. It is how close two open connectors must come to count as having met, and it is deliberately tight: loosening it makes structures close loops they were never meant to close.

BridgeScoreWeightDistance.tooltip: Weight for distance component of bridge scoring (closer = better)
BridgeScoreWeightDistance.semantics: The three scoring weights are independent and each clamps to 0 through 1, so they express relative pull rather than shares of a total. Zeroing all three leaves every candidate tied and the pick arbitrary.

BridgeScoreWeightAlignment.tooltip: Weight for alignment component of bridge scoring (aligned connectors = better)

BridgeScoreWeightBranchDiversity.tooltip: Weight for branch diversity (cross-seed > within-seed bridging)
BridgeScoreWeightBranchDiversity.semantics: Diversity here is measured across seeds, so raising it pulls bridges toward joining separate structures rather than closing loops inside one. Leave it low when the aim is circulation within a single grown mass.

hints.text: A bridge occupies space and is checked like any other placement. A Bridge Only module authored with a footprint bigger than the gaps it is meant to fill produces a run that finds pairs and spans none of them.

UPCGExValencyGrowthRandomFactory.name: Random Growth
UPCGExValencyGrowthRandomFactory.purpose: Takes any open connector, drawn uniformly, so the structure spreads without a shape of its own.
