Denser in places, thin in others, with short offshoots wherever the draw happened to land. It is the strategy for organic sprawl, and the one that ignores connector priority entirely.
UPCGExValencyGrowthRandomFactory.situation: Growth that should look accidental, where neither an even mass nor a long run is what you are after.

mechanism.text: One entry is drawn from the frontier at uniform chance, with no reference to how far it sits from its seed or what priority it was authored with. Under tensor guidance the draw stops being uniform and becomes weighted by how well each connector aligns with the field, which is the one thing that gives this strategy a direction. Everything else about a run comes from the library and the budget.

off_label.claim: Because the draw ignores depth, a partial run is a scatter of half-built arms rather than a smaller structure, which makes this the strategy least suited to iterating on a budget and the most useful for producing variants from one setup by changing only the seed.
off_label.grounded_in: SelectNextConnector draws a uniform index over the whole frontier, with no depth or priority key

SeedPatterns.tooltip: Patterns stamped as pre-built module groups from seed points. Connector or Cage assets.

hints.text: Seed patterns are unavailable here: the row is hidden because this strategy does not declare support for them. Start from an authored arrangement on BFS or DFS instead.

UPCGExValencyLatticeSettings.name: Valency : Lattice
UPCGExValencyLatticeSettings.purpose: Turns shapes you drew into a solve-ready cluster in one node. Building the same thing by hand means producing the points, connecting them along the right axes and running **Valency : Write Orbitals** over the result; this does all three from splines, polygons or volumes plus an **Orbital Set**. It is the shortest path from a floor plan to something a solve can work on.
UPCGExValencyLatticeSettings.situation: A layout drawn as shapes that has to become a cluster snapped to a set of bonding directions.

mechanism.text: The orbital set supplies the lattice axes and Cell Size the scale, and every input is quantized onto that lattice: a Vtx wherever a shape paints, an edge wherever two painted positions sit one orbital step apart. What each input paints depends on which pin it arrived on, and the three pins compose by union. The orbital data is written as the cluster is built, so the result arrives carrying its own substrate and a Valency Map, with no separate Write Orbitals pass.

off_label.claim: Points on the Volumes pin each contribute their own oriented box, so a scattered point cloud becomes a usable occupancy source and this node doubles as a way of snapping loose points onto a bonding lattice.
off_label.grounded_in: the Volumes pin accepts point data and converts each point to its oriented bounding box before unioning it with the other pins

inputs.label: Shapes
inputs.note: Points, splines or polygons, open or closed. Quantized as a linear spine: the outline is painted, the interior is not.

inputs.label: Surfaces
inputs.note: Closed shapes whose interior is filled. An open shape here degrades to its outline. A shape flagged as a hole subtracts instead.

inputs.label: Volumes
inputs.note: 3D occupancy from points, volumes or primitives, unioned with the other two pins.

inputs.label: Match Rules
inputs.note: Partitions the inputs of all three pins into exclusive groups, each painting and emitting its own cluster.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: One point per painted lattice position, carrying the mask of the orbitals its edges occupy.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: One edge per pair of painted positions one orbital step apart, each carrying its orbital.

outputs.label: Valency Map
outputs.note: Names the substrate this node wrote, so a solve downstream finds it without being told where to look.

pins.dynamic: There is no main points input. Every input arrives on one of the node's own three pins, all of which are optional, and at least one has to carry data.

OrbitalSet.tooltip: Orbital set defining the lattice axes. If left null, sourced from the Bonding Rules below.
OrbitalSet.semantics: It decides which directions the lattice runs along and nothing else changes with it: a hex set produces a hex lattice, a three-axis set a volumetric one. Left null the set comes from the Bonding Rules asset instead, which is the usual setup since a solve needs one anyway.

BondingRules.tooltip: Optional convenience: source the Orbital Set from a Bonding Rules asset when the field above is null.

CellSize.tooltip: Base lattice spacing. Each orbital's step length = CellSize * that orbital's Normalized Length.
CellSize.semantics: The base spacing. Each orbital steps by this multiplied by its own normalized length, so a set mixing long and short axes keeps their proportions rather than flattening them to one distance.

CaptureRadius.tooltip: Brush thickness, one value per shape via @Data. Shapes: dilates the outline (0 = one-node spine). Surfaces: grows the fill, negative erodes it (a fully eroded shape stays empty).

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

CaptureRadius.semantics: The brush, read per shape rather than per node. On Shapes it dilates the spine outward and inward, with 0 giving a line one Vtx wide. On Surfaces it grows the fill, and a negative value erodes it.
CaptureRadius.trap: A shape small enough to be fully eroded stays empty and produces nothing. Where part of a Surfaces input silently disappears, that is the first value to check.

MatchingDetails.tooltip: Optional data matching. Partitions the inputs of ALL pins (Shapes/Surfaces/Volumes together) into exclusive groups; each group paints and emits its own cluster, and holes only carve within their group. Unmatched inputs become singleton clusters. Disabled = one merged cluster. Match-by-Index rules see positions in the combined Shapes -> Surfaces -> Volumes input order (duplicate data deduped). (Split/output-unmatched options have no effect on this node.)
MatchingDetails.semantics: Off, everything merges into one cluster on one frame, which is the common case and needs no configuration. On, all three pins are partitioned together into exclusive groups and each group emits its own cluster, with anything unmatched becoming a cluster of its own. A hole then carves only inside its own group, so two buildings can each carry their own courtyards without either cutting the other.

CarryOverDetails.tooltip: Filter in/out which input tags get carried over onto each group's output cluster. Applies only when matching forms the groups; conflicting value tags (same key, different values) resolve to the last contributor in gather order.

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.tooltip: Attributes to carry over.

fields.name: bDataDomainToElements
fields.tooltip: If enabled, data domain attributes are promoted to the elements domain (the single @Data value is broadcast to every point). Off by default; Merge Points is the node that enables it. Not used by all nodes.

fields.name: Scope
fields.tooltip: Scope

fields.name: Tags
fields.tooltip: Tags to carry over.

fields.name: bTestTagsWithValues
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will test full tag with its value ('Tag:Value'), otherwise only test the left part ignoring the right `:Value` ('Tag').

BaseMode.tooltip: Where the frame sits along the directions the lattice doesn't span. No-op for a 3-axis lattice.
BaseMode.semantics: It decides where the frame sits along the directions the lattice does not span, which is what matters when a flat lattice is fed shapes at varying heights. Average is the default, Min and Max pin it to the extremes, and Flat ignores the inputs and uses Origin exactly. A three-axis lattice spans everything, so this does nothing there.

bSharedFrame.tooltip: When matching emits several groups, infer ONE frame base from ALL inputs (co-registered group lattices) instead of a snug per-group base. No-op for Flat base mode, 3-axis lattices, or a single group.
bSharedFrame.semantics: Only reaches groups produced by matching, and only when the base is inferred at all. It infers one frame from every input rather than a snug one per group, which is what makes several group lattices co-register so a Vtx in one lands on the same grid as a Vtx in another.

Origin.tooltip: Offset applied on top of the Base Mode result; the absolute world origin when Base Mode is Flat.

LatticeRotation.tooltip: Global rotation of the whole lattice frame (orbital directions are taken within it).

SplineFidelity.tooltip: How far the polyline may deviate from the source spline -- a tolerance, so lower = finer. Keep it well below Cell Size, or chords cut inside arcs and drop nodes.
SplineFidelity.semantics: A tolerance, so lower means finer.
SplineFidelity.trap: Keep it well below Cell Size. At coarser values the polyline chords cut inside the arcs of a curved spline, and lattice positions that should have been painted are never visited, which reads as a curve that came out with holes in it.

ProjectionDetails.tooltip: Projection used to interpret polygon / 2D inputs.

Suffix.tooltip: Layer suffix for the written attributes (PCGEx/V/Mask|Orbital/{Suffix}). None = the orbital set's Identifier.
Suffix.semantics: Left at None it resolves to the orbital set's own identifier, exactly as Write Orbitals resolves its own, which is what makes the two interchangeable to whatever reads the substrate downstream.

GraphBuilderDetails.semantics: The ordinary PCGEx cluster output configuration. Its minimum-cluster-size filtering is what discards the stray one-Vtx islands a thin shape or a coarse cell size leaves behind.

bQuietInvalidLattice.tooltip: Quiet the warnings for an orbital set that forms no usable lattice, or has dropped orbitals.

bQuietNoShapes.tooltip: Quiet the warnings for missing inputs, or inputs that quantize to too few nodes to bond.

hints.text: The same drawn outline produces unrelated results depending on which pin it arrives on: an outline from Shapes, a fill from Surfaces, an occupancy block from Volumes. The pin is the decision, not the shape.

UPCGExValencyLoadPropertiesSettings.name: Valency : Load Properties
UPCGExValencyLoadPropertiesSettings.purpose: Puts the data authored on a cage back onto points, as ordinary attributes anything downstream can read: a material index chosen per piece, a gameplay value, a flag deciding what spawns alongside the module. It also writes the module's name and its gameplay tags on request. Nothing comes out that was not asked for, so the node does nothing at all until it is configured.
UPCGExValencyLoadPropertiesSettings.situation: Authored per-module data that has to reach the rest of a PCG graph.

mechanism.text: Each point's entry is resolved through the Valency Map to a module, and every property named in the mapping is written to the attribute the mapping names. A value is looked for in the module first and falls back to the defaults the library declares. On points a grammar produced there is one tier above both, because growth records which grammar node placed each point and that node may carry overrides. The points are written in place and nothing else changes, so this can sit anywhere after resolution.

off_label.claim: A property the grammar declares that no module carries still comes out: name it in the mapping and its attribute is created, with the points the grammar never overrode keeping the schema default. That makes the node a way of stamping per-placement data that exists nowhere in the library.
off_label.grounded_in: resolution creates the attribute from the mapping and falls through the placing node override, the module, then the two defaults tiers

inputs.label: In
inputs.note: The resolved points. Any point set carrying a Valency entry will do.

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: What the entry hashes mean, and where the grammar travels. Take it from the node that produced the points.

outputs.label: Out
outputs.note: The same points, carrying one attribute per mapped property plus whichever of the name and tag outputs are on.

EntrySuffix.tooltip: Suffix for the ValencyEntry attribute to read (e.g. "Main" -> "PCGEx/V/Entry/Main")
EntrySuffix.semantics: It names the entry attribute to read, and on grammar-produced data it also names the parallel attribute recording which grammar node placed each point. Both have to match what the producing node wrote.

bOutputModuleName.tooltip: If enabled, write the module name as a point attribute

ModuleNameAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the module name output

PropertiesOutput.semantics: One configuration per property you want written, each naming the property and the attribute it lands on. Nothing comes out that is not listed. Included schema assets pull in a shared set declared once, and importing the configurations off a Bonding Rules asset is the fastest way to a mapping that matches the library actually in use.
PropertiesOutput.trap: A property name resolving to a different concrete type on a different tier is an authoring conflict, and the mismatched source is skipped rather than converted, so those points keep the attribute default. The symptom is an override that appears ignored. Check that the grammar schema, the cages and the rules defaults all declare the property as one type.

DefaultsPrecedence.tooltip: Which defaults tier wins when neither the placing grammar node nor the module authored a value. Only relevant for grammar-produced points; non-grammar points always resolve rules defaults.
DefaultsPrecedence.semantics: Consulted only for grammar-produced points, and only where neither the placing node nor the module authored a value. On anything a grammar did not produce, resolution starts at the module and this setting is never read.

bOutputModuleTags.tooltip: Output module gameplay tags as a single comma-separated string attribute.

bShortNames.tooltip: Emit only the leaf segment of each tag (e.g. "Corner") instead of the full dotted path.
bShortNames.semantics: Emits the leaf segment of each tag rather than the full dotted path, which suits a hierarchy that exists for authoring while downstream logic only cares about the leaf.
bShortNames.trap: Two branches sharing a leaf name become indistinguishable once shortened, and the tags land in one comma-separated string, so nothing downstream can tell them apart afterwards.

hints.text: Every output here is off or empty until asked for. A node that appears to be doing nothing has usually not been given a mapping yet, which is the first thing to check.

UPCGExValencyModulePresenceFilterProvide.name: ✱ Filter : Has Module
UPCGExValencyModulePresenceFilterProvide.purpose: The simplest of the four: does this point carry a placed module. Inverted, it selects the positions that do not, which is the gate for a pass that finishes what an earlier one left unsolved. Two settings decide how strict the question is, and both change what counts as carrying a module rather than what is tested.
UPCGExValencyModulePresenceFilterProvide.situation: Telling the part of a result that resolved from the part that did not, in either direction.

mechanism.text: Per point, the entry layer is read and the answer is whether it holds a module. A missing entry layer is a valid state here rather than an error, so an input that has never been through a solve evaluates as every point having no module instead of failing the whole filter chain. That is what lets the same filter sit on a first pass and a second one without being reconfigured.

off_label.claim: With Require Resolvable off the filter needs no Valency Map at all, which makes it the one Valency filter that works on a bare PCGEx node with nothing wired to its map pin.
off_label.grounded_in: WantsValencyMap returns Config.bRequireResolvable, and the pin drops to Advanced and is reported unused when it is false

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Resolves entries to modules. Required in Pin mode while Require Resolvable is on; otherwise it sits under Advanced and is ignored.
inputs.condition: when Map Source is Pin and Require Resolvable is on

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: An ordinary point filter factory, accepted anywhere a filter pin is.

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Where the entry layer and the resolving Valency Map come from.

fields.name: bRequireResolvable
fields.tooltip: Entries must also resolve against the Valency Map -- foreign/undecodable entries then count as "no module".

fields.name: bConsumedCounts
fields.tooltip: Whether pattern-consumed points (absorbed by a pattern, placing nothing) count as having a module.

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Invert the result: pass points WITHOUT a module (the filler-pass gate).

UPCGExValencyOrbitalFilterProviderSettin.name: ✱ Filter : Orbitals
UPCGExValencyOrbitalFilterProviderSettin.purpose: One generic question about a point's orbital configuration, rather than a menu of canned ones: a fact, a set of orbitals to ask it over, and a comparison between the two. It is the facts vocabulary exposed as a filter, so anything a connector gate or a grammar constraint can ask about orbitals, this can ask of a point.
UPCGExValencyOrbitalFilterProviderSettin.situation: Selecting positions by how they sit in the structure: the ones facing outward, the ones with a neighbour on a named side, the ones whose module declared a boundary that is occupied anyway.

mechanism.text: Operand A is a fact, read per point as a set of orbital bits. Operand B is the set of orbitals the question is about, which is either fixed for the whole run or read per point. The comparison between them is either bitwise or a count of shared bits against a threshold, and the result is the verdict. Nothing else about the point is consulted.

off_label.claim: With Selection set to Fact the filter compares two facts rather than a fact against a list, which is how a disagreement becomes a single test: Module Boundary against Occupancy finds the positions whose module declared a side should face nothing and got a neighbour there anyway.
off_label.grounded_in: the Fact selection mode reads a second orbital fact as operand B, and the two tiers can be mixed in one test

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Resolves entries to modules, and carries the orbital layer, count and set path even when no module fact is read. Required in Pin mode while a module fact is in play.
inputs.condition: when Map Source is Pin and either operand reads a module fact

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: An ordinary point filter factory, accepted anywhere a filter pin is.

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Where the orbital substrate, the entry layer and the resolving Valency Map come from.

fields.name: Fact
fields.tooltip: Operand A -- the orbital fact tested at each point.

fields.name: Selection
fields.tooltip: Operand B -- which orbitals take part in the test.

fields.name: OrbitalNames
fields.tooltip: Orbital names, resolved against the orbital set. A name that matches nothing selects nothing and warns. Set an Orbital Set Override to pick these from a list -- in Host Context mode the runtime set is only known at execution, so nothing can populate the picker at authoring time.

fields.name: OrbitalIndices
fields.tooltip: Raw orbital indices. Out-of-range entries select nothing and warn.

fields.name: SelectionAttribute
fields.tooltip: Per-point int64 attribute carrying an orbital bitmask.

fields.name: SelectionFact
fields.tooltip: The second fact, when operand B is itself a fact.

fields.name: Check
fields.tooltip: How operand A is compared against operand B -- the shared Valency fact-check machinery.

fields.name: NoModuleFallback
fields.tooltip: Result for points carrying no module. Only consulted when a module fact is in play; honored as-is -- Invert does not flip fallbacks.

fields.name: UnresolvedFallback
fields.tooltip: Result for entries whose rule set is not in the resolved map (merged maps, mismatched wiring).

fields.name: ConsumedFallback
fields.tooltip: Result for pattern-consumed points (absorbed by a pattern -- they place nothing).

hints.text: Some combinations need to know how many orbitals exist: anything reading Vacant, an All selection, and any relative-threshold count. An unbounded range would silently widen a complement and inflate a bit count, so the filter refuses to run rather than answer wrongly when it cannot resolve the orbital count. Supplying the map, or an Orbital Set Override, is what resolves it.

UPCGExValencyOrbitalSet.name: Orbital Set
UPCGExValencyOrbitalSet.purpose: The direction topology: every direction modules may bond along, and the angular tolerance for matching one. Swapping the set is what turns a grid layout into a hex one with nothing else changing, because every consumer reads its directions from here rather than assuming any.
UPCGExValencyOrbitalSet.situation: Deciding which directions a structure can connect along.

mechanism.text: Up to 63 directions, each named, with bit 63 reserved. Cages author spatially and their orbital identity is read back from the set, so the set tolerates late edits: a recompile re-derives the masks rather than invalidating the authoring. The angle threshold is what every consumer uses to decide whether a real direction counts as one of these.

Identifier.tooltip: Names the attributes this layer writes (PCGEx/V/Mask|Orbital/{Identifier}).
Identifier.semantics: It names the attributes this set writes, so it is how a consumer locates a substrate without being told where it is. Write Orbitals and Lattice both default their own suffix to this value, which is what makes those two interchangeable downstream.

AngleThreshold.tooltip: Angle threshold in degrees for direction matching
AngleThreshold.semantics: Shared by everything reading the set, so widening it to make one node match more also widens what every other node matches.
AngleThreshold.trap: Both failure modes surface at Write Orbitals first: too tight leaves edges unmatched, too loose on a dense set matches edges to the wrong orbital. Its warning is the fastest diagnostic for a set that has not been tuned to the clusters it runs on.

bTransformDirection.tooltip: Whether to transform directions using the vertex point transform
bTransformDirection.semantics: On by default, which means directions follow each point rotation rather than staying in world space. On unrotated points that changes nothing; on points carrying varied rotations it changes every answer, and it is the first thing to check when a probe or a write pass matches nothing.

bAuthorDirectionsAsRotator.tooltip: Authoring view only -- directions are always stored as vectors, and flipping this never marks dependents stale.

fields.name: Direction
fields.tooltip: Direction of this orbital

fields.name: NormalizedLength
fields.tooltip: Step multiplier on the consumer's cell size, so 1.0 is one full cell. Above 1.0 it also EXTENDS this orbital's probe reach by the same factor; below 1.0 it shortens the step but never the reach.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.tooltip: Display name for UI

fields.name: DebugColor
fields.tooltip: Debug visualization color

fields.name: Reciprocal
fields.tooltip: Orbital facing this one across an aligned edge (West -> East). None = unpaired. Directed -- setting it does NOT populate the reverse.

SymmetryToleranceDegrees.tooltip: Angular tolerance for symmetry detection only, absorbing float error. Keep it far tighter than Angle Threshold -- a loose value invents bogus symmetries.
SymmetryToleranceDegrees.semantics: For symmetry detection only, absorbing float error, and unrelated to the matching threshold above.
SymmetryToleranceDegrees.trap: Keep it far tighter than Angle Threshold. A loose value invents symmetries that do not exist, and the variants derived from them place modules in orientations nobody authored.

DisplayCellSize.tooltip: Purely visual: fallback spacing for the editor's orbital-cell display when no containing volume overrides it. Never read by the Lattice node or any other runtime consumer -- set the real spacing on the consuming node.
DisplayCellSize.semantics: Purely visual, a fallback spacing for the editor orbital-cell display when no containing volume overrides it. No runtime consumer reads it, and Valency : Lattice takes its spacing from its own Cell Size.

Corners.tooltip: Cell corners for corner-state seam derivation. Authored data with a populate helper (Populate Corners, planar sets) -- empty = the corner-tags feature is off for this set.

fields.name: CornerName
fields.tooltip: Corner name; the populate helper composes it from the flanking orbitals ("North_East"), which keeps it stable across re-populates while orbital names hold. Cage rows key on it.

fields.name: Direction
fields.tooltip: Direction from the cell center to this corner (normalized). Drives display, gestures, and corner-permutation detection.

fields.name: UnitDistance
fields.tooltip: Distance from the cell center in UNIT-CELL space (1 = one lattice step; 0.707 for a square's corner). Lets display land markers exactly on the drawn cell polygon vertex. 0 = unauthored (hand-built or legacy tables) -- consumers fall back to the annotation reach.

Corners.semantics: Empty turns the corner-tags feature off for this set entirely. Populated, it supplies the cell corners that corner-state seams are derived from, and the per-orbital incidence list beside it has to stay parallel to the orbital list.

OrbitalCorners.tooltip: Per-orbital winding-ordered corner references, PARALLEL to Orbitals. An orbital with an empty list (out-of-plane, seed edge) derives no seam profile.

DisplayUpAxis.tooltip: Purely visual: the layout plane's up direction, in orbital-set space. Orbitals perpendicular to it get flanking cell edges in the orbital-cell display; orbitals along it get a bead only. Sidescroller sets can point this at the screen axis.
DisplayUpAxis.semantics: Also purely visual. It decides which orbitals get flanking cell edges in the editor display and which get only a bead, which matters for reading a sidescroller-style set at a glance.

UPCGExValencyPatternAsset.name: Pattern Asset
UPCGExValencyPatternAsset.purpose: Authored multi-module arrangements that can be recognised in a finished result. One asset class covers both connection models, and either half may be left out, so a pattern can describe an orbital arrangement, a connector one, or a mix of the two.
UPCGExValencyPatternAsset.situation: An arrangement worth recognising after the fact: a hero piece to substitute in, or a shape later stages need to find.

mechanism.text: Patterns are authored as named entries and compiled against the sets that resolve their slot names. An asset with no orbital set authors no orbital slots, and the same holds on the connector side, so what the asset can express follows from which sets it was given rather than from a mode.

fields.name: PatternName
fields.tooltip: Pattern name for identification and filtering

fields.name: Entries
fields.tooltip: Pattern entries (index 0 = root). Each entry represents a position in the pattern.

fields.name: Weight
fields.tooltip: Weight for probabilistic selection among competing patterns

fields.name: bExclusive
fields.tooltip: If true, matched points are claimed exclusively

fields.name: MatchLimits
fields.tooltip: Min/max match constraints; a relative max is a ratio of found candidate matches (per partition).

fields.name: bMatchRotatedVariants
fields.tooltip: Also match rotated instances, one clone per detected orbital-set symmetry. Min/Max Matches budget the whole rotated family, and Weight splits across it.

fields.name: Placement
fields.tooltip: What a match does to the modules it matched. A pattern with no cages authors no modules, so every value behaves as None there -- placement rides on the cages a pattern was baked from.

OrbitalSet.tooltip: Orbital set resolving orbital slot names to indices. Null = this asset authors no orbital slots.
OrbitalSet.semantics: Null means this asset authors no orbital slots at all, rather than defaulting to something. That is the switch between an orbital pattern and a connector one, and setting both is what makes a pattern that matches across the two.

ConnectorSet.tooltip: Connector set resolving connector slot names to type indices. Null = no connector slots.

LevelContributors.tooltip: Levels hosting the pattern cages that feed this asset. Auto-registered by volumes targeting it.

fields.name: Level
fields.tooltip: Soft reference to the level -- most levels aren't loaded when the consumer asset is.

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: Temporarily exclude this contributor, keeping its shadow and flags for later re-enable.

LevelContributors.semantics: Auto-registered by a Context Volume targeting this asset, the same route the bonding rules use. A pattern cage in a level no volume targets contributes nothing.

CollectionContributors.tooltip: Collections walked to their level-sourced entries at compile time.

fields.name: Collection
fields.tooltip: Soft reference to the collection.

fields.name: bEnabled
fields.tooltip: User toggle -- temporarily exclude without removing.

fields.name: WeightSource
fields.tooltip: How an entry's Weight folds into the weight its level authored. Weight 0 skips the entry in every mode -- a Valency convention, not a toolkit one (pickers store Weight+1 and never exclude).

CollectionContributors.semantics: Walked to their level-sourced entries at compile, so a collection here contributes the pattern cages inside the levels it points at rather than the collection entries themselves.

bAutoRebuildOnStale.tooltip: Auto-refresh from PostLoad / asset-registry hooks when upstream dependencies change.

UPCGExValencyPatternMatcher.name: Pattern Matcher
UPCGExValencyPatternMatcher.purpose: The matcher **Valency : Find Patterns** runs, picked in its details panel. It names the **Pattern Asset** to search for and decides which candidate wins where two matches want the same positions. It searches over orbital and connector bonds alike, so one matcher works on a solved cluster, a grown one, or a result that mixes both.
UPCGExValencyPatternMatcher.situation: Any pattern search. This is the matcher unless a project ships another.

mechanism.text: Each Vtx is tried as a possible root, and the pattern is walked outward from there across the cluster's bonds, backtracking whenever the arrangement stops fitting. Every complete walk is one candidate match. Candidates competing for the same positions are then ordered, and the winner takes them while the losers are discarded, unless the consuming node has been told not to reserve anything.

OverlapResolution.tooltip: How to resolve overlapping pattern matches
OverlapResolution.semantics: It only ever decides between candidates that want the same positions, so on a result where nothing overlaps every value produces the same output. Weight Based reads the pattern weights, which is the value that respects authoring. Largest First maximises how much of the result gets replaced, Smallest First leaves room for more matches to survive, and First Defined makes the order in the library the answer.
OverlapResolution.trap: Connect biases to the consuming node and this stops being the primary key: the bias score orders overlap resolution instead, and this setting is left breaking ties.

PatternAssetPath.tooltip: Pattern asset to match against. Constant, or per-input @Data so each cluster can resolve its own asset.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

PatternAssetPath.semantics: Read as a constant or per input dataset, so one graph can search each cluster for its own asset rather than the same one everywhere. That is what makes a single Find Patterns node serve several structures that share nothing but their rules.

UPCGExValencyPatternReplacementSettings.name: Valency : Find Patterns
UPCGExValencyPatternReplacementSettings.purpose: Looks through a finished result for arrangements you authored, and acts on every occurrence it finds. It is the only node that consumes a **Pattern Asset**, and the whole reason for authoring one. Because it reads a result rather than driving placement, it works on anything that produced modules: a solve, a growth, a grammar, or a mixture of them.
UPCGExValencyPatternReplacementSettings.situation: An arrangement that should become one hero piece, or a recurring shape that later stages need to be able to find.

mechanism.text: A matcher sub-node searches the cluster for occurrences of each pattern, over orbital and connector bonds alike. What a match does to its points is decided by the pattern rather than by this node: consumed points place nothing, substituted ones carry the root's whole-arrangement module, swapped ones carry the module authored on their own pattern cage, and annotated ones are only tagged. The cluster is never thinned; every point comes back, carrying its pattern name and match index, and the optional Matched pin is purely additive.

off_label.claim: With Claim off and every pattern annotating rather than replacing, the node becomes a pure query: nothing changes about what spawns, and every occurrence of every authored arrangement comes back on the Matched pin with its name and index attached.
off_label.grounded_in: Claim off emits every valid match without reserving positions, and the annotated outcome leaves the points otherwise unchanged

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of the cluster to search. Every Vtx is read back as a resolved module.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Bonds are what a pattern is matched against.

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Resolves entries to modules, and is where the rules the patterns were authored against are found.

inputs.label: Vtx Filters
inputs.note: Gates which Vtx may take part in a match, with the meaning of the gate set by Vtx Filter Mode.

inputs.label: Biases
inputs.note: Valency : Bias and Valency : Bias (Channel) nodes. Connected, the bias score becomes the primary key deciding which candidate matches survive.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: Every input Vtx, carrying its pattern name and match index where it took part in one, and its new module where a pattern re-moduled it.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: Forwarded unchanged. Matching never touches connectivity.

outputs.label: Matched
outputs.note: The matched points, in the shape Matched Output names. Additive: the main output is never thinned to compensate.
outputs.condition: when Matched Output is not Off

outputs.label: Valency Map
outputs.note: Forwarded, carrying the modules the matches assigned.

Matcher.tooltip: Pattern matcher to use for matching patterns. Required -- the node errors out without one.
Matcher.semantics: A class picker, not a wire, and it is required: the node errors out without one. The matcher owns which pattern asset is searched for and how competing matches are ordered, so the settings that decide what counts as a match live under it rather than here.

TagPredicate.tooltip: Tag predicate over the pattern root cage's tags. Empty = no filtering.

fields.name: RequireAll
fields.tooltip: Module must carry ALL of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: RequireAny
fields.tooltip: Module must carry AT LEAST ONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: Exclude
fields.tooltip: Module must carry NONE of these tags (empty = unconstrained).

fields.name: bInvert
fields.tooltip: Flips the final match result, so an empty predicate becomes veto-all instead of no-constraint.

TagPredicate.semantics: Tested against the tags on each pattern's root cage rather than against the modules being matched, so it narrows which patterns are looked for and never which positions take part.

PatternNames.tooltip: Match only these patterns by name. Empty = all patterns, subject to the tag filters.

bClaim.tooltip: Reserve matched nodes from later matchers in the chain. Off emits every valid match without reserving, and per-pattern Exclusive stops filtering.
bClaim.semantics: On, a matched position is reserved and later matchers in a chain cannot use it, which is what makes chained Find Patterns nodes ordered rather than simultaneous: the first has first refusal. Off, every valid match is emitted with nothing reserved, and a pattern's own exclusivity stops filtering, which is the setting for using matching to find things rather than to replace them.

VtxFilterMode.tooltip: How the Vtx Filters pin gates matching. No filters connected = no gating.
VtxFilterMode.semantics: Exclude As Root is the subtler value and often the wanted one: it says a position may be part of an arrangement without being allowed to start one, which is a different rule from putting the position off limits entirely.

PartitionMode.tooltip: How a multi-node match maps to a partition when partitioned limits are enabled.
PartitionMode.semantics: A pattern covers several positions, so a multi-node match has to belong to exactly one partition before a partitioned cap can count it. Root Key assigns it to its root's partition and lets it span a boundary; Require Uniform rejects any match whose active positions do not all share one.

MatchedOutput.tooltip: Whether -- and in what shape -- to emit the secondary "Matched" pin. Purely additive. Re-moduled points are emitted carrying the module they now hold.
MatchedOutput.semantics: Matched Points gives one point per active matched Vtx, deduped where matches overlap. Match Roots gives one point per match at the pattern root, bounded to that match's active points, which is the shape to reach for when something should act once per occurrence rather than once per position.

bInvertConnectorTransformPolicyOnMatched.display: Invert Connector Transform Policy On Matched
bInvertConnectorTransformPolicyOnMatched.tooltip: Describes the INPUT -- set it to match the upstream Bonding node's own transform policy. Points are un-posed to cage space either way; this only selects what gets composed off.
bInvertConnectorTransformPolicyOnMatched.semantics: This one describes the input rather than the output: set it to whatever the upstream solve or growth used for its own transform policy. Points are un-posed back to cage space either way, and this only selects what gets composed off to get there.
bInvertConnectorTransformPolicyOnMatched.trap: Left disagreeing with the upstream node, matches are searched for against poses that were never applied, so patterns that clearly exist in the result are not found.

bApplyConnectorTransformPolicy.tooltip: Re-pose vtx that a pattern re-moduled (Swap / Substitute) into their new asset pose. Main output only -- never the Matched pin. Off leaves them in cage space.
bApplyConnectorTransformPolicy.semantics: Re-poses the Vtx a pattern re-moduled into their new asset pose, and only on the main output: the Matched pin is never re-posed. Off leaves them in cage space, which is what you want when a downstream node will do the posing.

PatternNameAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the pattern name annotation

PatternMatchIndexAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the pattern match index (which occurrence of the pattern this point belongs to)

BondingRulesOverride.tooltip: Bonding rules the matcher's patterns were authored against. Null = resolved from the Valency Map by matching the pattern set's recorded paths.
BondingRulesOverride.semantics: Left null the rules are resolved from the Valency Map by matching the pattern set's recorded paths, which is the ordinary case. Naming an asset here is for the case where the map carries several rule sets and the patterns belong to one the matching cannot pick out.

bQuietNoPatterns.tooltip: Suppress warnings about no patterns in bonding rules

bQuietNoMatcher.tooltip: Suppress warnings about no matcher connected

hints.text: A consumed position stays in the cluster and keeps its entry. It is Valency : Staging that declines to spawn it, so a graph that skips staging places both the arrangement and its replacement.

UPCGExValencyPlanarPartitionSettings.name: Valency : Planar Partition
UPCGExValencyPlanarPartitionSettings.purpose: Finds structure in a cluster that is otherwise one undifferentiated set of positions: which floor each Vtx sits on, and which connected region of that floor it belongs to. Nothing is placed and nothing moves. What it writes is meant to be read while modules are being chosen, so it belongs on the cluster going into a solve or a growth rather than on the result coming out.
UPCGExValencyPlanarPartitionSettings.situation: A structure whose parts should be treated differently by floor or by space: a ground floor drawing from other modules, a stairwell capped per level, a bias that prefers the outermost region.

mechanism.text: A reference plane is chosen, and the orbitals lying in it are the ones floors are measured across; the rest step between levels. Every Vtx gets the floor it sits on, numbered from 0 at the extreme opposite the plane normal with empty levels skipped, and within its floor the ordinal of the connected region it belongs to. A region is a set of Vtx on one floor reachable from each other through in-plane orbitals alone, so two wings joined only by a link on the floor above are two regions.

off_label.claim: Regions Above reading 0 on a Vtx that is not on the top floor names a region nothing above it connects to, which is how a dead-end wing or an isolated roof section is found without inspecting the geometry.
off_label.grounded_in: the two vertical-adjacency counts are mirrored onto every Vtx and count distinct linked regions on the floor above and below

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of the cluster to partition. Each one gets a floor and a region.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Their orbitals are what separate in-plane connections from the ones that step between levels.

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Supplies the orbital substrate and the set the plane is inferred from.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The same Vtx, each carrying its floor, its region, the packed region key and the two adjacency counts.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: Forwarded unchanged.

outputs.label: Regions
outputs.note: One point per region, at its centroid, oriented to the region's own spread and bounding its members.

PlaneSource.tooltip: Where the reference plane's normal comes from.
PlaneSource.semantics: The node derives an up direction rather than assuming world up. Auto takes the plane containing the most orbitals. From Orbital and Custom respect the sign exactly as authored, which is a lever rather than a nuisance: naming a downward orbital puts floor 0 at the top and numbers downward.

UpHint.tooltip: Breaks Auto's ties and decides which side is up -- a cube-symmetric set has three equally valid planes.
UpHint.semantics: Auto can be genuinely undecided, because a cube-symmetric orbital set has three equally good planes. This picks the one best aligned with the hint, and it is consulted only when there is a tie to break.

UpOrbitalName.tooltip: Orbital whose direction is the plane normal. Its sign is respected, so naming a downward orbital puts floor 0 at the top.

CustomNormal.tooltip: Explicit plane normal. Its sign is respected, exactly as for From Orbital.

PlanarityToleranceDegrees.tooltip: How far off perpendicular an orbital may sit and still count as lying in the plane. Loose values merge genuinely stepping orbitals into the plane, which silently fuses two real floors.
PlanarityToleranceDegrees.semantics: How far off perpendicular to the normal an orbital may sit and still count as lying in the plane.
PlanarityToleranceDegrees.trap: Loose values are the failure to watch for. An orbital that genuinely steps between levels but is admitted as in-plane merges two real floors into one, and the result reads as though floor detection is broken rather than as though the tolerance is wrong.

FloorReconcile.tooltip: How floors are numbered across parts of the cluster that share no vertical connection.
FloorReconcile.semantics: It only matters where parts of the cluster share no vertical connection. Measured gives them one shared numbering off a layer height taken from the cluster itself, which is what makes two towers agree about floor three. Independent numbers each part from its own extreme, so separate structures get overlapping numbers.

LayerQuantizationTolerance.tooltip: How far an orbital's layer step may stray from a whole multiple of the smallest one before it is dropped from floor propagation.
LayerQuantizationTolerance.semantics: It supports the measured numbering: an orbital whose vertical step strays too far from a whole multiple of the smallest one is dropped from floor propagation rather than distorting the measurement. A set mixing genuinely irregular vertical steps loses them all and falls back on what remains.

FloorIndexAttributeName.tooltip: Floor the vtx sits on, 0 at the extreme opposite the plane normal. Skips values where a level is empty.

RegionIndexAttributeName.tooltip: Region ordinal within the vtx's own floor.

RegionHashAttributeName.tooltip: Packed floor+region key, never 0. Feed this to Partitioned Limits on Bonding or Find Patterns.
RegionHashAttributeName.semantics: The one to reach for when a limit or a match needs to be per region: a single value unique across the whole cluster, never 0, so it can be fed straight to the partitioned limits on a solve or a growth, or to Find Patterns.

bOutputAdjacencyOnVtx.tooltip: Mirror the two vertical-adjacency counts onto every vtx, so they can be filtered on directly instead of joining back through the Regions output.

RegionsAboveAttributeName.tooltip: Number of distinct regions on the floor above linked to this vtx's region.

RegionsBelowAttributeName.tooltip: Number of distinct regions on the floor below linked to this vtx's region.

bOutputRegions.tooltip: Emit one point per region on a secondary pin, oriented to the region's own spread and bounding the geometry of its members.

MinRegionExtent.tooltip: Smallest half-extent a region point may report, per axis. A region of one vtx spreads along no axis and one of two spreads along a single line, so without a floor their boxes are degenerate.
MinRegionExtent.semantics: A floor on the half-extent each region point reports, per axis. A region of one Vtx spreads along no axis and one of two spreads along a single line, so without it those boxes come out degenerate and anything scaling by them divides by zero.

bQuietPlaneInference.tooltip: Quiet the plane-inference advisories (ambiguous up hint, unquantized orbitals, 2D set, mixed vtx rotations).

bQuietLevelConflicts.tooltip: Quiet the warnings for links whose floors disagree, or that span more than one floor.

bQuietDisconnectedFloors.tooltip: Quiet the warnings for clusters whose parts share no vertical connection.

hints.text: A floor number and a region answer different questions about the same Vtx, and the region count can differ from floor to floor on an unchanged structure. Where a floor number alone is not telling one space from another, the region is what does.

UPCGExValencyPrioritySolver.name: Priority Solver
UPCGExValencyPrioritySolver.purpose: Hands the decision order to you, as a per-Vtx attribute. Positions are solved from the highest value down, or the lowest first when inverted, so a spine can be settled before the detail hanging off it and a ground floor before the storeys above. The entropy heuristic is given up in exchange, which is the whole trade: an order that ignores where the constraints actually sit can strand positions the default would have saved.
UPCGExValencyPrioritySolver.situation: The structure has an order you already understand and want the solve to respect.

mechanism.text: The attribute is read once per Vtx and the whole cluster is sorted by it up front, so the order is fixed before the first module is committed and nothing during the solve changes it. Each position in turn draws a module by weight from its surviving candidates, and a module that has fallen far enough behind on its minimum spawns to have no spare positions left is taken instead of the draw. Positions already resolved, and positions whose only candidates are fillers, are skipped and picked up by the filler sweep at the end.

off_label.claim: An attribute holding one constant leaves every position tied, and the solve then runs in whatever order the sort settles on rather than in Vtx index order.
off_label.grounded_in: CreateAllocations sorts SortedNodeIndices on the priority value alone, with no index tiebreak in the comparator

PriorityAttribute.tooltip: The attribute to read priority from. Higher values are solved first.
PriorityAttribute.semantics: Read from the Vtx as a float, and read once, before solving starts. A missing attribute is not an error: the solver falls back to plain Vtx index order and every position reports a priority of zero, so a mistyped name looks like a working solve that quietly ignored your ordering.
PriorityAttribute.trap: Ties carry no second key. Two positions on the same value land in whatever order the sort produced, so an attribute with a handful of distinct values orders the groups and leaves everything inside a group unordered.

MinimumSpawnWeightBoost.tooltip: Weight boost multiplier for modules that need more spawns to meet minimum
MinimumSpawnWeightBoost.semantics: It multiplies a module's draw weight for as long as that module is behind on its minimum, and stops once the quota is met. Separately from the boost, a module whose remaining positions have run down to exactly what its minimum still needs is taken outright rather than drawn, so minimums here are part preference and part hard pick.

bInvertPriority.tooltip: If true, treat lower values as higher priority (invert priority order)

hints.text: Priority decides only the order positions are visited in. It never decides which module lands, so a high-priority position with a wide-open candidate set still draws at random from it.

UPCGExValencyTagPredicateFilterProviderS.name: ✱ Filter : Module Tag
UPCGExValencyTagPredicateFilterProviderS.purpose: Tests the module a point resolved to against a gameplay-tag predicate, so a result can be split by what its pieces are rather than by where they sit. Tags come from the module as it was authored, which makes this the filter that reads a library's own vocabulary: entrances, exteriors, decoration, whatever the cages declare.
UPCGExValencyTagPredicateFilterProviderS.situation: Aiming a second pass at one kind of module, or partitioning a finished result by role before spawning it.

mechanism.text: Each point's entry is resolved to a module, and that module's compiled tags are tested against the predicate. A map can carry several rule sets, and tag identity is per rule set, so the predicate is compiled once against each set's own tag space rather than once globally. Points with no module, points whose entry resolves to nothing, and points a pattern consumed never reach the predicate at all and take their own fallbacks instead.

off_label.claim: An empty predicate passes every resolved module, so the three fallbacks on their own turn this into a live-module test that distinguishes unsolved, foreign and pattern-consumed points from each other, which the Has Module filter collapses into one answer.
off_label.grounded_in: an empty predicate short-circuits to a pass for any resolved module, while the three non-module states are answered by NoModuleFallback, UnresolvedFallback and ConsumedFallback separately

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Resolves entries to modules and supplies the tag space the predicate compiles against. Required in Pin mode.

outputs.label: Filter
outputs.note: An ordinary point filter factory, accepted anywhere a filter pin is.

fields.name: Source
fields.tooltip: Where the entry layer and the resolving Valency Map come from.

fields.name: Predicate
fields.tooltip: Tag predicate tested against the resolved module. Empty = every resolved module passes (fallbacks below still apply).

fields.name: NoModuleFallback
fields.tooltip: Result for points carrying no module (ValencyEntry unset or invalid). Honored as-is -- the predicate's Invert does not flip fallbacks.

fields.name: UnresolvedFallback
fields.tooltip: Result for entries whose rule set is not in the resolved map (merged maps, mismatched wiring).

fields.name: ConsumedFallback
fields.tooltip: Result for pattern-consumed points (absorbed by a pattern -- they place nothing). The predicate never runs on them.

hints.text: A missing entry layer is an error for this filter, unlike Has Module which treats it as every point having no module. Pointed at data that has never been through a solve, it fails rather than answering.

UPCGExValencyWriteConnectorsSettings.name: Valency : Write Connectors
UPCGExValencyWriteConnectorsSettings.purpose: Emits one point per connector on a finished result's resolved modules, each carrying a packed reference back to the connector it came from. A connector point is a position with a facing and a type, which is the shape of input a second pass wants, so this is the chaining node: a solve or a growth followed by something that builds onto its sockets.
UPCGExValencyWriteConnectorsSettings.situation: A finished structure whose open sockets have to become the input of whatever comes next.

mechanism.text: Every Vtx is read back as a resolved module and each of that module's connectors is considered in turn, subject to the claim scope, the eligibility selection and any gates the connector itself carries. What survives becomes one point at the connector's own transform, so the count out has nothing to do with the count in. The cluster passes through untouched: this node adds a stream rather than modifying one.

off_label.claim: Claim Scope set to Any turns this into a census of a library as it landed, one point per socket whatever it is doing, which is the quickest way to see whether a result has the sockets you expected in the places you expected them.
off_label.grounded_in: the Any scope skips the claim test entirely and emits every claim-tracked instance the selection allows

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of the cluster to read. Every Vtx is read back as a resolved module.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half.

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Resolves entries to modules and supplies the connector set.

inputs.label: Vtx Filters
inputs.note: Narrows which Vtx contribute connectors at all, which is how a second pass is confined to part of a structure. Failing Vtx emit nothing.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: Forwarded unchanged.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: Forwarded unchanged.

outputs.label: Connectors
outputs.note: One point per emitted connector, posed at the connector and carrying its packed reference.

outputs.label: Valency Map
outputs.note: Forwarded, so the connector points and the cluster stay resolvable together downstream.

ClaimScope.tooltip: Claim-state emission filter. Authored connector gates (orbital/claim) still evaluate on top.
ClaimScope.semantics: Unclaimed is the chaining scope and the default, because open sockets are where more can be built. Claimed emits one point per consumed connector, so a bonded pair becomes two collocated points each knowing only its own half.
ClaimScope.trap: On growth or grammar output where everything bonded, Unclaimed emits nothing. That is the correct answer for a fully closed structure, so check what the upstream run left open before looking at this node. And where Claimed is what you reached for, Write Junctions is usually the node you actually wanted: it emits one point per connection carrying both sides.

ConnectorSelection.tooltip: Which connector instances are eligible at all (identifier/type/index selection). With a non-All selection, untracked instances (local index >= 64) are never emitted.

fields.name: Selection
fields.tooltip: Which of a module's connector instances take part.

fields.name: Identifiers
fields.tooltip: Connector identifiers, matched against each module's instances.

fields.name: ConnectorTypes
fields.tooltip: Connector type names -- selects every instance of these types on each module.

fields.name: ConnectorIndices
fields.tooltip: Raw module-local instance indices.

ConnectorSelection.semantics: Narrows which instances are eligible before claim state is even consulted, by identifier, type or index.
ConnectorSelection.trap: With anything other than an All selection, connectors past the claim-tracked range on a module are never emitted. A module carrying an unusually large number of sockets can therefore lose its later ones from a narrowed selection while keeping them under All.

AllowMultiSpawnPerConnector.tooltip: Per-point: emit one point per Generator candidate, capped by the connector's Spawn Capacity. Off emits a single point at the base transform and skips Generators.

fields.name: Input
fields.tooltip: Whether to use the constant value or read from an attribute.

fields.name: bCleanupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Allow this attribute to be registered as consumable, i.e. deleted from the consuming node's outputs when its 'Cleanup Consumable Attributes' toggle is enabled. Disable to always preserve the attribute.

fields.name: Attribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute or property selector to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

AllowMultiSpawnPerConnector.semantics: Off, a connector emits exactly one point at its own transform and any Generator constraints authored on it are skipped. On, the Generators run and the connector emits a point per candidate pose they produce, capped by the connector's own spawn capacity. It reads per point, so the two behaviours can coexist in one run.

ConnectorOutputAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the packed connector reference written to output connector points. Carries connector TYPE identity, which is a different layout from the per-edge PCGEx/V/Connector/{Layer} attribute -- hence the distinct default name.
ConnectorOutputAttributeName.semantics: Carries connector type identity, which is a different packing from the per-edge connector attribute growth writes, hence the distinct default name. Renaming it is for keeping two Write Connectors passes apart on one dataset.

bOutputSourceIndex.tooltip: Output an attribute containing the source vertex index
bOutputSourceIndex.semantics: This is the attribute that matters for chaining: it is what lets a downstream pass find its way back to the module that owned the socket rather than treating the points as unrelated positions.

SourceIndexAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for source vertex index

bOutputConnectorIdentifier.tooltip: Output an attribute containing the connector identifier

bOutputConnectorType.tooltip: Output an attribute containing the connector type

UPCGExValencyWriteJunctionsSettings.name: Valency : Write Junctions
UPCGExValencyWriteJunctionsSettings.purpose: Turns each bonded connector pair into a point, sitting where the pair meets and carrying what met there. The joint is where a lot of content lives, doors in doorways, seams where two walls meet, transitions where a corridor becomes a room, and those are all connections rather than modules, so until this node runs there is nothing at them to place anything on. A second mode rebuilds the cluster with the junctions inserted as Vtx.
UPCGExValencyWriteJunctionsSettings.situation: Content that belongs at a connection rather than at a module.

mechanism.text: Every bonded pair on the input becomes one junction point when the two connectors sit in the same place, and two points, one at each end, when they do not. Attributes are written per side, so the pair has to be ordered, and one setting decides which connector counts as the start. Points mode leaves the cluster alone and adds a stream; Split Cluster additionally rebuilds it with the junction points inserted between the modules they join.

off_label.claim: With the span attributes on, filtering the junctions on Spanning isolates every bridge in a result as a point set, which is a direct readout of how much of a structure is held together by spans rather than by mating.
off_label.grounded_in: the spanning flag is written false on mated junctions and the span length is 0 there, so the two classes separate on one attribute

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of the cluster to read. Every Vtx is read back as a resolved module.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Each bonded edge is a candidate junction.

inputs.label: Valency Map
inputs.note: Resolves entries to modules and supplies the connector set.

inputs.label: Vtx Filters
inputs.note: A junction is emitted only when both of its endpoint Vtx pass, so a filter here narrows by connection rather than by position.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: Forwarded untouched in Points mode; rebuilt with junction Vtx inserted in Split Cluster.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: Forwarded untouched in Points mode; in Split Cluster each bonded edge becomes two, or three across a spanning bond.

outputs.label: Junctions
outputs.note: One point per mated bond, two per spanning bond, carrying the whole junction attribute schema.

outputs.label: Valency Map
outputs.note: Forwarded, so the junctions and the cluster stay resolvable together downstream.

OutputMode.tooltip: Points forwards clusters untouched; Split Cluster rebuilds them with junction vtx inserted.
OutputMode.semantics: Points describes the result and changes nothing about it. Split Cluster changes the topology: each bonded edge A to B becomes A to junction to B, and a spanning bond gains two junction Vtx rather than one. Those inserted Vtx carry no Valency entry, so every downstream node that resolves modules has to expect Vtx that resolve to nothing.

PrimarySide.tooltip: Which side of a pair is Start -- junction frame and attribute-suffix assignment.
PrimarySide.semantics: It decides which connector is the start, which the per-side attributes are keyed to and which also orients the junction point, so it decides which way anything spawned there faces. Edge Direction reads the authored endpoint order, and growth authors edges parent to child, so on grown output start is the parent.
PrimarySide.trap: Polarity only has an answer when exactly one side is a plug. Universal against Universal, plug against plug, and port against universal all fall back to the authored endpoint order, so a library built mostly on universal connectors gets edge-direction behaviour while the setting says otherwise.

DirectionSettings.tooltip: Edge direction rules resolving which endpoint is Start.

MatedDistanceTolerance.tooltip: Bonded connectors closer than this (cm) are mated: one junction point at the shared origin. Farther pairs are spanning bonds (bridges) and emit one point per connector end.
MatedDistanceTolerance.semantics: The threshold between one junction point and two, in centimetres. Raising it far enough makes short bridges read as mated, which collapses each of them into a single point at a location neither connector actually occupies.

ConnectorTypeAttributeName.tooltip: Base attribute name for the pair's connector types (suffixed _Start / _End).

ConnectorIdentifierAttributeName.tooltip: Base attribute name for the pair's connector identifiers (suffixed _Start / _End).
ConnectorIdentifierAttributeName.semantics: This is where a connector identifier earns its keep. It takes no part in matching during generation, and on the way out it is the name that says which specific socket a joint came from.

VtxIndexAttributeName.tooltip: Base attribute name for the pair's endpoint vtx indices (suffixed _Start / _End).

TypePairAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the canonical type-pair key.
TypePairAttributeName.semantics: Matching on the start and end attributes means handling both permutations of every pair, because which type landed on which side depends on the direction growth happened to travel. The sorted key removes that: one value per type meeting, whichever way round it occurred.

bWriteSpan.tooltip: Flag spanning-bond points (bridges) and write the bond's connector-to-connector length.
bWriteSpan.semantics: The two attributes it controls are what separate bridges from ordinary bonds after the fact: the flag reads false and the length reads 0 on every mated junction, so one comparison partitions the set.

SpanningAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the spanning flag (bool; false on mated junctions).

SpanLengthAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the span length (0 on mated junctions).

JunctionFlagAttributeName.tooltip: Attribute name for the junction-vtx flag.

hints.text: Where you reached for Write Connectors on the Claimed scope, this is usually the node you wanted. That one emits one point per connector, so a bond becomes two collocated points each knowing only its own half; this one emits one point per connection, carrying both sides.

UPCGExValencyWriteOrbitalsSettings.name: Valency : Write Orbitals
UPCGExValencyWriteOrbitalsSettings.purpose: Gives a cluster the orbital data a solve reads. A solve does not work out for itself which direction each connection runs in: it reads that per edge, and a cluster built by anything other than **Valency : Lattice** carries nothing for it to read. The node places no modules and needs no library, only geometry and an **Orbital Set**.
UPCGExValencyWriteOrbitalsSettings.situation: A cluster you built yourself that has to become something a solve can work on.

mechanism.text: Every edge is assigned one orbital, and every Vtx ends up with the mask of the orbitals its edges occupy. The counts and the connectivity are untouched: the same Vtx and Edges come back with two attributes added and a Valency Map alongside them. An edge that matches no orbital is left unassigned rather than forced onto the nearest one, so the Vtx bit for that direction stays clear.

off_label.claim: Run twice with two suffixes and one cluster carries two independent orbital substrates, which is how a coarse set and a fine set can both be solved against without duplicating the cluster.
off_label.grounded_in: the attributes are written under PCGEx/V/Mask and PCGEx/V/Orbital keyed by Suffix, and consumers locate a substrate by that key

inputs.label: Vtx
inputs.note: The Vtx half of every cluster to annotate.

inputs.label: Edges
inputs.note: The Edges half. Every edge is what gets an orbital assigned to it.

outputs.label: Vtx
outputs.note: The same Vtx, each carrying the mask of the orbitals its edges occupy.

outputs.label: Edges
outputs.note: The same edges, each carrying the orbital it was assigned.

outputs.label: Valency Map
outputs.note: Names the substrate this node wrote, so a solve downstream finds it without being told where to look.

AssignmentMode.tooltip: How orbital indices are assigned to edges
AssignmentMode.semantics: Direction is geometric and works on a cluster from any source: each edge is measured and matched to the closest orbital within the set's tolerance. Connector reads an attribute instead, so it only works on input a growth pass produced, and what it buys is orbital data consistent with the connectors that actually bonded rather than with wherever the edges happen to point. The two can disagree about the same edge.

OrbitalSet.tooltip: Orbital set defining the directional slots. Defaults to the project default, then to the Bonding Rules' set.

ConnectorSet.tooltip: Connector set defining connector types. Null falls back to the Bonding Rules' set.

BondingRules.tooltip: Sources the Orbital / Connector Set when the fields above are null. Only its sets are used.

Suffix.tooltip: Layer suffix for the written attributes (PCGEx/V/Mask|Orbital/{Suffix}). None = the source set's own identifier, which is how consumers locate the substrate.
Suffix.semantics: Left at None it resolves to the source set's own identifier: the orbital set's in Direction mode, the connector set's layer name in Connector mode. That default is what lets a consumer locate the substrate without being told where it is, and Lattice resolves its own suffix the same way, which is what makes the two interchangeable to whatever reads them.
Suffix.trap: Naming one by hand breaks that convention, so every downstream node then has to be pointed at the same name. Two passes under different suffixes coexist happily; one pass under a name nothing else knows reads as a solve that found no substrate.

ConnectorAttributeName.tooltip: Edge attribute holding packed connector instance references, as written by generative growth. Resolving them to connector types needs the Bonding Rules' compiled connector payload. None = the resolved Connector Set's own layer (PCGEx/V/Connector/{LayerName}), which is where growth writes them; set explicitly only to read a non-standard name.

bBuildOrbitalCache.tooltip: Build and cache OrbitalCache for downstream valency nodes. Avoids redundant rebuilding.
bBuildOrbitalCache.semantics: It hands the resolved substrate straight to the next Valency node instead of making it re-derive one from the attributes. Turning it off changes no result, only the work a downstream solve has to repeat.

bWarnOnNoMatch.tooltip: If enabled, will output warnings for edges that don't match any orbital
bWarnOnNoMatch.semantics: An unmatched edge is not an error here and nothing stops, which is exactly why the warning matters: the consequence surfaces much later, as a position that will not solve for no visible reason. This is the fastest diagnostic available for an orbital set whose tolerance has not been tuned to the clusters it is used on.

bQuietMissingBondingRules.tooltip: Quiet mode - suppress missing bonding rules errors

bQuietMissingConnectorAttribute.tooltip: Quiet mode - suppress warnings when connector attribute is missing from edges

hints.text: The angular tolerance belongs to the orbital set, not to this node. Tight tolerance on a cluster whose edges sit slightly off-axis leaves edges unmatched; loose tolerance on a dense set of directions matches edges to the wrong orbital. Both show up here first.
